     1	# The Orchestration Process
     2	
     3	How this project is actually built: a human researcher directing a
     4	multi-model AI system whose workflow is itself a deliberate, versioned,
     5	self-instrumenting piece of engineering. This document is the single
     6	in-repo description of that process. (The executable playbooks live
     7	outside the repository as reusable "skills" so they transfer to future
     8	projects; this page describes what they do and where their evidence
     9	lands in this repo.) Binding role and process changes live in
    10	`docs/decision_log.md`; this page avoids copying volatile model versions.
    11	
    12	## Roles: a lead, independent implementers/reviewers, and a human at the top
    13	
    14	- **Ed (researcher)** sets research direction, methodology
    15	  non-negotiables (raw-evidence bundles, dual-basis capture with gross-energy
    16	  headlines, named
    17	  measurement boundaries, no unauditable claims), hardware/access
    18	  decisions, and — critically — *process policy*: every rule below
    19	  traces to a standing instruction issued after an observed failure or
    20	  opportunity. External-facing claims and merge authority derive from
    21	  him (he granted the lead conditional self-merge authority on
    22	  2026-07-08 once the review gate had proven itself).
    23	- **The designated lead** owns
    24	  decomposition, triage, design adjudication, every final diff gate,
    25	  all live/hardware verification, merge decisions, bookkeeping, and
    26	  process evolution. Other agents save lead capacity without inheriting
    27	  final authority; all escalation paths terminate at the lead.
    28	- **Independent implementation and review agents** do the heavy reading and
    29	  writing: implementation against pinned specs, adversarial review
    30	  lenses, test writing, test *auditing* (never of its own tests — a
    31	  fresh instance audits), docs drafting, and review of the lead's own
    32	  consequential decisions. Cross-model review is load-bearing by
    33	  design: the attributed per-layer catch record (below) shows the two
    34	  roles consistently catching different classes of defect.
    35	- **Specialist agents** handle bounded sweeps (for example, docs
    36	  consistency) and, when a stream genuinely needs
    37	  mid-stream judgment, as a stream director — a role that is now the
    38	  exception rather than the default (see Topology).
    39	- **Image-heavy analysis uses the designated image-capable review route** per
    40	  C-012, after the site-observatory stream's image-critique rounds.
    41	- **Invited-peer validation is allowed to overturn lead designs**; C-014
    42	  recorded two lead designs overturned by an invited peer before
    43	  implementation.
    44	
    45	## The loop, end to end
    46	
    47	Every substantial session runs one conductor procedure:
    48	
    49	1. **Intake** — read `RUN_STATE.md` (the intake pointer), the task
    50	   queue, the latest run report; never re-decide anything the decision
    51	   log settled.
    52	2. **Decompose** — split work into genuinely independent streams
    53	   (disjoint expected diff footprints), one git worktree + branch each;
    54	   assign each stream a review tier by *cost of being wrong*
    55	   (measurement-semantics and contract-bearing work gets the full
    56	   pipeline; docs get a light tier). Preflight gates: hardware-shaped
    57	   streams require a confirmed device inventory; anything pinned
    58	   without live validation carries a PROVISIONAL label; measurement
    59	   sessions require a no-agent "quiet machine" lock.
    60	3. **Per-stream pipeline** — for each reviewable unit: an invited
    61	   design-argument round (the implementer must argue trade-offs before
    62	   coding), implementation, then a layered review stack:
    63	   2–3 fresh-instance counterreview lenses over the diff → lead triage
    64	   with recorded dispositions → fixes → a dedicated test-amplification
    65	   round (an independent writer adds edge-case tests) → a
    66	   writer≠reviewer test audit (a fresh instance hunts tautological,
    67	   vacuous, or wrong-expectation tests) → the lead's diff gate.
    68	4. **Lead live gates** — never delegated: the lead runs the real flow
    69	   (real corpus, real CLI, real hardware where present). This layer has
    70	   repeatedly caught blockers no other layer saw, including defects
    71	   whose own tests were green because the tests encoded the same wrong
    72	   assumption as the code.
    73	5. **Merge gate** — multi-commit series land as branch + PR. Before any
    74	   merge: a pre-merge oversight pass by 2–3 fresh reviewers with
    75	   distinct angles (deep regression hunt; claim-to-evidence trace;
    76	   merge-order simulation across sibling PRs), lead triage, fixes, CI
    77	   green. **Final-head rule:** any commit that lands after the last
    78	   review round gets one more fresh review before merge — no commit
    79	   merges unreviewed, however small (its first application caught a
    80	   crash path in a "trivial" post-review fix).
    81	6. **Integration review** — after parallel streams merge, one dedicated
    82	   review hunts *interaction* defects no single-stream review can see.
    83	   Its catches are definitionally unique (first outing: two).
    84	7. **Bookkeeping** — a single session record (run report) with a
    85	   verbatim process-trace appendix; the intake pointer and queue
    86	   refreshed; a delegated docs-consistency sweep before the final
    87	   commit (its latest pass found 15 real drift items; earlier passes
    88	   found 5–6). Large documentation batches add the pre-commit
    89	   docs-verify mode; the `consistency-sweep` skill owns that shape,
    90	   including the D-043 supersession check.
    91	8. **Same-session distillation** — lessons fold into the process
    92	   playbooks the same session they are learned. Measured effect: one
    93	   failure mode recurred five times before its fix was distilled, zero
    94	   times after. The current operation-loop also runs its §0
    95	   primary-deliverable check and §8 shipped-check before the session is
    96	   considered done.
    97	9. **Post-landing verification and close-out** — landed work gets the
    98	   matching verification workflow with severity-tiered refuters. Sessions
    99	   that change front-facing state refresh `docs/site/DRIFT.md`; no agent
   100	   regenerates or deploys the site. Automation informs and Ed deploys
   101	   manually, per D-068 and `RUN_STATE.md` end-of-work step 8.
   102	10. **Meta-review (the final step)** — event-driven, not calendar-driven:
   103	    when a review layer stops earning its keep, when an intervention
   104	    repeats despite a folded fix, or when the user asks, the loop is
   105	    reviewed with its own evidence discipline (see Topology for the
   106	    consensus one such review produced). After large workloads the
   107	    post-large-workload meta-reassessment (owned by operation-loop §10)
   108	    always fires, and it runs LAST.
   109	
   110	### Stop cards and paused work
   111	
   112	When a session stops with live work in progress, the lead creates or
   113	updates an `ACTIVE_STOP_CARD` at the top of `RUN_STATE.md`. While active,
   114	that card is the single restart authority and overrides every lower
   115	"what next" list, queue rank, mission guide, and run-report default.
   116	
   117	A stop card must name:
   118	
   119	- the resume authority and exact artifact pointer,
   120	- the reason for stopping,
   121	- worktrees, branches, PRs, and off-repo artifacts that must not be
   122	  cleaned accidentally,
   123	- status terms for each paused item,
   124	- the first resume action, and
   125	- the clearance criteria.
   126	
   127	Use these status terms for paused work:
   128	
   129	| Term | Meaning |
   130	|---|---|
   131	| `APPLIED_UNVERIFIED` | A worker reports code or docs are applied, but the lead has not gated the diff. Not merge-safe. |
   132	| `LEAD_GATED` | The lead has reviewed and run the required local/live checks for the item. |
   133	| `PR_OPEN_CI_GREEN` | A PR exists and CI is green, but merge authority has not yet fired. |
   134	| `MERGED` | The accepted work has landed on main. |
   135	| `UNREAD_UNADJUDICATED` | A report/synthesis exists but has not been consumed into decisions, queue rows, or rejected findings. |
   136	| `ADJUDICATED` | Findings have explicit accept/reject/defer disposition and downstream artifacts are updated. |
   137	
   138	Before an intentional pause, do the minimal stop sync even if full
   139	bookkeeping cannot fit: update only `RUN_STATE.md`'s stop card and the
   140	rank-0 queue row. That is enough to prevent accidental bypass.
   141	
   142	## The artifact system (where rigor becomes auditable)
   143	
   144	Each fact has exactly one home; everything else points at it:
   145	
   146	| Artifact | Role |
   147	|---|---|
   148	| `docs/decision_log.md` | Binding design decisions, each with alternatives considered, consequences, and revisit conditions. The log is the count authority; nothing re-decides these silently. |
   149	| `docs/council_log.md` | The deliberation record: review-council positions, reasoning exchanged, who prevailed, overridden dissents — so a future reader can reconstruct *why*, not just *what*. The log is the range/count authority. |
   150	| `docs/contracts/` | Claim/evidence contracts: `claims_ladder.md` (D-037) plus `analysis_plans.md` (D-038) form the claim gate; strict validation is the evidence ticket. |
   151	| `docs/stream_logs/` | Per-stream decision ledgers, committed WITH the code they justify: every non-trivial in-stream decision (`A-1..A-30`, `B-1..B-46`, …) with mandatory evidence pointers; wrong pins are SUPERSEDED in place, never erased. |
   152	| `docs/run_reports/` | One record per working session: outcomes, verification evidence, a per-layer catch/yield table, the delegation-calibration ledger, restart instructions. |
   153	| `docs/process/state_kernel.json` | Source of truth for work selection: active gates, dependencies, and machine-state lanes ([QUIET-MAC] / [AGENT] / [ED-EXTERNAL]). |
   154	| `TASK_QUEUE.md` | Generated detailed queue projection plus dated history; do not hand-copy its live rows into reader docs. |
   155	| `RUN_STATE.md` | Intake pointer with the generated restart projection. History lives in run reports. |
   156	| `docs/risk_register.md` | Live risks with triggers and mitigation states. |
   157	
   158	Instrumentation ledgers close the loop on the process itself:
   159	
   160	- **Per-layer yield:** every review layer's unique catches are
   161	  attributed and tallied per session under D-061 (C-027; replaces the
   162	  earlier two-zero-sessions auto-drop, which the integration-review
   163	  zero/zero/five sequence falsified): applicability is decided by
   164	  PRE-DECLARED mechanical predicates; outcomes are classified
   165	  accepted-unique-defect / duplicate / clean-verification /
   166	  false-positive-suppression (suppression is not a catch); severity
   167	  weights are fixed before the session; three applicable exposures
   168	  TRIGGER an expected-loss review decision, never automatic deletion;
   169	  safety/final-head/integration layers are never auto-dropped on
   170	  zero-defect streaks. (One layer, the default specialist review lens, was
   171	  dropped under the old rule before D-061.)
   172	- **Delegation calibration:** every delegated unit gets a row — task
   173	  altitude (pinned-spec / design-freedom / judgment-call), outcome
   174	  (assigned by the lead after the gate, never self-labeled), catches,
   175	  and lead rework minutes, with prompt-defects separated from
   176	  model-defects. Delegation boundaries move on this evidence, not
   177	  vibes. Current signal: pinned-spec delegation runs essentially
   178	  defect-free; the serious defects cluster in volunteered additions and
   179	  design-freedom wire contracts — which is exactly where the full lens
   180	- **Invocation manifest:** substantial delegated/tool/skill runs get a
   181	  lightweight manifest row per invocation. Minimum fields:
   182	  `run_id`, `parent_report`, `role_or_lens`, `model`, `wrapper`,
   183	  `session_id`, `prompt_sha256`, `prompt_path`, `output_path`, `status`,
   184	  `consumed_by`, `disposition`, and `commit_or_pr`. Raw logs can stay
   185	  out of git; every ephemeral artifact still needs a committed pointer
   186	  row with `path`, `sha256` or stable id, `promoted_to`, and
   187	  `not_promoted_reason`.
   188	
   189	## Council discipline
   190	
   191	Councils are expensive instruments. Use a full council for methodology,
   192	measurement validity, schema/contract changes, claim boundaries, hardware
   193	protocols, or explicit user requests. For ordinary implementation, use a
   194	small number of targeted lenses plus lead adjudication.
   195	
   196	Every high-impact council must leave a durable scorecard:
   197	
   198	- unique catches by severity,
   199	- accepted/rejected/deferred/false-positive counts,
   200	- lead triage and rework time when practical,
   201	- shipped artifacts,
   202	- queue rows created or re-ranked,
   203	- decision-log IDs promoted, and
   204	- a disposition table: finding → ruling → owner → artifact/queue/decision
   205	  target → closure check.
   206	
   207	Deferred decision-log promotion is itself a tracked obligation, not
   208	ambient prose in a report.
   209	
   210	## Spend guardrails (WO-022; R2 ruled, Ed-ratified 2026-07-13)
   211	
   212	The following policy text is the R2-ratified section, landed verbatim per
   213	audit work order WO-022 (`docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/`).
   214	
   215	SPEND GUARDRAILS (capstone benchmark bands) — provisional calibration constants; review after two completed arcs; sunset at capstone submission.
   216	
   217	1. ACCOUNTING SOURCE. Sol spend: `codex-usage` local accounting (the standing snapshot convention), corroborated by codex-run-v3 manifest `token_usage` rows where populated. The extraction window must cover the full arc — sum incremental snapshots for multi-day arcs; a single trailing-24h view is insufficient. Fable spend: estimated from local usage accounting; each snapshot names its method and price-table version. Price table v2026-07 (pinned until amended): GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30 per M in/out, cached input $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1. All figures are estimates, not billing truth, and are recorded as such. Missing data is recorded as `accounting_unknown`, never as zero.
   218	
   219	2. DENOMINATOR AND CACHED-TOKEN TREATMENT. Token bands count total tokens (cached + uncached, all directions) exactly as codex-usage reports them — cached tokens are never excluded (exclusion invites cache-heavy gaming). Dollar figures apply cached pricing honestly. Cross-family aggregate ceilings bind in combined estimated dollars, because raw cross-family token sums are not commensurable (C-028: Sol ~180x the token volume, Fable ~3.4x the cost).
   220	
   221	3. BOUNDARIES AND ATTRIBUTION. An arc = one council-log C-row, opened at its first delegated session, closed at its closeout snapshot. A work order = one WO/task id. Failed calls, retries, resumes, refuters, fix rounds, delta re-audits, lead usage, and subagents all count against the initiating WO and arc. Arcs and WOs may not be split, renamed, or reopened to reset counters.
   222	
   223	4. BANDS. Each dimension is independent. SOFT crossing = record-and-continue: flag in the spend snapshot plus a one-line justification in the council row. HARD crossing = pause-and-ask Ed before any NEW delegated work in that category; in-flight sessions finish; quiet-machine measurement is never interrupted.
   224	
   225	   | Scope | Soft | Hard |
   226	   |---|---|---|
   227	   | Sol high session | 6M tokens | 12M |
   228	   | Sol xhigh session | 8M | 16M |
   229	   | Sol ultra session | 40M | 60M |
   230	   | Bench-effort WO | 10M / 3 Sol sessions / ~$40 combined | 20M / 6 / ~$80 |
   231	   | Session-effort WO | 30M / 8 Sol sessions / ~$100 combined | 60M / 12 / ~$200 |
   232	   | Arc | 100M / 25 Sol sessions / ~$400 combined / 6 Sol active-hours / 2 elapsed days | 200M / 40 / ~$800 / 12 h / 4 days |
   233	
   234	   WO dollar figures are best-effort: when per-WO Fable attribution is accounting_unknown, the token/session pair binds. Ultra: at most 2 INTENDED ultra sessions per arc, each with a pre-run recorded statement of why xhigh is insufficient and what bounded subagent work it will perform; an unintended ultra is recorded as an anomaly and still counts.
   235	
   236	   Calibration anchors (recorded so recalibration stays honest): healthy xhigh ≈ 2.3–3.5M tokens/session (C-030 post effort-fix; C-028 average); the recorded broken state averaged ~9M. C-028 (330.6M / 59 sessions / ~$1,050 / ~17.5h) crosses every substantive arc HARD dimension — it is the anti-example. The 2026-07-13 comprehensive audit (~30 Sol sessions + ~70 Fable agents, Ed-authorized) crosses arc SOFT on session count only — the intended "exceptional: justify and continue" outcome.
   237	
   238	5. CHECKPOINTS (procedural; owner = the Fable lead). (a) At arc open: predeclare one accepted deliverable increment for the arc — a corpus/measurement result, analysis/figure/report increment, evaluator requirement, or cited advancement of a D-060 gate — and classify planned delegated work as deliverable-facing or process-facing (mixed sessions count as process-facing unless separately attributable). (b) Before each next delegated call: check the completed session against its tier band (a lightweight glance, not a full snapshot); no runtime killing is promised — evaluation happens on completed sessions before any resume, replacement, or new call. (c) At WO close and arc close: take the spend snapshot and evaluate all bands. One missed checkpoint blocks new process-facing delegation until reconciled.
   239	
   240	6. DELIVERABLE-PROGRESS TRIPWIRE (binds while ANY D-060 gate is unmet). If process-facing combined estimated cost exceeds 33% of arc cost OR $250 — whichever occurs first — HARD pause-and-ask Ed before further process-facing delegation. Independently, an arc that closes with process-facing spend but NO accepted deliverable increment pauses further non-exempt process work even if the 33% threshold was not crossed.
   241	
   242	7. EXCEPTIONS AND OVERRIDES. Gate-closing work is deliverable-facing by definition. Correctness-defect and data-preservation work may override the allocation tripwire but is always fully counted. Ed direction is NOT a blanket exemption (the finding's own exemplar — bridge v1/v1.1 — was Ed-directed): it is a recorded override carrying an incremental budget and an expiry, and its spend counts.
   243	
   244	8. NAMED-FAILURE BAR FOR PROCESS INNOVATION. Any NEW process layer, tool, skill, wrapper version, or contract version requires a decision-log entry citing: (a) a named recorded failure it addresses, (b) why existing controls did not cover it, (c) the smallest new layer that does, (d) its applicability predicate, (e) its marginal budget, (f) a sunset/retirement condition. Absent that entry, it is D-060 breadth and waits for the gates.
   245	
   246	9. KEEP-DEFENDER GUARANTEE. No cap consequence auto-deletes a review layer. Layers with recorded unique catches survive any cap; a cap response batches, rescopes, or seeks Ed approval — never silently drops catch-bearing gates (final-head, integration, lead-live, claim/evidence safeguards).
   247	
   248	10. MECHANISM. This policy is PROCEDURAL, not mechanical: no checker script is built now (adding process code during an overengineering correction is self-defeating; the arithmetic is a handful of numbers already recorded at existing snapshot points). Two recorded accounting discrepancies or skipped checkpoints across two arcs constitute the named failure that authorizes an executable checker with tests — via the §8 bar.
   249	
   250	11. RECALIBRATION AND OWNERSHIP.    261	## Topology: how it evolved (an example of the loop improving itself)
   262	
   263	- **v1 (2026-07-07 AM):** per-stream Fable orchestrator subagents, each
   264	  driving its own Codex thread. Worked, but expensive at the apex tier.
   265	- **v2 (2026-07-07 PM):** Opus orchestrators directing Codex, Fable
   266	  apex-only. Ran four streams — and surfaced a structural flaw: subagent
   267	  orchestrators are not woken by their childrens' completion (the "wake
   268	  gap"), forcing the lead to babysit with heartbeats. The session's own
   269	  trace captured two fleet-wide stalls.
   270	- **Meta-review (C-009):** a signed cross-model consensus — two blind
   271	  Codex analyses vs. the lead's blind position, one conferral round —
   272	  produced a hybrid: the lead drives pipeline-shaped streams directly
   273	  (inheriting the harness's only reliable wake guarantee); subagent
   274	  directors are reserved for judgment-heavy streams.
   275	- **Validation (C-010, 2026-07-08):** the first full session under the
   276	  new topology ran ~26 Codex sessions across four streams — resume
   277	  through merge — with zero coordination stalls, zero manual wake
   278	  interventions, and no subagent stream directors at all.
   279	  The consensus is now the stamped default.
   280	
   281	The same mechanism has overturned the lead's own designs: a Codex
   282	review of the lead's process schemas rejected two of them and supplied
   283	better ones (now the v2 ledger and calibration formats), and review
   284	lenses have refuted two of the lead's sanctioned wire-protocol pins
   285	before they could reach hardware. Seniority is not infallibility; the
   286	adjudication of every such challenge remains the lead's.
   287	
   288	## What one session looks like (2026-07-07/08, the merge session)
   289	
   290	Four checkpointed streams resumed, completed, and landed as four PRs:
   291	the integrity/provenance overhaul (all 31 audit-pinned defects fixed;
   292	strict validation now re-derives the power trace from raw evidence),
   293	the docs package, the KV-cache replay feasibility verdict, and the
   294	complete fixture-first NVIDIA stack. The layered review recorded, among
   295	~30 attributed catches: two blockers found only by fresh-instance
   296	lenses (a provenance hash that did not prove the actual generation
   297	input; a strict-gate bypass via mutable metadata), two pinned wire
   298	contracts overturned before hardware contact, one fabricated-evidence
   299	defect caught only at the lead's diff gate, two integration defects
   300	caught only by the post-merge integration review, and a crash path
   301	caught only by the final-head rule on the last commit of the night.
   302	Suite: 415 → 546 tests, zero expected failures. Roughly two dozen
   303	delegated Codex sessions; the lead never wrote implementation code and
   304	never skipped a gate.

     1	# Claude Code Notes

     3	This repository has a project-local Codex MCP server plus an audited script
     4	bridge. On Ed's configured desktop, the script bridge is also the native
     5	pet-visible background route.

     7	## Primary Path: Codex MCP
     8	
     9	The tracked `.mcp.json` starts `codex mcp-server`. Claude Code exposes the
    10	server's two entry points as the `codex` tool (start a session) and
    11	`codex-reply` (continue the returned thread).
    12	
    13	Select effort only as specified by `.claude/skills/codex/SKILL.md` §Effort
    14	selection.

    16	The Claude-facing MCP server disables the reverse Claude server for its child
    17	Codex sessions; top-level Codex sessions still load the reverse server.
    18	
    19	On the first launch from a clone, run Claude Code and approve the project
    20	server when prompted; Claude intentionally requires per-project approval for
    21	tracked `.mcp.json` servers. Then verify the bridge:
    22	
    23	```bash
    24	scripts/check-codex-mcp.mjs
    25	```
    26	
    27	The ONE home for bridge wire policy is `docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md`
    28	(`bridge-protocol/v1.1`). The launch sequence lives in
    29	`.claude/skills/codex/SKILL.md`.

    31	The enforcement boundaries remain local because prompt text is part of their
    32	enforcement:
    33	
    34	- `WRITE_SCOPE` is exhaustive; never infer additional scope from tests, generated files, repository instructions, or work believed necessary for completion.
    35	- Never start or continue a `[QUIET-MAC]` measurement while an agent session is active.
    36	- Never use `danger-full-access` or sandbox/approval bypass flags.
    37	- Bridge depth is one hop: a Claude-originated Sol session must not call Claude by MCP, `claude -p`, or any other launcher.
    38	- A missing, duplicated, malformed, or non-final required envelope is protocol failure, never success.

    40	The tracked Claude subagent `.claude/agents/codex.md`, `/codex` command in

     1	# Agent Playbook: Ordered Missions
     2	
     3	Audience: an agent (or human) told "go do the next step" with no other
     4	context. This file turns the project's plans into self-contained,
     5	executable missions. Each mission says what to read, what to do, how to
     6	verify, and what to update afterward.
     7	
     8	Division of labor (D-023 discipline — do not duplicate):
     9	
    10	- **This file owns:** the operational wrapper per mission (read-first
    11	  lists, execution order, verification commands, handoff checklists) and
    12	  the code-level pointers from the 2026-07-05 external code review that
    13	  exist nowhere else.
    14	- **It points to:** `docs/phase_N/phase_N_plan.md` for objectives, gates,
    15	  acceptance criteria, and fallbacks; `docs/phase_2/
    16	  hardware_slice_implementation_guide.md` for hardware-slice pinned APIs;
    17	  `docs/decision_log.md` for settled decisions; the phase exit checklists
    18	  for current per-item status.
    19	- **No status lives here.** To find out what is already done, read
    20	  `RUN_STATE.md` and the exit checklists. To find out what outranks what,
    21	  read `TASK_QUEUE.md`. If this playbook and a plan disagree, the plan
    22	  wins; fix the drift in the same run.
    23	
    24	## How To Pick A Mission
    25	
    26	1. Run Mission M0 (preflight) — always.
    27	2. Take the highest-ranked task in `TASK_QUEUE.md` whose gate is open.
    28	3. Find its mission below and execute it. One mission per session unless
    29	   the first finishes early and cleanly.
    30	
    31	Gate summary (check the queue/checklists for live status; this is just
    32	the dependency shape):
    33	
    34	```text
    35	ungated, any time:      M1 (Slice 2N), M2 (backup protocol prep), M3 (related work)
    36	needs user/advisor:     M4 (D-016 model selection), and the P1 evidence gates
    37	needs D-016 + install:  M5 (2G MLX)
    38	needs auth session:     M6 (2H powermetrics)
    39	needs M5+M6:            M7 (2I Mac slice — the flagship)
    40	needs P1-006 evidence:  M8 (2K/2L remote-target live validation;
    41	                         2K fixture-first stack merged 2026-07-08 via PR #11)
    42	needs M7:               M9 (2M baselines)
    43	post-docs branch:       M10 Stage 3.0.1 verdict is replay_supported
    44	                         after lead live re-verification
    45	needs 2M baselines:     M10 later pairing-feasibility matrix + split runs
    46	```
    47	
    48	---
    49	
    50	## Mission M0: Preflight (every session)
    51	
    52	1. Read only the targeted `RUN_STATE.md` sections: `ACTIVE_STOP_CARD`
    53	   if present, "Current Project Status", "Known Workspace State", and
    54	   "What Is Next". If the stop card is ACTIVE, it overrides this
    55	   playbook and the task queue until cleared.
    56	2. Read `TASK_QUEUE.md`'s Current Queue and Do-Not-Do-Yet list.
    57	3. Read the selected mission's own read-first list. Read `AGENT_PLAN.md`
    58	   only at phase starts or when the project structure changes. Consult
    59	   `docs/decision_log.md` by targeted decision ID, not as a whole-file
    60	   intake step.
    61	   If the session involves delegation, review, or multi-stream work, also
    62	   read `docs/orchestration.md` (the process layer) — not optional for
    63	   landing code.
    64	4. Check workspace state with `git status --short --branch`; inspect
    65	   recent commits only when the handoff or mission needs them.
    66	5. `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` — expect `Ran <N> tests` (N per `RUN_STATE.md` Current Verification; `, OK
    67	   (skipped=10)` with zero expected failures as of 2026-07-08 after
    68	   P2-013/P2-014 and the C-011 rigor mechanics. The skips are the `[analysis]`-extra chart tests plus one
    69	   optional-jsonschema test. A red suite is itself the mission: stop and fix
    70	   or report.
    71	6. Review `docs/risk_register.md` at phase starts, before hardware tasks,
    72	   when a trigger fires, or if >14 days passed since the last run report
    73	   with no break recorded in `docs/milestones.md`.
    74	7. At session end, always: update `RUN_STATE.md`, update `TASK_QUEUE.md`,
    75	   write a dated run report in `docs/run_reports/`, update the phase exit
    76	   checklist for anything that closed, and `PROJECT_STATUS.md` if
    77	   advisor-visible state changed. Commit when the user asks or has
    78	   standing-approved it.
    79	
    80	Environment cautions:
    81	
    82	- The repo must stay at a non-iCloud path (`~/code/...`; R-017). If you
    83	  see `Operation not permitted` on reads inside the repo, stop, wait for
    84	  the lock to clear, re-run the suite, and record the incident.
    85	- CI installs no extras; every new test must pass on a bare Python

     6	## Intake Rule For New Tasks
     7	
     8	For every new user task:
     9	
    10	1. Read `RUN_STATE.md`.
    11	2. Read this file.
    12	3. Check `git status --short --branch`.
    13	4. Review the last 2-3 commits with `git log --oneline --decorate -3`.
    14	5. Check relevant handoffs in `docs/run_reports/`.

    16	   outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card's resume/cleanup
    17	   instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.
    18	7. Decide whether the task is:
    19	   - urgent workspace hygiene,
    20	   - Phase 1 evidence work,
    21	   - Phase 2 implementation prep,
    22	   - later-phase research work,
    23	   - documentation/reporting,
    24	   - or unrelated/new scope.
    25	8. Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence,
    26	   and blockers.
    27	9. If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.
    28	10. Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the
    29	    corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same
    30	    status with dated evidence, and the Completed row's evidence cell
    31	    must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists
    32	    for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.
    33	
    34	## Priority Scale
    35	
    36	- **P0 Safety**: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or
    37	  corrupted repo state.
    38	- **P1 Phase Gate**: required to close the current phase or unblock the next
    39	  phase responsibly.
    40	- **P2 Next Slice**: next implementation slice after current phase gates are
    41	  adequately planned or closed.
    42	- **P3 Research Expansion**: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for
    43	  current gate.
    44	- **P4 Polish**: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or
    45	  presentation work.
    46	
    47	## Ranking Factors
    48	
    49	Rank higher when a task:
    50	
    51	- Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.
    52	- Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.
    53	- Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.
    54	- Is required before physical hardware time is spent.
    55	- Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.
    56	- Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.
    57	
    58	Rank lower when a task:
    59	
    60	- Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.
    61	- Is a later-phase feature.
    62	- Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.
    63	- Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.
    64	
    65	## Ready/Shelf Rule
    66	
    67	A partially built or proposed task is **READY** only when it has:
    68	
    69	- one authority document or stream-log pointer,
    70	- bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,
    71	- explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,
    72	- no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and
    73	- a named lane (`[AGENT]`, `[QUIET-MAC]`, or `[ED-EXTERNAL]`).
    74	
    75	If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or
    76	planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work.
    77	Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer
    78	and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.
    79	
    80	## Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)
    81	
    82	Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with
    83	its machine state, not the top task absolutely:
    84	
    85	- **[QUIET-MAC]** — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex
    86	  load, idle gate will flag contamination.
    87	- **[AGENT]** — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy
    88	  sessions.
    89	- **[ED-EXTERNAL]** — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access,
    90	  purchases, destinations.

     1	# Claude ↔ Codex Bridge Protocol
     2	
     3	`bridge-protocol/v1.1`
     4	
     5	This contract defines the task, return, scope, concurrency, continuation, and
     6	reverse-consult protocols used when Claude and Codex collaborate on JouleWise.
     7	Its goals are bounded authority, machine-detectable outcomes, recoverable
     8	threads, attribution-aware workspace writes, and concise peer discussion.
     9	Repository safety rules and lead authority remain controlling.
    10	
    11	Provenance: co-designed by the Fable lead and gpt-5.6-sol over the MCP bridge
    12	itself (3 rounds, 2026-07-13; thread recorded in
    13	`docs/run_reports/2026-07-13-bridge-v1.md`).
    14	The five in-draft choices were adjudicated by the lead at review.
    15	
    16	Provenance for v1.1: amendments co-designed by the lead and a Sol xhigh
    17	consult on 2026-07-13, thread
    18	`019f5d1d-b681-7db1-8714-812fdd2f198b`.
    19	
    20	### Changes from v1
    21	
    22	Version 1.1 adds the read-only discussion lane, fail-closed session wrappers,
    23	tolerant single-line envelopes, per-call reverse-consult effort, peer channels
    24	and bounded proposal diffs, and a single-envelope protocol-deviation path.
    25	
    26	## 1. Prompt contract
    27	
    28	Every delegated prompt MUST begin with a machine-readable task header: a
    29	`BRIDGE_TASK_V1` sentinel line, one JSON object, and an `END_BRIDGE_TASK_V1`
    30	sentinel line. JSON gives the tracked helper and future adapters one
    31	unambiguous representation.
    32	
    33	Required fields:
    34	
    35	- `TASK_SHAPE`: Interaction shape; one of `interactive`, `bounded`, or
    36	  `autonomous`.
    37	- `GENRE`: Work genre; one of `discussion`, `implementation`, `review`, or
    38	  `diagnosis`.
    39	- `ROLE`: One bounded worker role or review lens.
    40	- `OBJECTIVE`: One concrete requested outcome.
    41	- `AUTHORITY`: Ordered authority pointers and inline rulings; highest
    42	  authority first.
    43	- `WRITE_SCOPE`: Exhaustive repository write allowlist; `[]` means read-only.
    44	- `BASE_HEAD`: Full Git HEAD object id at launch.
    45	- `BASELINE_MANIFEST`: Repository-relative path to the immutable launch
    46	  manifest.
    47	- `BASELINE_DIGEST`: SHA-256 of the canonical baseline manifest.
    48	- `ACCEPTANCE`: Observable conditions required for completion.
    49	- `VERIFICATION`: Checks or commands expected before completion.
    50	- `EARLY_RETURN`: Permitted decision returns; normally `NEEDS_SCOPE` and
    51	  `NEEDS_RULING`.
    52	- `OUTPUT_PROTOCOL`: Required return protocol; `bridge-report/v1`.
    53	
    54	`AUTHORITY` SHOULD point to durable repository sources instead of reproducing
    55	large files. Inline context SHOULD contain only the current ruling, unstable
    56	facts, and small controlling excerpts.
    57	
    58	Future gate packets MUST give source line ranges for their citations. Text
    59	labelled `verbatim` MUST be reproduced verbatim; paraphrase, ellipsis, or other
    60	editing MUST be labelled as such rather than presented as a verbatim excerpt.
    61	
    62	`ROLE` MUST NOT combine implementation, independent review, and final
    63	adjudication.
    64	
    65	Each `WRITE_SCOPE` entry is an object with `path` and `match`. `match` is
    66	`exact`, `subtree`, or `all`; paths are normalized repository-relative paths.
    67	`{"path": "*", "match": "all"}` is the only whole-repository form.
    68	
    69	A delegated worker MUST NOT infer additional scope from tests, generated
    70	files, repository instructions, or work believed necessary for completion.
    71	
    72	Read-only sessions (`WRITE_SCOPE: []`) MAY omit `BASELINE_MANIFEST` and
    73	`BASELINE_DIGEST`; `BASE_HEAD` remains required.
    74	
    75	### Read-only discussion lane
    76	
    77	For an interactive MCP turn with `GENRE: discussion` that is read-only, the
    78	required header fields reduce to `TASK_SHAPE`, `GENRE`, `ROLE`, `OBJECTIVE`,
    79	`AUTHORITY`, and `OUTPUT_PROTOCOL`. `WRITE_SCOPE` MAY be omitted and then means
    80	`[]`; `EARLY_RETURN` MAY be omitted and then means `["NEEDS_RULING"]`.
    81	
    82	`BASE_HEAD` is REQUIRED whenever the advice depends on repository state,
    83	including code review, diagnosis, or any turn expected to carry a proposal
    84	diff. It MAY be omitted only for repository-independent discussion.
    85	`ACCEPTANCE`, `VERIFICATION`, `BASELINE_MANIFEST`, and `BASELINE_DIGEST` are
    86	omitted in this lane.
    87	
    88	The discussion context capsule SHOULD provide section-level authority anchors
    89	rather than bare file paths; current HEAD plus dirty-path and concurrent-writer
    90	state when repository-dependent; and the settled decisions, rejected
    91	alternatives, and remaining challengeable questions.
    92	
    93	A same-thread peer-channel continuation MAY use a compact delta prompt. It
    94	inherits `ROLE`, `GENRE`, `AUTHORITY`, and `OUTPUT_PROTOCOL` from the opening
    95	header and states only new rulings and repository changes since the previous
    96	turn. A change of role, authority, scope, or objective class REQUIRES a fresh
    97	full header and usually a fresh thread under §5.
    98	
    99	The full header remains mandatory whenever `WRITE_SCOPE` is nonempty or
   100	`TASK_SHAPE` is `autonomous`.
   101	
   102	Compact example:
   103	
   104	```text
   105	BRIDGE_TASK_V1
   106	{
   107	  "TASK_SHAPE": "bounded",
   108	  "GENRE": "implementation",
   109	  "ROLE": "focused bridge-tool implementer",
   110	  "OBJECTIVE": "Implement lease acquisition and release with focused tests.",
   111	  "AUTHORITY": [
   112	    "docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md",
   113	    "AGENTS.md",
   114	    "User ruling: overlapping write leases hard-block by default."
   115	  ],
   116	  "WRITE_SCOPE": [
   117	    {"path": "scripts/bridge", "match": "exact"},
   118	    {"path": "tests/test_bridge.py", "match": "exact"}
   119	  ],
   120	  "BASE_HEAD": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
   121	  "BASELINE_MANIFEST": ".codex-bridge/baselines/inv-123.json",
   122	  "BASELINE_DIGEST": "sha256:0123456789abcdef",
   123	  "ACCEPTANCE": [
   124	    "Overlapping write leases fail unless a lead override is recorded.",
   125	    "Release and abandoned states are distinguishable."
   126	  ],
   127	  "VERIFICATION": [
   128	    "python3 -m unittest tests.test_bridge"
   129	  ],
   130	  "EARLY_RETURN": ["NEEDS_SCOPE", "NEEDS_RULING"],
   131	  "OUTPUT_PROTOCOL": "bridge-report/v1"
   132	}
   133	END_BRIDGE_TASK_V1
   134	```
   135	
   136	## 2. Return envelope
   137	
   138	Protocol layering is intentional: `claude-codex-report/v1` (D-064) remains
   139	the canonical full session report for audited CLI runs made through
   140	`codex-run-v3 --genre`, while `bridge-report/v1` is the lightweight final-lines
   141	envelope REQUIRED for MCP turns and the reverse consult. An audited CLI run
   142	carrying a valid `claude-codex-report/v1` body is exempt from the trailer.
   143	
   144	Every successful MCP turn or reverse consult MUST end with exactly two
   145	nonempty lines:
   146	
   147	> `BRIDGE_REPORT_V1`
   148	> `{"status":"DONE","summary":"Lease support implemented.","pathspec":["scripts/bridge","tests/test_bridge.py"],"verification":["python3 -m unittest tests.test_bridge: OK"],"flags":[]}`
   149	
   150	The first line is the literal sentinel. The second line is one JSON object on
   151	one physical line with these required fields:
   152	
   153	- `status`: One status from the enum below.
   154	- `summary`: Concise outcome or blocker summary.
   155	- `pathspec`: Repository paths changed by this worker; `[]` for read-only
   156	  turns.
   157	- `verification`: Checks actually performed and their results, not planned
   158	  checks.
   159	- `flags`: Machine-consumable strings such as `route_cli`, `no_edits`, or
   160	  `verification_incomplete`.
   161	
   162	Statuses:
   163	
   164	- `DONE`: The requested outcome and acceptance conditions are complete.
   165	- `PARTIAL`: Useful bounded work is complete, but requested work remains.
   166	- `DISCUSSION`: A read-only design or judgment turn completed.
   167	- `NEEDS_SCOPE`: Progress requires additional write authority.
   168	- `NEEDS_RULING`: Progress requires a lead-owned decision.
   169	- `BLOCKED`: An external or technical prerequisite prevents progress and is
   170	  not resolved solely by scope or a design ruling.
   171	- `FAILED`: Execution failed or the worker cannot provide a trustworthy
   172	  result.
   173	
   174	The envelope is a protocol failure if its sentinel is absent, duplicated,
   175	malformed, or not final. No non-whitespace content may follow its JSON line.
   176	Interior whitespace on the JSON line is allowed. Unknown additional object
   177	keys are tolerated and ignored for forward compatibility; the five required
   178	fields and the status enum remain mandatory. Normatively, `status` and
   179	`summary` are JSON strings, `summary` is nonempty, and `pathspec`,
   180	`verification`, and `flags` are JSON arrays whose elements are strings.
   181	
   182	Malformed or missing envelopes MUST NOT be interpreted as successful
   183	completion, regardless of preceding prose.
   184	
   185	For a substantive, multi-issue `GENRE: discussion` turn, the human-readable
   186	body uses this order:
   187	
   188	1. `Positions`
   189	2. `Disagreements`
   190	3. `Open questions`
   191	4. `Recommendation`
   192	
   193	Sections with no content MAY say `None`. A trivial single-question discussion
   194	MAY answer directly without these headings. The final envelope is always
   195	required.
   196	
   197	## 3. Early returns
   198	
   199	A worker MUST return early instead of guessing when authority or a lead-owned
   200	decision is missing.
   201	
   202	A `NEEDS_SCOPE` body MUST contain:
   203	
   204	- `Requested paths`: Exact additional paths and match semantics.
   205	- `Reason`: Why each path is necessary.
   206	- `Completed`: Independent authorized work already completed.
   207	- `Blocked work`: Work that cannot proceed without expansion.
   208	
   209	A `NEEDS_RULING` body MUST contain:
   210	
   211	- `Question`: One decision the lead must make.
   212	- `Options considered`: Material alternatives and consequences.
   213	- `Recommendation`: The worker's preferred option and reason.
   214	- `Blocked work`: Work awaiting the ruling.
   215	
   216	The lead SHOULD continue the same thread after answering either early return.
   217	
   218	Scope approval is prospective only. It does not legitimize an earlier
   219	out-of-scope write.
   220	
   221	Before resuming with expanded scope, the lead MUST update `WRITE_SCOPE` and
   222	atomically acquire the corresponding workspace lease or use `lease-expand` to
   223	expand it prospectively.
   224	
   225	## 4. Task-shape routing
   226	
   227	Reasoning effort does not determine transport. Interaction shape does.
   228	
   229	| Work shape | Preferred path | Examples |
   230	|---|---|---|
   231	| Interactive | MCP | Discussion, rulings, follow-up questions, short diagnosis |
   232	| Bounded | MCP when short; CLI when evidence-heavy | Focused edit, narrow review, small fix round |
   233	| Autonomous | Audited CLI | Broad audit, long test run, multi-file implementation, subagent work |
   234	| Durable evidence required | Audited CLI | D-050/D-064 run, timeout-sensitive work, mechanically enforced scope |
   235	| Independent review | Fresh MCP or CLI thread | Adversarial lens, final-head review, counterreview |
   236	
   237	An xhigh discussion MAY use MCP. A long high-effort mechanical run SHOULD use
   238	CLI.
   239	
   240	### T3-mediated presentation, routing, and provenance
   241	
   242	T3 is the preferred presentation plane when it is in use. It is neither a
   243	mandatory nor an exclusive bridge plane, and it never becomes the compliance
   244	plane. These t3-specific rules apply only to t3-mediated activity. A plain
   245	Claude Code session remains first-class and carries no t3-specific ceremony.
   246	
   247	For a t3-mediated invocation, the tracked provenance record MUST distinguish
   248	four axes: `control_plane`, `transport`, `authority_class`, and `governance`
   249	(implementation follow-on: `T3-PROV-SCHEMA-01` in
   250	`docs/process_traces/2026-08-05-t3-amend/AMENDMENT-MAP.md`).
   251	The selected task-shape route in the table above is the authoritative
   252	transport record. A rollout's `session_meta.originator` MAY be recorded beside
   253	that set only as a provenance hint. It is never the sole discriminator and
   254	never authority-bearing. The observed values `t3code_desktop` and
   255	`codex_cli_rs` are version-bound observations from CLI version `0.146.0`, not
   256	a closed enum or a compatibility promise. Classification authority comes from
   257	the §4 launch route and the lease event's §6 `owner_kind`. Absence of the
   258	optional hint never disables a route or classification. If the hint is present,
   259	an unknown value or a value contradictory to those authoritative fields fails
   260	closed: it does not establish native, wrapped, delegated, top-level, approval,
   261	or gate status.
   262	
   263	T3 `Full access` mode is prohibited for this repository; t3-mediated work uses
   264	only Supervised or Auto. The prohibition does not depend on an asserted
   265	UI-to-CLI flag mapping. In Auto, phone cards are post-hoc notifications and
   266	never approval evidence. Thread-side reports are inadmissible on approval
   267	semantics because the model is blind to the harness approval layer. Anything
   268	requiring Ed's eyes uses Supervised, and a claim that Supervised held or
   269	blocked an action requires harness-event evidence rather than the thread's own
   270	account.
   271	
   272	T3-native Codex threads are Ed-direct only. They MUST NOT receive
   273	lead-delegated or gate-bearing work. If their output is materially consumed,
   274	the lead MUST append a tracked ingestion event that binds the native session
   275	identity, output digest, lead disposition, and tracked process-trace location
   276	(implementation follow-on: `T3-PROV-SCHEMA-01` in
   277	`docs/process_traces/2026-08-05-t3-amend/AMENDMENT-MAP.md`). A t3 activity
   278	marker or thread transcript alone is not that event.
   279	
   280	The tracked Codex subagent route is limited to substantial background or
   281	parallel Sol rounds that require operator-visible lifecycle state. It is a
   282	thin dispatch and presentation steward, not an implementation or adjudication
   283	authority, and the audited child ceremony remains controlling. Each wrapper
   284	invocation counts as a subagent invocation for D-080 accounting and MUST NOT be
   285	silently deduplicated from the child run. This conditional route is a two-arc
   286	pilot; each arc records whether Ed used the activity view, wrapper failures,
   287	latency, and Fable overhead before the default is retained or changed through
   288	its owning process.
   289	
   290	TUI operation remains available only outside `[QUIET-MAC]` work. Claim-bearing
   291	runs use an ordinary guarded shell with zero agent sessions; t3 availability
   292	does not relax the repository's zero-agent doctrine.
   293	
   294	If MCP work expands beyond a short bounded turn, the worker SHOULD stop at a
   295	safe boundary and return:
   296	
   297	- `status: PARTIAL`
   298	- `flags` containing `route_cli`
   299	- A body stating completed work, remaining work, verification state, and an
   300	  exact CLI handoff
   301	
   302	The worker MUST NOT use routing as implicit authority to broaden scope.
   303	
   304	## 5. Thread semantics
   305	
   306	Continue an existing thread for:
   307	
   308	- A ruling requested by that thread
   309	- A prospective scope expansion
   310	- Fixes to the same implementation
   311	- Questions about that thread's result
   312	- Delta review of the same worker's changes
   313	- Completion of the same objective after a bounded interruption
   314	
   315	Start a fresh thread for:
   316	
   317	- A new objective or workstream
   318	- A different role or review lens
   319	- Independent or adversarial review
   320	- Materially different authority or privilege
   321	- A completed thread receiving unrelated work
   322	- Repository assumptions too stale to repair with a compact continuation
   323	  prompt
   324	
   325	`resume_policy` values:
   326	
   327	- `preferred`: Same-thread continuation preserves useful task state.
   328	- `allowed`: Continuation is safe, but a fresh thread is also reasonable.
   329	- `fresh_required`: Independence, changed authority, or context degradation
   330	  requires a new thread.
   331	
   332	Thread states:
   333	
   334	- `pending`: MCP call started; thread id not yet returned.
   335	- `waiting_lead`: Worker returned an early question or partial result.
   336	- `active`: Continued work is running.
   337	- `complete`: Objective finished.
   338	- `abandoned`: Thread intentionally closed or superseded.
   339	- `lost_before_return`: Blocking call ended without exposing a thread id.
   340	
   341	Thread events MUST include:
   342	
   343	- `schema`, `event`, `invocation_id`, and timestamp
   344	- `thread_id`, nullable until bind
   345	- `task`, `role`, `genre`, and `task_shape`
   346	- `state`, `resume_policy`, and `resume_reason`
   347	- `base_head` and `baseline_digest`
   348	- `write_scope_digest`
   349	- Last bridge status
   350	- Prompt and output paths or hashes when available
   351	
   352	Long threads degrade through stale repository facts, accumulated rejected
   353	approaches, reduced instruction salience, and role drift. Continuation
   354	prompts MUST restate current rulings and changed repository state rather than
   355	assuming the old context remains current.
   356	
   357	## 6. Workspace leases
   358	
   359	Workspace leases are cooperative concurrency controls recorded in
   360	`.codex-bridge/workspace-lease-events.jsonl`.
   361	
   362	Lease events MUST include:
   363	
   364	- `schema`: `bridge-lease-event/v1`
   365	- `event`: `acquire`, `expand`, `release`, `abandon`, or `override`
   366	- `lease_id`
   367	- `invocation_id`
   368	- `owner_id`
   369	- `owner_kind`: `claude-thread`, `codex-mcp`, `codex-cli`, or `human`
   370	- `access`: `write` or `snapshot_read`
   371	- Canonical `paths`
   372	- `base_head`
   373	- `baseline_manifest`
   374	- `baseline_digest`
   375	- `task`, `role`, and optional `thread_id`
   376	- `host`
   377	- Optional process-identity fields `pid`, `process_start_time`, and
   378	  `process_ancestry` (an ordered ancestry record)
   379	- Event timestamp
   380	- Optional `expires_at`
   381	- Optional `note`
   382	- For overrides: conflicting lease ids, approver, reason, and resulting
   383	  attribution policy
   384	
   385	`owner_kind` is an authoritative launch-route field, not a value inferred from
   386	rollout metadata. When a t3-mediated record also carries §4 `originator`, the
   387	two fields MUST be retained separately. Absence of the optional hint never
   388	disables a route or classification. A present unknown or contradictory hint
   389	cannot override `owner_kind` and fails closed for any classification that would
   390	confer authority.
   391	
   392	Conflict detection and acquisition MUST occur under the exclusive
   393	`.codex-bridge/bridge.lock`, held via a Python standard-library `fcntl.flock`.
   394	The inner critical section reads active events, resolves stale state, checks
   395	conflicts, appends and flushes the event, then releases the lock.
   396	
   397	Every public command that mutates bridge state -- `lease-acquire`,
   398	`lease-expand`, `lease-release`, `lease-abandon`, `baseline`, `thread-record`,
   399	`session-open`, and `session-close` -- MUST also acquire the exclusive
   400	`.codex-bridge/session.lock` as its outer lock before reading bridge state.
   401	The fixed order is always `session.lock` outer, then `bridge.lock` inner.
   402	The wrappers hold `session.lock` across their complete ceremony and set
   403	`BRIDGE_SESSION_LOCK_HELD=1` for every primitive subprocess they invoke; that
   404	trusted-local delegation tells a wrapper child not to reacquire the outer lock
   405	while still taking `bridge.lock` for its own critical sections. The environment
   406	flag is a local lock-ownership convention, not general permission to bypass
   407	serialization.
   408	
   409	The read-only `lease-list`, `thread-list`, and `scope-check` commands do not
   410	take `session.lock` when invoked standalone. A `scope-check` subprocess invoked
   411	by `session-close` inherits the same held-lock environment convention and runs
   412	inside the wrapper's already-held outer lock.
   413	
   414	Overlapping active write leases hard-block acquisition.
   415	
   416	`lease-expand --lease-id ID --paths ...` is the atomic prospective-expansion
   417	mechanism: it preserves the lease owner and invocation, appends one `expand`
   418	event under the same lock, never conflicts with itself, and hard-blocks paths
   419	overlapping any other incompatible lease.
   420	
   421	A lead MAY override a conflict explicitly. The override event MUST name the
   422	conflicting leases, approver, reason, and timestamp. Unless isolation
   423	otherwise proves attribution, overridden overlap makes the affected scope
   424	check `ATTRIBUTION_INDETERMINATE`.
   425	
   426	Malformed override events MUST be rejected before append. Any malformed
   427	override already present makes the lease log unhealthy: conflict operations
   428	fail closed and `scope-check` returns `CHECK_ERROR`, never `SCOPE_OK`.
   429	
   430	Multiple `snapshot_read` leases MAY overlap when they identify the same
   431	pinned repository state.
   432	
   433	A write lease conflicts with an overlapping `snapshot_read` lease. This
   434	prevents mutation beneath an audit or other stable read.
   435	
   436	Ordinary read-only discussions need no lease unless they require a stable
   437	repository snapshot.
   438	
   439	Time expiry alone warns but does not abandon a lease. On the recorded host, a
   440	missing recorded process may be marked `abandoned` under the bridge lock.
   441	Human leases and leases without a process require explicit lead abandonment.
   442	
   443	Stale leases become `abandoned`, never silently `released`.
   444	
   445	No pattern-kills; kill only manifest-recorded PIDs verified by start-time + ancestry.
   446	
   447	A t3 checkpoint revert is forbidden in the main tree. In a worktree it is a
   448	workspace mutation: stop writers; capture the current manifest and diff;
   449	record the intended revert; resolve every active bridge lease by explicit
   450	release or abandonment; and perform the revert. Delegation MUST NOT resume
   451	until a fresh invocation has acquired a fresh lease and captured a fresh
   452	baseline. A t3 checkpoint reference is never audit evidence, and a t3
   453	checkmark is never a bridge return envelope.
   454	
   455	Lease and thread events use separate logs and join through `invocation_id`.
   456	
   457	Human edits remain a weak edge because a human can modify the workspace
   458	without acquiring a lease. Whole-project audits SHOULD therefore use a pinned
   459	clean commit or isolated worktrees, hold compatible `snapshot_read` leases,
   460	and defer writes until adjudication.

   462	### Session wrappers
   463	
   464	The preferred workspace-write ceremony layers two wrappers over the recovery
   465	primitives above:
   466	
   467	```text
   468	scripts/bridge session-open --invocation-id ID --owner-id OWNER \
   469	  --owner-kind KIND --access write --paths P... \
   470	  [--task ... --role ... --genre ... --task-shape ... --expires-in ... --note ...]
   471	scripts/bridge session-close --invocation-id ID --status STATUS \
   472	  [--lease-id ...] [--expect-digest sha256:...]
