   474	
   475	The session wrappers support write-access sessions only in v1.1.
   476	Snapshot-stable audits use the `snapshot_read` lease, baseline, scope-check,
   477	and terminal lease primitives directly under §6. Read-only advice turns need
   478	neither a lease nor a session wrapper.
   479	
   480	`session-open` MUST execute `lease-acquire`, `baseline`, and
   481	`thread-record --state pending` in that order and fail closed. If baseline
   482	capture, thread recording, or receipt creation fails after acquisition, it
   483	MUST abandon the lease with a recorded reason before returning nonzero. A hard
   484	process crash MAY leave the lease active; explicit recovery is then required.
   485	The invocation-id uniqueness check and the complete open ceremony are
   486	serialized by `session.lock`. Before acquiring a lease, `session-open` MUST
   487	refuse an invocation id already present in receipts, baseline manifests, the
   488	lease log, or the thread log. Every fresh attempt requires a new invocation
   489	id, including recovery after an abandoned pre-receipt attempt.
   490	
   491	On success it MUST create, without overwrite, an immutable
   492	`.codex-bridge/receipts/<invocation-id>.json` receipt with schema
   493	`bridge-session-receipt/v1`. The receipt binds the invocation and lease ids,
   494	base HEAD, baseline manifest and digest, canonical write-scope path specs and
   495	their digest, owner, and timestamps. An existing receipt is a hard error; a
   496	fresh attempt requires a fresh invocation id. Standard output contains the
   497	receipt plus a `header_fragment` with `BASE_HEAD`, `BASELINE_MANIFEST`,
   498	`BASELINE_DIGEST`, and `WRITE_SCOPE` ready for the task header.
   499	
   500	`session-close` MUST serialize its entire body under `session.lock`, beginning
   501	before receipt, lease, or terminal-thread reads and ending after its final
   502	output. After taking the lock it re-reads terminal state. It MUST load the
   503	receipt-bound lease's current canonical paths from the authoritative lease
   504	event chain, independently validate the receipt binding, and verify that the
   505	receipt scope is a subset of the current lease scope; a mismatch is a
   506	`CHECK_ERROR`-style hard error. Close scope is therefore the receipt scope plus
   507	recorded prospective `lease-expand` events on that same lease. The wrapper
   508	passes those current paths and their canonical digest to `scope-check` and to
   509	the closing thread event.
   510	
   511	The receipt's stored baseline digest, or an explicitly supplied
   512	`--expect-digest`, is the only external digest anchor; the wrapper MUST NOT
   513	rediscover an expected digest from the manifest being checked. It handles
   514	outcomes as follows:
   515	
   516	- For `SCOPE_OK` with `DONE`, it records `complete` and the last bridge
   517	  status, then releases the lease.
   518	- `session-close` refuses `--status DISCUSSION` unconditionally with a hard
   519	  error: no terminal thread event is appended and the lease is retained.
   520	  Advice turns use the read-only discussion lane without wrappers.
   521	- For `NEEDS_SCOPE`, `NEEDS_RULING`, `PARTIAL`, `BLOCKED`, or `FAILED`, it
   522	  records `waiting_lead` and the actual bridge status and retains the lease.
   523	  Scope-check still runs; a non-OK verdict still exits nonzero.
   524	- For `SCOPE_VIOLATION`, `ATTRIBUTION_INDETERMINATE`, or `CHECK_ERROR`, it
   525	  records the verdict in a `waiting_lead` thread event, retains the lease, and
   526	  exits nonzero. A non-OK verdict never causes automatic release; release or
   527	  abandonment after adjudication is an explicit lead action.
   528	
   529	Closing is idempotent for every outcome. If the most recent thread event
   530	already records the same state, last bridge status, current scope verdict, and
   531	current canonical write-scope digest, and the lease disposition is unchanged,
   532	another close is a no-op notice with the exit status that outcome normally
   533	has. A changed scope digest requires a new event even when the other fields
   534	match. A different status against an existing `complete` event is refused, and
   535	the wrapper MUST never append a contradictory terminal event. Standard output
   536	reports the scope-check verdict, recorded thread state, and observed lease
   537	disposition. Close observes the receipt-bound lease before validating optional
   538	argument consistency where possible, and after any subsequent error performs a
   539	best-effort locked re-read; errors therefore report the current `active` as
   540	`retained`, `released`, or `abandoned` state rather than a stale or unknown
   541	disposition.
   542	
   543	## 7. Baseline and scope check
   544	
   545	Before every workspace-write session, `scripts/bridge baseline` MUST create
   546	an immutable baseline manifest.
   547	
   548	`baseline` MUST refuse an existing invocation id and manifest path; every
   549	fresh capture requires a new invocation id.
   550	
   551	The manifest MUST contain:
   552	
   553	- Schema version and invocation id
   554	- Repository root and Git common directory
   555	- Capture timestamp
   556	- Full HEAD object id
   557	- Base64 representation of raw `git status --porcelain=v2 -z
   558	  --untracked-files=all`
   559	- Base64 representation of raw `git ls-files --stage -z`
   560	- For each baseline-dirty or untracked path:
   561	  - Repository-relative path
   562	  - Entry type
   563	  - File mode
   564	  - Content SHA-256, symlink-target hash, or submodule object id as
   565	    applicable
   566	- Canonical manifest SHA-256
   567	
   568	Canonical JSON uses UTF-8, sorted keys, compact separators, and no
   569	insignificant whitespace. Raw NUL-delimited Git output is base64-encoded so
   570	arbitrary records remain lossless.
   571	
   572	The prompt MUST provide `BASE_HEAD`, `BASELINE_MANIFEST`, and
   573	`BASELINE_DIGEST`.
   574	
   575	A future native-write acceptance-gate exercise MUST be predeclared before the
   576	write. Its evidence MUST bind the native session identity and authoritative
   577	launch route to the governing manifest, baseline digest, declared scope,
   578	output digest, and resulting artifact or commit. A later narrative or
   579	retroactive route designation cannot establish the gate. This requirement is
   580	forward-looking; it does not reopen the one previously accepted exercise:
   581	commit `97d6e3d`, the isolated one-file `RUN_STATE.md` native-write gate exercise
   582	recorded in `RUN_STATE.md`'s T3 gate/probe log and accepted in
   583	`docs/process_traces/2026-08-03-t3-doctrine-gate/SYNTHESIS.md` under
   584	“Acceptance-gate dispositions.”
   585	
   586	`scope-check` MUST receive the prompt-supplied digest through the required
   587	`--expect-digest sha256:...` argument, verify the manifest self-digest, and
   588	verify equality with that external anchor before using the manifest. A missing
   589	or mismatched anchor is `CHECK_ERROR`.
   590	
   591	When `scope-check` is invoked through `session-close`, that external anchor
   592	comes from the immutable open receipt (or an explicit close argument), never
   593	from the manifest being validated.
   594	
   595	After a workspace-write session, `scripts/bridge scope-check` compares
   596	persistent path-state changes against the baseline, declared scope, and lease
   597	history.
   598	
   599	Verdicts:
   600	
   601	- `SCOPE_OK`: Every persistent attributable delta is within declared scope;
   602	  no attribution-invalidating overlap or state change exists; and one active
   603	  or properly released write lease, selected by matching invocation id or an
   604	  explicit `--lease-id`, covers the complete declared scope. Without that
   605	  governing lease the verdict is `ATTRIBUTION_INDETERMINATE` with reason
   606	  `no_governing_lease`.
   607	- `SCOPE_VIOLATION`: At least one persistent attributable delta is outside
   608	  declared scope, or the worker made an unauthorized HEAD change. Violating
   609	  paths and reasons are listed.
   610	- `ATTRIBUTION_INDETERMINATE`: The checker observes relevant changes but
   611	  cannot attribute them soundly because of overlapping writers, unexplained
   612	  repository movement, an invalid baseline relationship, or equivalent
   613	  ambiguity. Candidate paths and reasons are listed.
   614	- `CHECK_ERROR`: The checker could not acquire required state, parse the
   615	  manifest or logs, or complete Git inspection. The result MUST NOT be
   616	  accepted.
   617	
   618	Known concurrent leases with provably non-overlapping scopes do not
   619	invalidate attribution.
   620	
   621	HEAD movement rules:
   622	
   623	- If commits were not explicitly authorized, worker-owned HEAD movement is
   624	  `SCOPE_VIOLATION`.
   625	- If commits were authorized and ownership is proven, committed and remaining
   626	  worktree deltas are scope-checked normally.
   627	- If HEAD movement is external, concurrent, or unexplained, the verdict is
   628	  `ATTRIBUTION_INDETERMINATE`.
   629	- No HEAD movement may produce `SCOPE_OK` merely because the final worktree
   630	  is clean.
   631	
   632	Scope checking proves final persistent state only. It cannot detect an
   633	out-of-scope file modified and restored before the final snapshot.
   634	
   635	Git-visible checking also does not prove the history of ignored files or
   636	writes outside the repository.
   637	
   638	`.codex-bridge/**` is bridge-internal state exempt from task `WRITE_SCOPE`,
   639	but only `scripts/bridge` and bridge launchers may write it. This is a
   640	protocol boundary, not filesystem enforcement.
   641	
   642	## 8. Reverse consult: `consult_fable`
   643	
   644	`consult_fable` is available only to a top-level Codex lead for one bounded,
   645	read-only peer judgment.
   646	
   647	In the represented steady state, top-level status is established by the
   648	authoritative §4 launch route and §6 `owner_kind`; the optional §4 `originator`
   649	hint cannot establish or elevate that status. Its absence never disables a
   650	consult, while a present unknown or contradictory value fails closed.
   651	
   652	**Normative rule.** Only an actually top-level Codex lead may invoke a reverse
   653	consult; a Claude-originated or delegated session is ineligible.
   654	
   655	**TRANSITIONAL — convention, not enforcement.** Until the four-axis provenance
   656	record, including its `authority_class` field, is representable through the
   657	implementation follow-on `T3-PROV-SCHEMA-01` in
   658	`docs/process_traces/2026-08-05-t3-amend/AMENDMENT-MAP.md`, the adapter has no
   659	authoritative signal for the caller's launch route or delegated status: it
   660	validates only the caller-supplied `BRIDGE_ORIGIN: codex` and
   661	`BRIDGE_HOPS_REMAINING: 0` lines, which neither prove top-level status nor
   662	create authority. **Mechanical acceptance of the caller-supplied header tuple is
   663	not proof of top-level status and does not establish reverse-consult
   664	authority.** During the transition the normative rule is therefore a
   665	best-effort convention, not a mechanically enforced eligibility test: a caller
   666	known or visibly marked delegated MUST NOT invoke, and a *present* unknown or
   667	contradictory delegated/origin marker fails closed — but wholly-absent status
   668	does not disable the consult (mirroring the §4 provenance rule; see §9,
   669	"Convention versus enforcement," for which properties are mechanically enforced
   670	versus convention-bound). **Fail closed at consumption:** a transitional
   671	consult result is non-authority-bearing advice — it cannot prove caller
   672	eligibility, satisfy an independent-review or approval requirement, establish
   673	gate status, expose privileged data, or displace lead adjudication. The
   674	transition ends only when `T3-PROV-SCHEMA-01` both represents the four-axis
   675	record (including `authority_class`) AND makes admission consume the
   676	authoritative §4 launch-route and §6 `owner_kind` evidence with rejection
   677	tests; merely defining or persisting the schema does not end it. Once that
   678	lands, the authoritative §4/§6 record supersedes this transitional convention.
   679	
   680	The caller's prompt MUST begin with:
   681	
   682	```text
   683	BRIDGE_ORIGIN: codex
   684	BRIDGE_HOPS_REMAINING: 0
   685	```
   686	
   687	The request MUST provide:
   688	
   689	- `Decision question`
   690	- `Current Sol position`
   691	- `Alternatives`
   692	- `Evaluation criteria`
   693	- `Settled constraints`
   694	- `Authority order`
   695	- `Repository pointers`
   696	- `Requested counterargument`
   697	- `Requested output shape`
   698	
   699	Large repository context SHOULD be supplied as exact file pointers because
   700	Fable has read/search access.
   701	
   702	The adapter MUST:
   703	
   704	1. Validate the caller-supplied bridge headers.
   705	2. Reject a Claude-originated or nonzero-hop request.
   706	3. Strip the caller headers.
   707	4. Inject one canonical header and the read-only peer role.
   708	5. Launch Fable with the configured read-only, no-MCP, no-persistence
   709	   boundary.
   710	6. Require a `bridge-report/v1` return envelope.
   711	
   712	The adapter MUST NOT pass duplicate origin headers to Fable.
   713	
   714	The tool input MAY include `effort`, whose only accepted values are `high` and
   715	`xhigh`. Unsupported values are rejected with a synthesized `FAILED`
   716	`protocol_failure` envelope and are never silently coerced; `ultra` is not
   717	exposed. The process default comes from `CLAUDE_BRIDGE_EFFORT` only when that
   718	environment value is `high` or `xhigh`; every other value falls back to
   719	`high`. The effective default remains `high` to bound latency under the tool
   720	timeout.
   721	
   722	For reproducibility, the adapter MUST pass the selected effort explicitly and
   723	prefix returned child-result text with `[consult effort: <effort>]` as its
   724	first line. This prefix precedes the child output; the envelope-final rule
   725	still binds the end of the combined text.
   726	
   727	The consult remains one-shot because persistence would weaken independence,
   728	invite bridge recursion, and blur decision ownership. Fable provides advice;
   729	the top-level Codex caller adjudicates and verifies it.
   730	
   731	Transport or protocol failure MUST return or synthesize `status: FAILED`; it
   732	MUST NOT be consumed as peer approval.
   733	
   734	A successful one-shot consult may end only `DISCUSSION` or `NEEDS_RULING`.
   735	Any other well-formed child status is a protocol deviation: the adapter strips
   736	the child's trailing sentinel and JSON line, passes through the remaining
   737	child text, names the claimed status in diagnostic prose, and appends one
   738	synthesized `FAILED` envelope flagged `protocol_deviation`. The returned text
   739	therefore contains exactly one sentinel, and the adapter returns
   740	`isError: true`.
   741	
   742	## Peer channels and proposal diffs
   743	
   744	A peer channel is a long-lived `GENRE: discussion` thread scoped to one
   745	coherent design objective or workstream. A new objective, changed role, or
   746	independent or adversarial review requires a fresh thread under §5. A peer
   747	channel MUST NOT be presented or counted as independent review.
   748	
   749	A `DISCUSSION` turn MAY carry a proposal diff as a unified diff in its body.
   750	The proposal is advice, not a write: the worker's `pathspec` stays `[]`, no
   751	workspace lease or baseline is involved, and the lead applies it at the bench
   752	and owns verification. The applying session MUST keep a durable run report or
   753	equivalent change record containing the thread id, the proposal diff or its
   754	SHA-256, the `BASE_HEAD` revision anchor, the proposer, changes the lead made
   755	while applying it, and the verification performed. A commit-message citation
   756	supplements but never substitutes for that durable record.
   757	
   758	Proposal diffs are bounded in aggregate per objective, not per turn, to about
   759	three files and 200 changed lines. Splitting a larger implementation across
   760	nominal discussion turns is prohibited. Regardless of size, generated
   761	artifacts, dependency or lock files, migrations, renames, broad mechanical
   762	rewrites, and security- or concurrency-sensitive implementation MUST route to
   763	a leased write session. The governing test is whether the lead can fully
   764	understand, apply, and verify the proposal at the bench without effectively
   765	rubber-stamping delegated implementation.
   766	
   767	## 9. Known limitations
   768	
   769	- Lost blocking calls: Claude records `pending` before MCP invocation, but if
   770	  the call is lost before return, its Codex thread id may be unrecoverable.
   771	  Record `lost_before_return`; do not guess by timestamp.
   772	- Correlated reviewers: Sol and Fable are not statistically independent
   773	  evidence sources. Shared training, shared repository context, and shared
   774	  prompt framing can correlate errors.
   775	- Transient-write blindness: Final-state scope checks cannot detect files
   776	  modified and restored during the invocation.
   777	- Human lease non-compliance: A human or ungoverned process may edit without
   778	  acquiring a lease, defeating cooperative attribution.
   779	- Ignored and external writes: Git-based manifests do not comprehensively
   780	  observe ignored files, external paths, or side effects in external systems.
   781	- Convention versus enforcement: Prompt and envelope rules are mechanically
   782	  validated only where a helper or adapter performs validation.
   783	- Installed MCP ceiling: The project does not control `codex mcp-server`
   784	  internals, so adapter-level persistence of a not-yet-returned thread id is
   785	  unavailable.
   786	
   787	## 10. Implementation and consumption pointers
   788	
   789	### Clause-by-clause consumption inventory
   790	
   791	This inventory is the deduplication boundary. A `pointer` consumer names the
   792	canonical home but does not restate its procedure. An `enforcement` consumer
   793	keeps the applicable boundary text locally because prompt text is part of the
   794	guard. Configuration and invocation identify how to enter the bridge; they do
   795	not become alternate wire contracts.
   796	
   797	| Clause | Canonical home | Consumer treatment |
   798	|---|---|---|
   799	| Effort selection | `.claude/skills/codex/SKILL.md` §Effort selection | `CLAUDE.md`, the Claude agent, and the `/codex` command point to the skill; they do not repeat triggers. |
   800	| Claude-to-Sol operating sequence and config override shape | `.claude/skills/codex/SKILL.md` §Primary MCP path | The agent and command invoke the skill; `CLAUDE.md` supplies clean-clone discovery only. |
   801	| Full and discussion prompt headers | Contract §1 | Pointer only outside the contract; exhaustive scope remains an explicit enforcement boundary. |
   802	| MCP and audited-CLI return envelopes | Contract §2 | Pointer only outside the contract; failure-is-not-success remains an explicit enforcement boundary. |
   803	| Scope and ruling early returns | Contract §3 | Pointer only outside the contract; `AGENTS.md` retains receiver stop/ask rules. |
   804	| MCP-versus-CLI routing | Contract §4 | The operating skill performs the selection by reference to §4. |
   805	| Thread reuse, independence, and peer-channel continuity | Contract §§5 and 8 | Pointer only outside the contract; callers retain only the invocation fact that a returned thread can be continued. |
   806	| Leases, wrappers, baselines, and scope checks | Contract §§6-7 | Pointer only outside the contract; invocation docs may name the wrapper command but do not restate state transitions. |
   807	| Reverse-consult request, adapter, and status rules | Contract §8 | `CLAUDE.md` and the reverse skill point here; the reverse skill remains a receiver boundary outside WO-020 by lead ruling. |
   808	| Proposal-diff eligibility, ceiling, and provenance | Contract §8 | Pointer only outside the contract. |
   809	| Exhaustive write scope | Contract §§1, 3, and 7 | Explicit canonical enforcement snippet at every WO-020 in-scope entry surface; `AGENTS.md` keeps its fuller receiver rules. |
   810	| Quiet-machine exclusion | Repository machine-state policy plus contract safety boundary | Explicit canonical enforcement snippet at every WO-020 in-scope entry surface. |
   811	| Sandbox and approval bypass prohibition | Repository safety policy | Explicit canonical enforcement snippet at every WO-020 in-scope entry surface. |
   812	| One-hop prohibition | Contract §8 plus adapter boundary | Explicit canonical enforcement snippet at every WO-020 in-scope entry surface. |
   813	| Envelope failure is not success | Contract §2 | Explicit canonical enforcement snippet at every WO-020 in-scope entry surface. |
   814	
   815	Surface disposition is therefore:
   816	
   817	| Surface | Invocation/configuration retained | Normative policy form |
   818	|---|---|---|
   819	| `CLAUDE.md` | Clean-clone MCP and audited-CLI discovery | Contract/skill pointers plus canonical enforcement snippets |
   820	| `AGENTS.md` | Receiver authority and repository intake | Contract/skill pointers plus canonical enforcement snippets and fuller receiver rules |
   821	| `.claude/agents/codex.md` | Agent role and handoff | Contract/skill pointers plus canonical enforcement snippets |
   822	| `.claude/commands/codex.md` | Slash-command dispatch | Contract/skill pointers plus canonical enforcement snippets |
   823	| `.claude/skills/codex/SKILL.md` | Effort policy and operating sequence | Operating home; wire details remain contract pointers; canonical enforcement snippets stay local |
   824	| `.agents/skills/claude-consult/SKILL.md` | Reverse-consult invocation | Receiver boundary pointing to contract §8; previously excluded from WO-020 edits by lead ruling, then amended by T3-AMEND-01 |
   825	
   826	### Canonical enforcement snippets
   827	
   828	The following manifest defines the snippets before any byte-identity check is
   829	applied. Each listed consumer MUST contain each snippet exactly once as plain
   830	UTF-8 prose. Changes begin here, then propagate atomically to every listed
   831	consumer. Explanatory policy must not be added around these snippets as a new
   832	normative home.

class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. Anything user-facing (push/merge/publish) follows the user&#39;s standing instructions.</p> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Date</th> <th>Topic</th> <th>Outcome</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>C-001</td> <td>2026-07-06</td> <td>Adopt review/counterreview between Claude and Codex (2H precedent)</td> <td>adopted; PRs #41-#58 are merged; current main&#39;s canonical suite is 1,220 OK (<code>skipped=10</code>) and the corpus gate is 6/6. PR #59 remains open with a 1,224-test green worktree replay (<code>skipped=12</code>), and <code>impl/doc008-kernel</code> is pushed awaiting PR. These open follow-ups do not reopen the card. Every Window-A software gate and P0-003 are satisfied; quiet-machine execution with Ed remains deliberately separate from landed-software status. NVIDIA/Orin protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL pending live evidence.</p> <p>Layer structure: Sol implementation sessions (xhigh; 2 ultra for the p2041-vetted composition and the P2-037 engine) → review lenses (contract + semantics per stream) → severity-tiered refuters (2 per blocker) → independent post-hoc audits (P2-037) → delta re-audits after fix rounds → lead gates (live runs, arithmetic checks, final heads, CI) → cross-stream integration tree before each merge.</p> <p>Unique catches per layer (D-061 evaluation record):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Sol merge review:</strong> caught the lead&#39;s own merge-resolution error — the branch&#39;s updated P2-005 row silently lost by a whole-file <code>--theirs</code> checkout during the #49 conflict resolution; repaired as a proper 3-way merge (<code>13f6c9e</code>). Only layer to catch it.</li> <li><strong>Refuter tier:</strong> narrowed 2 blockers via CONTRADICTORY paired verdicts — P2-041 B1 (contract refuter confirmed, reachability refuter refuted the broad form → landed as the narrowed shared fail-closed cooldown verifier, <code>f2c4701</code>) and P2-037 F1 (design vs repro refuters split the same way → F1 narrowed before the fix round). The disagreement itself was the signal; neither single refuter would have produced the narrowed form.</li> <li><strong>Delta re-audits:</strong> 2 fresh blockers in paths newly reachable only after the fix round (P2-037 delta re-audit: blocker=2/should-fix=3), plus the recurring symlink pattern — cooldown provenance <code>Path.resolve</code> unwrapped against symlink loop/OSError, wrapped fail-closed with a cross-version regression test (<code>5f1f161</code>). Neither finding existed in the pre-fix tree; the re-audit layer is what sees post-fix reachability.</li> <li><strong>Lead gates:</strong> P2-044 F1 cadence arithmetic verified directly (all-intervals population; binding Qwen-r3 values asserted exactly: median 0.1199250625, ratio 1.0581313969 — <code>dc1ab95</code>); live NV-5 localhost gate 3/3 OK closing the open lead gate on #49 (<code>10e0ad2</code>); live doctor run. All three are lead-live-only — no static layer could produce them.</li> <li><strong>Integration tree:</strong> 38 pre-merge cross-stream test failures caught at the combined head, dominated by REPRO-002&#39;s fail-closed environment/inventory checks meeting post-cut fields from sibling streams. Zero of these were visible in any single stream&#39;s green suite.</li> <li><strong>Enforcement layer (scope backstop, live):</strong> 2 bytecode false-positive firings tuned same-day; NEEDS_SCOPE compliant stops ×3 (p2037 fix round, doc008 ×2) — each returning the correct paths where the lead had guessed wrong.</li> </ul> <p>Scope enforcement fired in production: two sessions (p2043-impl, p2044-fixround) exited SCOPE_VIOLATION with work preserved in evidence bundles, not landed; one wrapper crash (lead in-place edit of the installed runner mid-run) was recovered via a lead-authored recovery row rather than a mutated record — both behaviors are now ratified in D-064.</p> <p>Rough spend (from the two manifests + local usage accounting; estimates, not billing truth): 2 ultra sessions ≈ 100M tokens (p2041-vetted composition, P2-037 engine); 53 recorded xhigh invocations (14 v2-manifest + 37 v3-event-stream + 2 transition-era rows) — local 24h accounting shows 50 xhigh sessions ≈ 171M tokens; 2 high (both FAILED rc=1 resume attempts, work recovered in later sessions) ≈ 40M. Fable lead: ~1.8M generation / ~14.8M billed-ish / ~570M cache reads. Two v3 sessions (doc008-r3, pr59-review) still RUNNING at the manifest snapshot.</p> <p>Spend snapshot addendum (2026-07-11 ~20:00Z, <code>codex-usage</code> 24h window, arc-close truth for the table above; estimates, not billing): 59 Sol sessions / 330.6M tokens / ~17.5h session time — xhigh 55 ≈ 190.4M, ultra 2 ≈ 100.3M, high 2 ≈ 40.0M (both FAILED). Composition (measured from raw session records): ~97.4% of Sol input is cached, output ≈ 0.37% of volume. API-list-price equivalent (GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30, cached $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1): Sol ≈ $240, Fable ≈ $810 — combined ≈ $1,050 for the recorded arc; upper bound ≈ $2,300 counting all local Codex sessions (includes non-manifest sessions; resume rows may double-count). Note the inversion: Sol is ~180x the token volume but Fable is ~3.4x the cost — cache reads dominate the lead&#39;s footprint. Snapshot convention now standing in the council skill §Recording + instrumentation.</p> <p>Process artifacts adopted this arc (ratified as/alongside D-064):</p> <ul> <li><strong>claude-codex-report/v1</strong> — canonical machine-parsed session report envelope; run_finished rows record parse validity, finding counts, verification counts, scope flags.</li> <li><strong>codex-run-v3</strong> — append-only event-stream manifest (run_started/run_finished/run_consumed), retry-with-resume, lead-authored recovery rows on wrapper failure.</li> <li><strong>WRITE_SCOPE backstop</strong> — post-run diff vs declared scope; exit 77 + evidence bundle on violation; NEEDS_SCOPE prospective-only expansion (AGENTS.md precedence section, <code>9ca89cc</code>).</li> <li><strong>NEEDS_RULING</strong> — any blocking non-delegable decision early-returns a structured question instead of a guess (<code>31b3f5e</code>); usage guard + usage-pressure mode active.</li> <li><strong>Design-consult-by-default</strong> — Ed-prompted global-rule amendment; exercised for P2-044 (HAC/ESS design consult, <code>827df12</code>) before implementation.</li> </ul> <p>Dissents overridden: none unresolved. The P2-041 RED tranche (ultra round deleting P2-038/P2-040 wholesale) was not landed or argued — it was triaged per-file and rebuilt from main under three Ed-approved C rulings (<code>96e10bd</code>, <code>750f7d0</code>).</p> <p>Calibration note (model-version scoping, per C-027): the refuter contradictory-verdict pattern produced correct narrowings twice; the two scope violations and one thin-output ultra warning are the arc&#39;s recorded 5.6-sol failure modes. Sealed A/B remains the gate before any delegation-boundary change.</p> <h2 id="c-031-d-078-p0-instrument-repair-close-out-session-round-8-landing-round-9-final-confirmation-sign-off-2026-07-22">C-031: D-078 P0 instrument-repair close-out session — round-8 landing, round-9 final confirmation, sign-off (2026-07-22)</h2> <p>Shape: lead resumed the paused arc cold from scratchpad pointers; collected the checkpointed Sol round-8 fix wave; §C-028 delta re-audit (3 fresh read-only Sol lenses over a shared packet → 8 xhigh refuter verdicts, blockers 2 refuters with distinct lenses); Sol xhigh round-8b fix wave under enforced WRITE_SCOPE (one NEEDS_SCOPE early-return, lead-ruled, fixture fix applied at the bench); bounded 8b delta re-audit; lead full-suite gates (2081 → 2088 passed, 0 failures); commit <code>040ca3a</code>; round-9 FINAL confirmation (Sol xhigh review genre); CR9-1 adjudicated as registered limitation L1 per the loop-termination doctrine; close-out <code>debc6d2</code>; PR #79 opened for Ed-named merge.</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li>Sol review lenses: A1 (v3 claim-eligibility contract divergence), B1 (ClockStamp physical-sanity gap → understated B_fiducial ~3 µs), C1/C2 (boundary float, OverflowError escape), C3/C4 (test-wiring gaps).</li> <li>Sol xhigh refuters: killed A2/B2 outright (both plausible, both wrong — A2&#39;s &quot;legacy records break&quot; was self-invalid synthetic-only; B2&#39;s stale-vs-invalid relabel would have broken a ratified distinction); narrowed C1 to a registered nit; split on A1 (contract-confirmed, reachability-refuted) — lead synthesis: pre-existing defense-in-depth hardening, not a round-8 regression.</li> <li>Round-9 confirmation: CR9-1 (floor artifacts self-attesting) — the only finding of the round, repro-backed, lead-reproduced at the bench.</li> <li>Lead unique: false-attribution triage of the 8b audit&#39;s two &quot;blockers&quot; (both were the lead&#39;s own authorized bench edits); the L1 adjudication.</li> </ul> <p>Failure modes recorded: (1) upstream cyber-content filter killed 3/8 refuters mid-run on adversarial phrasing (&quot;malformed/tamper/escape&quot;) — rephrasing as data-quality QA of our own instrument recovered all three (route: keep refuter briefs mechanism-neutral); (2) lead bench-edited the worktree while an enforced-scope Sol session ran in it → false SCOPE_VIOLATION attribution + resume-registry loss (rule: no lead edits in a tree with a live enforced-scope session); (3) the known xhigh review-genre null-final-message mode recurred on round 9; the documented bridge-resume recovery worked first try.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: the 8b delta auditor&#39;s should-fix (OverflowError normalization also reaching v1 replay error behavior) was overridden by lead ruling — frozen-replay doctrine protects computed semantics of parsable artifacts, not crash reproduction on impossible inputs; the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Yield: the peer&#39;s structural correction (anomaly screen must not erase drift from the claim budget) was adopted — the second recorded case of invited peer design judgment beating the lead&#39;s ruling. The debate also surfaced one gap neither model had specced (drift-bound freshness horizon — prompted by Ed&#39;s own risk question) and one open science question (a7-vs-a5 prefill floor scatter, 3x). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise: Project Status — Full Reference</h1> <p><strong><a href="project_status.html">← Back to project status summary</a></strong></p> <p>This page continues the project-status document with its architecture, planning, and historical reference material.</p> <h2 id="summary">Summary</h2> <p>JouleWise combines a reusable, typed measurement harness with a benchmark defined by its frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator. It measures the energy of LLM inference across heterogeneous local hardware. The name nods to JouleSort and Splitwise: energy measurement is the spine of the system; disaggregated (&quot;split&quot;) inference - running prefill and decode on different machines with the KV cache transferred between them - is the validating research study, not the whole architecture.</p> <p>The capstone now has two explicit claim tracks. The guaranteed capstone is auditable local LLM energy measurement: the harness plus the Apple-Silicon characterization it can already execute on the M3 Max. Split (disaggregated) inference remains the differentiating validating study; when Phase 3 hardware and feasibility gates land, it upgrades the capstone from local characterization to a split-energy crossover study.</p> <p>The frozen capstone headline, fallback claims, contribution ladder, and minimum-viable stop-lines are now recorded in <code>docs/contracts/capstone_scope.md</code>; that contract is the scope pointer for reader-facing wording under the claims ladder.</p> <p>The first working slice runs on a MacBook (Apple Silicon) with MLX as the runtime and <code>powermetrics</code> as the power source, producing complete, auditable run bundles. Further backends (NVIDIA + vLLM/llama.cpp, Jetson Orin, Raspberry Pi + Hailo as a feasibility finding) plug into the same adapter interfaces.</p> <p>Research questions:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Q1</strong>: Under what conditions (model size, prompt length, link speed, device pair) does splitting inference reduce total energy versus running monolithically on either device?</li> <li><strong>Q2</strong>: How sensitive is the split&#39;s energy cost to interconnect bandwidth (1GbE vs 2.5GbE vs optional 10GbE) - where is the crossover?</li> <li><strong>Q3</strong>: When splitting saves energy, what latency does it cost, and vice versa (energy-latency Pareto frontier)?</li> <li><strong>Q4</strong> (added 2026-07-07, council C-003): What fixed-vs-marginal energy model <code>E = fixed + prefill(prompt_tokens) + decode(output_tokens)</code> does each target/model/quantization follow — and can split-run energy be predicted compositionally from monolithic coefficients plus transfer measurements?</li> <li><strong>Q5</strong> (C-003/C-007): On one machine, do workload/model/quantization efficiency rankings stay stable as workload shape, model, and quantization change, or where do they flip? A cross-device ranking extension is hardware-gated.</li> <li><strong>Q6</strong> (C-003; gated on the wall meter): Does the measurement boundary (platform rails vs AC wall power) change the conclusions?</li> </ul> <p>Current question status, aliases, gates, and claim ceilings live in the canonical live index, <code>docs/research_question_registry.md</code>. The curated bank of further candidate questions and deliberately killed ones remains the historical/deliberative record in <code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>; the measurement noise floor / detection limit is treated as the methodology centerpiece rather than a numbered question.</p> <p>The capability map by claim ceiling is reflected in <code>docs/research_question_registry.md</code> (C-015), alongside the suite architecture v2 and benchmark interop direction; the guaranteed-capstone stop-line is recorded in the Phase 2 plan.</p> <p><strong>Q4 architectural stress-test agenda (D-070).</strong> Static batching, speculative decoding / native MTP, MoE versus dense execution, quantization, and reasoning-length variance are five stress tests of Q4&#39;s single fixed-plus-marginal energy thesis, not five additional theses. The harness must instrument every axis well enough to produce strict-valid L0 smoke bundles; the benchmark supplies the frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator for claim-bearing runs. Per Ed&#39;s ruling, all five axes have characterized-study commitments. Every study remains floor-gated and capped at L2; L3 is available only through Q4/AP-1&#39;s existing holdout machinery. Window A remains first, and no AXI quiet-Mac characterization starts before Window A completes. Static batching is the capstone scope; continuous batching remains a post-capstone extension.</p> <p><strong>Ranked extension-axis intake (D-075).</strong> The later six-axis evaluation did not create six more theses. It attached DSpark/DFlash break-even, proposal-work, and contamination-control riders to the speculative-decoding home; admitted an on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and one named hybrid pair; and attached cache/context, module-nonattribution, kernel, and backend provenance riders to their existing questions. All admitted units remain candidate work with earliest-phase tags, named forbidden upgrades, floor gates, and an intake ceiling at or below L2. Unverified runtime, pair, adapter, and device-fit questions remain explicitly NEEDS-WEB, and Ed retains commitment and ordering authority under D-070.</p> <h2 id="status-at-a-glance">Status At A Glance</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Phase</th> <th>Scope</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>1. Approval, feasibility, measurement design</td> <td>contracts, methodology, hardware feasibility evidence</td> <td><strong>in progress</strong> — the Phase 1 exit checklist owns exact completion and external gates</td> </tr> <tr> <td>2. Harness, Mac vertical slice, homogeneous baselines</td> <td>runnable harness, first real measurements, per-target baselines</td> <td><strong>in progress</strong> — Mac vertical slice and analysis software are implemented; remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL; the state kernel and quiet-machine rules own execution eligibility</td> </tr> <tr> <td>3. Disaggregation, KV replay, interconnect sweep</td> <td>split-energy decomposition, crossover dataset</td> <td>planned (feasibility-first)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>4. Characterization and analysis</td> <td>statistics, figures, claims audit</td> <td>planned</td> </tr> <tr> <td>5. Presentation and submission</td> <td>report, colloquium, reproducible release</td> <td>planned</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="capstone-artifact-map">Capstone Artifact Map</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>chapter/report-component</th> <th>owning doc or deliverable</th> <th>status</th> <th>missing evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>Background / related work</td> <td>Phase 4 Stage 4.6, <code>docs/phase_4/related_work_draft.md</code></td> <td>drafted (11 verified sources)</td> <td>background-chapter assembly and the Phase 4 exit pass</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Measurement methodology</td> <td><code>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md</code></td> <td>complete</td> <td>Phase 4 ratification may amend statistical details against observed variance</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Harness / instrument</td> <td><code>joulewise/</code></td> <td>complete; pre-campaign software review cleared; C-028 closed</td> <td>live execution eligibility comes from the state kernel; quiet-machine work also requires Ed and the clean hardware lane</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Apple-Silicon characterization / homogeneous baselines</td> <td>Phase 2 Slice 2M, <code>docs/phase_2/baseline_results.md</code></td> <td>Window A open; production shakedown closed and first floors published; quiet-Mac execution remains</td> <td>P2-037 claim adjudication and the live state kernel govern the next baseline step; needs Ed + quiet Mac</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Split-inference study</td> <td>Phase 3</td> <td>planned</td> <td>needs KV-feasibility spikes plus a real pairing, or the synthetic-transfer + analytical-composition floor</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Results / limitations + claims audit</td> <td>Phase 4 Stages 4.3-4.5</td> <td>analysis path implemented; Window-A calibration data exist</td> <td>the floor corpus is strict-valid but claim-evidence-flagged; P2-037 adjudication must preserve the published caveats before any claim promotion</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Complete so far (all verifiable in the repository):</p> <ul> <li>A runnable harness: from a typed config, one command (<code>python3 -m joulewise run ...</code>) produces a complete, schema-valid, auditable run bundle and reduces it to energy/latency summary metrics - proven first on deterministic mock adapters (controller, bundle contract, and reducer math verified without hardware) and now running live on the Mac target. Bundle writer, controller lifecycle, reducer, static-HTML report generator, and CLI verbs <code>run</code> / <code>validate-bundle</code> / <code>reduce</code> (post-hoc re-derivation of summary metrics from the recorded power trace and events) / <code>report</code>. Strict validation now also re-derives powermetrics traces from raw plist evidence, checks legacy additive-summary compatibility, and requires shape-valid provenance on new-era bundles. All bundle consumers read through one shared, tested read layer, which sharply reduces the risk of displayed numbers diverging from reported ones.</li> <li>Typed config and output schemas with validation, JSON-Schema export, and a CLI, plus the canonical suite run in CI on every push, including a mock end-to-end run and bundle validation. The command and CI output own the current result; reader docs do not copy its volatile count. Emitted configs round-trip their own published schema, and config hashes (run identity) are pinned by test.</li> <li>Adapter interface contracts (runtime / telemetry / transport), the run bundle artifact contract, and the measurement methodology (idle subtraction, measurement boundaries, clock synchronization, statistical protocol - highlights below).</li> <li>Evidence-shaped plans for every phase, a design-decision log whose index is mechanically checked against its decision bodies (with D-060 ratified by Ed); the log itself is the structural authority, and most entries record the alternatives considered), a risk register with an explicit descope ladder, and example configs for the Mac and mock targets.</li> <li>The complete Mac vertical slice: the MLX runtime adapter (2G), the <code>powermetrics</code> telemetry adapter (2H, parser pinned to a captured privileged sample, raw plists preserved verbatim in every bundle), and the flagship integration (2I) — three strict-valid repetition bundles of real energy measurements on the M3 Max. <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per 512-token request. <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~44.4 J per request and ~79-90 mJ per generated output token. TTFT was ~94 ms at 257 tokens/s; these are legacy L1 preliminary observations for provisional model Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit, mirrored locally. The separately recorded <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~304.0 J per 512-token request; <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~298.7 J per request and ~583 mJ per generated output token. These historical values are basis labels on the recorded results, not a new reduction.</li> <li>The P2-042 frozen analysis manifest, P2-041 campaign verdict split, P2-037 contrast/claim engine, P2-040 reducer/gate remainder, P2-038 production-uncertainty software path, and NV-GATE-2 code-now hardening. Reducer dispatch is frozen across the legacy and 0.3.x arms and current through 0.4.2. None of this promotes fixture-first NVIDIA evidence to live validation.</li> <li>The report&#39;s related-work survey draft (11 sources with verified citations and an honest positioning audit) and an off-machine iCloud Drive backup whose fresh restored bundles passed strict validation and were byte-identical to their sources.</li> </ul> <p>Live remote-hardware validation has not started: NVIDIA/vLLM and Jetson Orin promotion (2K/2L) remain gated on device access. The fixture-first implementation and NV-GATE-2 software hardening are landed, but all remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL until live hardware contact; a P1-006 evidence checklist exists there. Code-level specs are in <code>docs/phase_2/hardware_slice_implementation_guide.md</code>. The mock-first core landed first by design, so measurement code is never debugging the measurement harness and a live hardware integration at the same time.</p> <p>Waiting on external input (most of it does not block current software work; P0-003&#39;s backup gate is satisfied, and the grading rubric/calendar (P1-008) carries the provisional-contract fallback under ratified D-060):</p> <ol> <li>NVIDIA / Jetson Orin device access evidence — the one hard gate left, for the remote-target slices 2K/2L. (The <code>nvidia_3050</code> in the architecture table is the owned always-available NVIDIA target; the 3080 Ti is a separate, borrowed card used only for Phase 3&#39;s interconnect sweep.)</li> <li>Calendar anchors: colloquium date, report deadline, and the 3080 Ti borrow window, to derive phase target dates.</li> <li>Advisor scope confirmation (see the sanity-check note above) — finalizes model selection; deliberately deprioritized while all work remains harness-shaped and valuable under any scope.</li> </ol> <p>Closed since the last revision: the comprehensive audit; AXI-SA&#39;s burst-decode contract; SITE-02 D1/D2; the SPLIT-AP Part I pre-registration freeze; AXI-SB&#39;s <code>supported</code> static-batch verdict with its Mac C5-2.2 leg; P2-038&#39;s production-shaped live gate; and AXI-SC&#39;s <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> pinned- runtime verdict. The later DSpark/DFlash MLX feasibility smokes and D-075 extension-axis intake are recorded without promoting an energy claim, and the nine-bundle OLMoE/Qwen follow-on remains explicitly exploratory. Window A&#39;s software gates are satisfied, its first floor corpus is published, and the window remains open. The floors are calibration thresholds rather than claim promotion: P2-037 adjudication remains pending because strict-valid collection and claim readiness are separate gates; execution timing is governed by the live work-selection state in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>&#39;s generated state-kernel region and still requires Ed plus a quiet Mac.</p> <h2 id="architecture">Architecture</h2> <pre><code class="language-text">typed config

review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. Zero of these were visible in any single stream&#39;s green suite.</li> <li><strong>Enforcement layer (scope backstop, live):</strong> 2 bytecode false-positive firings tuned same-day; NEEDS_SCOPE compliant stops ×3 (p2037 fix round, doc008 ×2) — each returning the correct paths where the lead had guessed wrong.</li> </ul> <p>Scope enforcement fired in production: two sessions (p2043-impl, p2044-fixround) exited SCOPE_VIOLATION with work preserved in evidence bundles, not landed; one wrapper crash (lead in-place edit of the installed runner mid-run) was recovered via a lead-authored recovery row rather than a mutated record — both behaviors are now ratified in D-064.</p> <p>Rough spend (from the two manifests + local usage accounting; estimates, not billing truth): 2 ultra sessions ≈ 100M tokens (p2041-vetted composition, P2-037 engine); 53 recorded xhigh invocations (14 v2-manifest + 37 v3-event-stream + 2 transition-era rows) — local 24h accounting shows 50 xhigh sessions ≈ 171M tokens; 2 high (both FAILED rc=1 resume attempts, work recovered in later sessions) ≈ 40M. Fable lead: ~1.8M generation / ~14.8M billed-ish / ~570M cache reads. Two v3 sessions (doc008-r3, pr59-review) still RUNNING at the manifest snapshot.</p> <p>Spend snapshot addendum (2026-07-11 ~20:00Z, <code>codex-usage</code> 24h window, arc-close truth for the table above; estimates, not billing): 59 Sol sessions / 330.6M tokens / ~17.5h session time — xhigh 55 ≈ 190.4M, ultra 2 ≈ 100.3M, high 2 ≈ 40.0M (both FAILED). Composition (measured from raw session records): ~97.4% of Sol input is cached, output ≈ 0.37% of volume. API-list-price equivalent (GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30, cached $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1): Sol ≈ $240, Fable ≈ $810 — combined ≈ $1,050 for the recorded arc; upper bound ≈ $2,300 counting all local Codex sessions (includes non-manifest sessions; resume rows may double-count). Note the inversion: Sol is ~180x the token volume but Fable is ~3.4x the cost — cache reads dominate the lead&#39;s footprint. Snapshot convention now standing in the council skill §Recording + instrumentation.</p> <p>Process artifacts adopted this arc (ratified as/alongside D-064):</p> <ul> <li><strong>claude-codex-report/v1</strong> — canonical machine-parsed session report envelope; run_finished rows record parse validity, finding counts, verification counts, scope flags.</li> <li><strong>codex-run-v3</strong> — append-only event-stream manifest (run_started/run_finished/run_consumed), retry-with-resume, lead-authored recovery rows on wrapper failure.</li> <li><strong>WRITE_SCOPE backstop</strong> — post-run diff vs declared scope; exit 77 + evidence bundle on violation; NEEDS_SCOPE prospective-only expansion (AGENTS.md precedence section, <code>9ca89cc</code>).</li> <li><strong>NEEDS_RULING</strong> — any blocking non-delegable decision early-returns a structured question instead of a guess (<code>31b3f5e</code>); usage guard + usage-pressure mode active.</li> <li><strong>Design-consult-by-default</strong> — Ed-prompted global-rule amendment; exercised for P2-044 (HAC/ESS design consult, <code>827df12</code>) before implementation.</li> </ul> <p>Dissents overridden: none unresolved. The P2-041 RED tranche (ultra round deleting P2-038/P2-040 wholesale) was not landed or argued — it was triaged per-file and rebuilt from main under three Ed-approved C rulings (<code>96e10bd</code>, <code>750f7d0</code>).</p> <p>Calibration note (model-version scoping, per C-027): the refuter contradictory-verdict pattern produced correct narrowings twice; the two scope violations and one thin-output ultra warning are the arc&#39;s recorded 5.6-sol failure modes. Sealed A/B remains the gate before any delegation-boundary change.</p> <h2 id="c-031-d-078-p0-instrument-repair-close-out-session-round-8-landing-round-9-final-confirmation-sign-off-2026-07-22">C-031: D-078 P0 instrument-repair close-out session — round-8 landing, round-9 final confirmation, sign-off (2026-07-22)</h2> <p>Shape: lead resumed the paused arc cold from scratchpad pointers; collected the checkpointed Sol round-8 fix wave; §C-028 delta re-audit (3 fresh read-only Sol lenses over a shared packet → 8 xhigh refuter verdicts, blockers 2 refuters with distinct lenses); Sol xhigh round-8b fix wave under enforced WRITE_SCOPE (one NEEDS_SCOPE early-return, lead-ruled, fixture fix applied at the bench); bounded 8b delta re-audit; lead full-suite gates (2081 → 2088 passed, 0 failures); commit <code>040ca3a</code>; round-9 FINAL confirmation (Sol xhigh review genre); CR9-1 adjudicated as registered limitation L1 per the loop-termination doctrine; close-out <code>debc6d2</code>; PR #79 opened for Ed-named merge.</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li>Sol review lenses: A1 (v3 claim-eligibility contract divergence), B1 (ClockStamp physical-sanity gap → understated B_fiducial ~3 µs), C1/C2 (boundary float, OverflowError escape), C3/C4 (test-wiring gaps).</li> <li>Sol xhigh refuters: killed A2/B2 outright (both plausible, both wrong — A2&#39;s &quot;legacy records break&quot; was self-invalid synthetic-only; B2&#39;s stale-vs-invalid relabel would have broken a ratified distinction); narrowed C1 to a registered nit; split on A1 (contract-confirmed, reachability-refuted) — lead synthesis: pre-existing defense-in-depth hardening, not a round-8 regression.</li> <li>Round-9 confirmation: CR9-1 (floor artifacts self-attesting) — the only finding of the round, repro-backed, lead-reproduced at the bench.</li> <li>Lead unique: false-attribution triage of the 8b audit&#39;s two &quot;blockers&quot; (both were the lead&#39;s own authorized bench edits); the L1 adjudication.</li> </ul> <p>Failure modes recorded: (1) upstream cyber-content filter killed 3/8 refuters mid-run on adversarial phrasing (&quot;malformed/tamper/escape&quot;) — rephrasing as data-quality QA of our own instrument recovered all three (route: keep refuter briefs mechanism-neutral); (2) lead bench-edited the worktree while an enforced-scope Sol session ran in it → false SCOPE_VIOLATION attribution + resume-registry loss (rule: no lead edits in a tree with a live enforced-scope session); (3) the known xhigh review-genre null-final-message mode recurred on round 9; the documented bridge-resume recovery worked first try.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: the 8b delta auditor&#39;s should-fix (OverflowError normalization also reaching v1 replay error behavior) was overridden by lead ruling — frozen-replay doctrine protects computed semantics of parsable artifacts, not crash reproduction on impossible inputs; the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Yield: the peer&#39;s structural correction (anomaly screen must not erase drift from the claim budget) was adopted — the second recorded case of invited peer design judgment beating the lead&#39;s ruling. The debate also surfaced one gap neither model had specced (drift-bound freshness horizon — prompted by Ed&#39;s own risk question) and one open science question (a7-vs-a5 prefill floor scatter, 3x). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
