class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Measurement Methodology</h1> <p>Living cross-phase contract, drafted in Phase 1. Changes require a decision-log entry when they bind later work.</p> <h2 id="measurement-principle">Measurement Principle</h2> <p>Every benchmark run must be reproducible from its raw artifacts. Summary metrics are derived outputs, not the source of truth.</p> <p>The source of truth for a run is the run bundle:</p> <ul> <li>Experiment config.</li> <li>Device and environment metadata.</li> <li>Event log with phase timestamps.</li> <li>Raw power trace.</li> <li>Raw model output.</li> <li>Reducer output.</li> <li>Runtime and telemetry logs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="run-lifecycle">Run Lifecycle</h2> <p>Before a campaign creates a run bundle, the operator runs the read-only doctor preflight described in <code>docs/contracts/doctor_preflight.md</code>. Schema-0.1 parsing continues to warn-and-ignore unknown keys for compatibility, but campaign execution fails before the first bundle when those warnings have not been explicitly acknowledged. The terminal campaign-verdict JSONL row records the exact warning set and acknowledgement; acknowledgement does not alter config bytes, collection evidence, claim readiness, or claim outcomes.</p> <p>Doctor also exposes architecture/version, configured model and tokenizer identity, requested sampler fields, inspect-only powermetrics privilege policy, thermal pressure, backup capacity, and quiet-machine warnings. These are preflight observations, not substitutes for per-bundle provenance or live measurement gates. In particular, doctor never starts powermetrics and never certifies that a machine is quiet.</p> <h3>Environment guard and per-run admission (D-077)</h3> <p>Campaigns select a strictly typed policy sidecar. <code>run_campaign.py</code> defaults to <code>configs/campaign_policies/quiet_mac_p2_production.json</code>, records the policy version and exact source-byte SHA-256 in campaign provenance and every member bundle, acquires the campaign lock, and only then performs the enforcing environment preflight before member 1. The production quiet-Mac guard requires AC power and an externally connected power source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Unknown critical probes fail closed. Load averages are recorded as preflight evidence only and never gate a member.</p> <p>Default operation is verify-only. <code>--arm-quiet-mode</code> is an explicit transient operation: the runner displays a countdown, requests <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, and repeats the complete environment probe before deciding admission. It does not write display-sleep, screensaver, or other persistent host settings. An operator override is accepted only when its JSON binds the exact failed snapshot and findings SHA-256 values and records a reason, approver, and timestamp. It is stored as an <code>override</code>, not a waiver, and universally bars all resulting members from gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</p> <p>At each governed member&#39;s idle-baseline stage, the controller captures the same critical environment evidence and verifies that the display remains asleep and the screensaver remains disengaged. Awake, engaged, or unknown state aborts immediately. The first idle baseline is admitted only when the existing powermetrics GPU-idle-quality classification records <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>. One and only one complete retry is allowed; both attempts preserve distinct raw artifacts and provenance. A persistent failure either aborts (production) or records the exploratory-only, unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> claim barrier (<code>on_fail: flag</code>). There is no skip disposition in a fixed-n campaign. A lightweight post-run display/screensaver/HID observation makes within-member transitions visible.</p> <p>The sidecar is deliberately separate from <code>BenchmarkConfig</code>. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy flag-only/non-enforcing behavior, and omission of the additive policy/admission metadata preserves legacy normalized config serialization and hashes.</p> <h3>Per-bundle source provenance</h3> <p><code>RunBundleWriter.create</code> captures the harness source state before it creates bundle artifacts or returns control to any adapter. <code>write_metadata</code> captures the end state after adapter execution. <code>metadata.git_commit</code> remains the creation-time commit for compatibility; the governed record is <code>metadata.source_provenance</code> with schema <code>joulewise.source_provenance.v1</code>.</p> <p>Each <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> snapshot records <code>git_commit</code>, <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, <code>untracked</code>, and <code>diff_sha256</code>. The three state values are independently:</p> <ul> <li><code>clean</code>: the corresponding Git probe succeeded and found no change;</li> <li><code>dirty</code>: an unstaged tracked diff, staged diff, or non-ignored untracked path was present, respectively; or</li> <li><code>unknown</code>: the corresponding probe or required file read failed. Failure is never interpreted as clean.</li> </ul> <p>The privacy-safe diff identity descriptor is <code>sha256</code> / <code>joulewise.git-diff.nul-v1</code>. The producer captures the byte output of <code>git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --binary</code>, the analogous <code>--cached</code> command, and <code>git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z</code>. For each sorted untracked path it hashes, without serializing, the NUL-safe length-framed path, file kind, mode, size, and SHA-256 of regular-file bytes or symlink-target bytes. The final identity is SHA-256 over the version plus length-framed <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, and untracked-inventory byte identities. Bundles contain only the final digest and state labels: never a diff, path, untracked file content, or secret.</p> <p><code>changed_during_run</code> is true when two fully known snapshots differ, false when they match, and null when either snapshot is not fully known. <code>claim_eligible</code> is true only when both commits and diff identities are known, all six component states are clean, and the snapshots match. <code>reason_codes</code> is the deterministic list of every start/end unknown or dirty component followed, when applicable, by <code>source_changed_during_run</code>. Bundle completion remains allowed in every state so raw evidence is not discarded.</p> <p>Dirty, unknown, changed, missing, or internally inconsistent provenance is a hard exclusion for claim-bearing use. The publication pack preflight enforces that boundary and refuses such bundles. Analysis-side admission propagation is separate from capture and field semantics and is owned by WO-004/T11.</p> <ol> <li>Validate config.</li> <li>Create run directory.</li> <li>Collect device metadata.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Warm up runtime.</li> <li>Wait the configured post-warmup settling interval (<code>sampling.warmup_seconds</code>; zero means no wait).</li> <li>Start measured telemetry.</li> <li>Run workload.</li> <li>Stop measured telemetry.</li> <li>Cleanup runtime.</li> <li>Reduce raw artifacts into summary metrics.</li> </ol> <p>The post-warmup settling interval begins only after all active <code>workload_profile.warmup_runs</code> calls and their clock-alignment captures have completed. It ends before the measured-run stage and sampling-active markers, so it is never integrated into the measured window. Controller events record the configured value on the warmup completion event and the runtime log records positive waits.</p> <h2 id="idle-subtraction">Idle Subtraction</h2> <p>Energy metrics must report both gross and idle-subtracted values when possible. The idle baseline is measured before each run and stored in the run bundle.</p> <p>Minimum idle fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle_power_w_mean</code></li> <li><code>idle_power_w_stddev</code></li> <li><code>idle_duration_s</code></li> <li><code>idle_sample_count</code></li> <li><code>telemetry_backend</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="thermal-state">Thermal State</h2> <p>Each telemetry backend should report thermal state before and after measured runs when the platform exposes it.</p> <p>Minimum thermal fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>temperature_c</code></li> <li><code>thermal_pressure</code> or platform equivalent, when available.</li> <li><code>fan_state</code> or cooling mode, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="uncertainty">Uncertainty</h2> <p>Phase 1 defines uncertainty fields; Phase 2 implements reducer behavior. Repeated runs should report:</p> <ul> <li>Number of repetitions.</li> <li>Mean.</li> <li>Standard deviation.</li> <li>Confidence interval method.</li> <li>Confidence interval bounds.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-quality-fields">Measurement Quality Fields</h2> <p>Each run summary should include:</p> <ul> <li>Sampling rate requested.</li> <li>Sampling rate observed.</li> <li>Dropped or malformed samples.</li> <li>Idle variance.</li> <li>Thermal drift.</li> <li>Telemetry source.</li> <li>Local runtime cleanup result (<code>runtime_cleanup_ok</code>: true/false/null). Cleanup occurs after the measured window, so failure is a quality concern for the following repetition and does not retroactively change current-run status or energy.</li> <li>Wall-meter comparison delta, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="phase-labels">Phase Labels</h2> <p>The event log should use stable phase names:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle</code></li> <li><code>warmup</code></li> <li><code>prefill</code></li> <li><code>decode</code></li> <li><code>serialize</code></li> <li><code>transfer</code></li> <li><code>deserialize</code></li> <li><code>cleanup</code></li> <li><code>failure</code></li> </ul> <p><code>deserialize</code> (cache load on the decode node) was added 2026-06-09 alongside the split-run accounting definitions (see <code>docs/phase_3/phase_3_plan.md</code>); phase labels are strings in the schema, so the addition is non-breaking. Split-stage accounting, pinned so reducers and prose agree: serialize = cache-persist window on the prefill node; transfer = byte-movement window; deserialize = cache-load window on the decode node; decode = first-token to last-token. Cache load is not decode energy.</p> <h2 id="hardware-classification">Hardware Classification</h2> <p>Every target should end Phase 1 in one state:</p> <ul> <li><code>supported</code>: known viable and ready for Phase 2 implementation.</li> <li><code>pending</code>: expected viable but not fully checked.</li> <li><code>unsupported</code>: not viable for a documented technical reason.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-boundaries">Measurement Boundaries</h2> <p>&quot;Power&quot; means a different physical boundary on each telemetry backend. Cross-target absolute comparisons must state the boundary difference; the final report&#39;s limitations section inherits this table. Decision D-018 defines the rail policy (per-rail trace rows plus a per-backend rail manifest naming the canonical sum).</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Backend</th> <th>Boundary</th> <th>Included</th> <th>Excluded</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>powermetrics</td> <td>Apple SoC subsystems</td> <td>CPU + GPU + ANE package power</td> <td>display, storage, memory at wall, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>nvidia_smi</td> <td>GPU board</td> <td>board power as reported by driver</td> <td>host CPU, DRAM, motherboard, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>jetson_rails</td> <td>module input (VDD_IN preferred; actual rail recorded)</td> <td>module power</td> <td>carrier-board peripherals (rail-dependent), PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>wall_meter</td> <td>full system AC</td> <td>everything incl. PSU losses</td> <td>nothing</td> </tr> <tr> <td>mock</td> <td>synthetic</td> <td>n/a</td> <td>n/a</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Rules:</p> <ul> <li>Within-target comparisons (the same backend) are always boundary-consistent and are the primary claim type.</li> <li>Cross-target comparisons are reported with boundaries named; where the wall meter exists, the wall-vs-platform delta is recorded per target and used to contextualize the gap.</li> <li>Each telemetry adapter declares its rail manifest in <code>device_metadata</code>; the reducer sums exactly the manifest rails to produce <code>power_w</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="clock-synchronization-and-multi-node-alignment">Clock Synchronization And Multi-Node Alignment</h2> <p>Policy per decision D-003:</p> <ul> <li>Canonical <code>timestamp_s</code> everywhere is epoch UTC from <code>time.time()</code> via the injected clock; no other time base appears in artifacts.</li> <li>Each process records its monotonic-vs-wall offset at start in metadata (detects wall-clock steps mid-run).</li> <li>Each node records NTP sync state in metadata when determinable.</li> <li>For multi-node runs, the controller bounds per-node clock offset with marker events: timestamp a no-op command on the remote node immediately before and after each remote stage; half the round trip bounds the offset. The bound is recorded in composite-bundle metadata.</li> <li>Reducers must flag (in measurement quality) any cross-node interval shorter than the recorded offset bound; such intervals are not used for energy attribution claims.</li> <li>Required precision: at 1-10 Hz power sampling, tens of milliseconds - comfortably within LAN NTP plus the marker bound.</li> </ul> <h2 id="controller-co-residency-controller-as-dut">Controller Co-Residency (Controller-As-DUT)</h2> <p>On Mac-local runs the controller process runs on the measured machine. Mitigation per decision D-013:</p> <ul> <li>The idle baseline is measured with the controller resident and quiescent, so the controller&#39;s floor load is included in what idle subtraction removes.</li> <li>During the measured window the controller only blocks on the runtime: no logging, no polling, no file writes; log records buffer in memory and flush after sampling stops.</li> <li>Residual risk is recorded, not hidden: OS background activity affects idle and measured windows alike; the upgrade path (remote-controlled Mac runs once the SSH transport exists) is queued as a validation comparison.</li> </ul> <h2 id="repetition-ordering-and-thermal-equilibrium">Repetition, Ordering, And Thermal Equilibrium</h2> <p>Per decisions D-005 and D-014:</p> <ul> <li>Each repetition is an independent run bundle; an experiment manifest groups members and records the executed order.</li> <li>Between live repetitions, cooldown v2 holds until the retained evidence has both a complete 30-second wall-clock span and at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code> of captured coverage (<code>coverage_fraction = 0.8</code> by default), and its duration-weighted idle-power mean satisfies the one-sided rule <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code> (10% by the production policy), while thermal pressure is Nominal. A below-reference mean therefore counts as recovery. An optional calibrated absolute ceiling is an additional upper cap and never an OR escape. The wait has a 5-minute cap; the cap is evaluated before release on every iteration, so recovery criteria first met at or after the deadline remain a <code>cap_hit</code> (with the late criteria recorded in the trace) and are recorded in the following repetition&#39;s measurement quality.</li> <li>The preceding baseline is eligible as a cooldown reference only when <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>, all critical environment probes passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. An ineligible or unknown reference falls back to one frozen clean anchor: the NEG-8 reference start when present, otherwise the first admission-passing baseline. The anchor&#39;s source and hashes are recorded and it is never updated from later outcomes. With neither an eligible reference nor an anchor the gate fails closed. The following member records policy version, eligibility decision, anchor provenance, thresholds (including <code>coverage_fraction</code>), wall-clock span, required and observed coverage, thermal result, and the exact release criterion under <code>preceding_campaign_cooldown</code>. Historical recovered rows retain their recorded meaning and are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>Conditions are interleaved round-robin where model-reload cost permits; where blocks are operationally forced, the order is recorded so drift correlation can be audited (Phase 4 Stage 4.5 does this audit).</li> </ul> <h2 id="statistical-protocol">Statistical Protocol</h2> <p>Per decision D-014 (draft to be ratified against observed variance at Phase 4 Stage 4.0), amended 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3; amendments ratified by D-053):</p> <ul> <li>Repetitions: n &gt;= 5 for headline comparisons; n &gt;= 3 minimum elsewhere; the n is recorded per experiment.</li> <li>Intervals: report mean, sample standard deviation, and 95% confidence interval via Student t; Phase 4 runs a bootstrap sensitivity comparison and reports both where they materially disagree.</li> <li>Outliers: flagged by modified z-score on MAD &gt; 3.5; never silently dropped; reported with-and-without only when a physical cause is identified and documented; otherwise kept in headline numbers. Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): at n &lt;= 10, reports also run a leave-one-out influence check on every claim-bearing contrast. The report lists the full-data estimate/CI/verdict and each leave-one-out estimate/CI/verdict. An omitted point is influential if it changes the sign, floor status, adjusted rejection/equivalence verdict, or moves the estimate by more than 0.25 x the active threshold: MDE for rank/MDE-gated claims, otherwise the floor gate. Influential points are reported as sensitivity evidence, not silently removed.</li> <li>Figures always show raw points alongside aggregates.</li> <li>Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): differences are claimed from the confidence interval of the paired/block difference, or from the named model contrast, not by visual separation of marginal intervals. Where execution order was randomized, the analysis includes a permutation/randomization check for the same contrast following the actual randomization scheme, permuting labels only within exchangeable blocks/strata. The minimum for this check is 6 exchangeable blocks; below that count, report the check as not run and rely on the contrast CI with the caveat that randomization-inference sensitivity was underpowered. A paired contrast is preferred when it matches the design; mixed or hierarchical models are reserved for real dependence structures that a paired/block contrast cannot represent. Floor-gated outcomes use a three-way rule: below-floor contrasts are <code>not resolvable</code>; above-floor contrasts whose CI does not support direction are <code>unresolved</code> with no directional claim; equivalence or &quot;no difference&quot; language requires a predeclared equivalence gate whose margin exceeds the floor and whose contrast CI lies entirely within that margin.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

class="source-file">docs/<wbr>council_log.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. (both were the lead&#39;s own authorized bench edits); the L1 adjudication.</li> </ul> <p>Failure modes recorded: (1) upstream cyber-content filter killed 3/8 refuters mid-run on adversarial phrasing (&quot;malformed/tamper/escape&quot;) — rephrasing as data-quality QA of our own instrument recovered all three (route: keep refuter briefs mechanism-neutral); (2) lead bench-edited the worktree while an enforced-scope Sol session ran in it → false SCOPE_VIOLATION attribution + resume-registry loss (rule: no lead edits in a tree with a live enforced-scope session); (3) the known xhigh review-genre null-final-message mode recurred on round 9; the documented bridge-resume recovery worked first try.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: the 8b delta auditor&#39;s should-fix (OverflowError normalization also reaching v1 replay error behavior) was overridden by lead ruling — frozen-replay doctrine protects computed semantics of parsable artifacts, not crash reproduction on impossible inputs; the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Yield: the peer&#39;s structural correction (anomaly screen must not erase drift from the claim budget) was adopted — the second recorded case of invited peer design judgment beating the lead&#39;s ruling. The debate also surfaced one gap neither model had specced (drift-bound freshness horizon — prompted by Ed&#39;s own risk question) and one open science question (a7-vs-a5 prefill floor scatter, 3x). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise: Project Status — Full Reference</h1> <p><strong><a href="project_status.html">← Back to project status summary</a></strong></p> <p>This page continues the project-status document with its architecture, planning, and historical reference material.</p> <h2 id="summary">Summary</h2> <p>JouleWise combines a reusable, typed measurement harness with a benchmark defined by its frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator. It measures the energy of LLM inference across heterogeneous local hardware. The name nods to JouleSort and Splitwise: energy measurement is the spine of the system; disaggregated (&quot;split&quot;) inference - running prefill and decode on different machines with the KV cache transferred between them - is the validating research study, not the whole architecture.</p> <p>The capstone now has two explicit claim tracks. The guaranteed capstone is auditable local LLM energy measurement: the harness plus the Apple-Silicon characterization it can already execute on the M3 Max. Split (disaggregated) inference remains the differentiating validating study; when Phase 3 hardware and feasibility gates land, it upgrades the capstone from local characterization to a split-energy crossover study.</p> <p>The frozen capstone headline, fallback claims, contribution ladder, and minimum-viable stop-lines are now recorded in <code>docs/contracts/capstone_scope.md</code>; that contract is the scope pointer for reader-facing wording under the claims ladder.</p> <p>The first working slice runs on a MacBook (Apple Silicon) with MLX as the runtime and <code>powermetrics</code> as the power source, producing complete, auditable run bundles. Further backends (NVIDIA + vLLM/llama.cpp, Jetson Orin, Raspberry Pi + Hailo as a feasibility finding) plug into the same adapter interfaces.</p> <p>Research questions:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Q1</strong>: Under what conditions (model size, prompt length, link speed, device pair) does splitting inference reduce total energy versus running monolithically on either device?</li> <li><strong>Q2</strong>: How sensitive is the split&#39;s energy cost to interconnect bandwidth (1GbE vs 2.5GbE vs optional 10GbE) - where is the crossover?</li> <li><strong>Q3</strong>: When splitting saves energy, what latency does it cost, and vice versa (energy-latency Pareto frontier)?</li> <li><strong>Q4</strong> (added 2026-07-07, council C-003): What fixed-vs-marginal energy model <code>E = fixed + prefill(prompt_tokens) + decode(output_tokens)</code> does each target/model/quantization follow — and can split-run energy be predicted compositionally from monolithic coefficients plus transfer measurements?</li> <li><strong>Q5</strong> (C-003/C-007): On one machine, do workload/model/quantization efficiency rankings stay stable as workload shape, model, and quantization change, or where do they flip? A cross-device ranking extension is hardware-gated.</li> <li><strong>Q6</strong> (C-003; gated on the wall meter): Does the measurement boundary (platform rails vs AC wall power) change the conclusions?</li> </ul> <p>Current question status, aliases, gates, and claim ceilings live in the canonical live index, <code>docs/research_question_registry.md</code>. The curated bank of further candidate questions and deliberately killed ones remains the historical/deliberative record in <code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>; the measurement noise floor / detection limit is treated as the methodology centerpiece rather than a numbered question.</p> <p>The capability map by claim ceiling is reflected in <code>docs/research_question_registry.md</code> (C-015), alongside the suite architecture v2 and benchmark interop direction; the guaranteed-capstone stop-line is recorded in the Phase 2 plan.</p> <p><strong>Q4 architectural stress-test agenda (D-070).</strong> Static batching, speculative decoding / native MTP, MoE versus dense execution, quantization, and reasoning-length variance are five stress tests of Q4&#39;s single fixed-plus-marginal energy thesis, not five additional theses. The harness must instrument every axis well enough to produce strict-valid L0 smoke bundles; the benchmark supplies the frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator for claim-bearing runs. Per Ed&#39;s ruling, all five axes have characterized-study commitments. Every study remains floor-gated and capped at L2; L3 is available only through Q4/AP-1&#39;s existing holdout machinery. Window A remains first, and no AXI quiet-Mac characterization starts before Window A completes. Static batching is the capstone scope; continuous batching remains a post-capstone extension.</p> <p><strong>Ranked extension-axis intake (D-075).</strong> The later six-axis evaluation did not create six more theses. It attached DSpark/DFlash break-even, proposal-work, and contamination-control riders to the speculative-decoding home; admitted an on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and one named hybrid pair; and attached cache/context, module-nonattribution, kernel, and backend provenance riders to their existing questions. All admitted units remain candidate work with earliest-phase tags, named forbidden upgrades, floor gates, and an intake ceiling at or below L2. Unverified runtime, pair, adapter, and device-fit questions remain explicitly NEEDS-WEB, and Ed retains commitment and ordering authority under D-070.</p> <h2 id="status-at-a-glance">Status At A Glance</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Phase</th> <th>Scope</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>1. Approval, feasibility, measurement design</td> <td>contracts, methodology, hardware feasibility evidence</td> <td><strong>in progress</strong> — the Phase 1 exit checklist owns exact completion and external gates</td> </tr> <tr> <td>2. Harness, Mac vertical slice, homogeneous baselines</td> <td>runnable harness, first real measurements, per-target baselines</td> <td><strong>in progress</strong> — Mac vertical slice and analysis software are implemented; remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL; the state kernel and quiet-machine rules own execution eligibility</td> </tr> <tr> <td>3. Disaggregation, KV replay, interconnect sweep</td> <td>split-energy decomposition, crossover dataset</td> <td>planned (feasibility-first)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>4. Characterization and analysis</td> <td>statistics, figures, claims audit</td> <td>planned</td> </tr> <tr> <td>5. Presentation and submission</td> <td>report, colloquium, reproducible release</td> <td>planned</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="capstone-artifact-map">Capstone Artifact Map</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>chapter/report-component</th> <th>owning doc or deliverable</th> <th>status</th> <th>missing evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>Background / related work</td> <td>Phase 4 Stage 4.6, <code>docs/phase_4/related_work_draft.md</code></td> <td>drafted (11 verified sources)</td> <td>background-chapter assembly and the Phase 4 exit pass</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Measurement methodology</td> <td><code>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md</code></td> <td>complete</td> <td>Phase 4 ratification may amend statistical details against observed variance</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Harness / instrument</td> <td><code>joulewise/</code></td> <td>complete; pre-campaign software review cleared; C-028 closed</td> <td>live execution eligibility comes from the state kernel; quiet-machine work also requires Ed and the clean hardware lane</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Apple-Silicon characterization / homogeneous baselines</td> <td>Phase 2 Slice 2M, <code>docs/phase_2/baseline_results.md</code></td> <td>Window A open; production shakedown closed and first floors published; quiet-Mac execution remains</td> <td>P2-037 claim adjudication and the live state kernel govern the next baseline step; needs Ed + quiet Mac</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Split-inference study</td> <td>Phase 3</td> <td>planned</td> <td>needs KV-feasibility spikes plus a real pairing, or the synthetic-transfer + analytical-composition floor</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Results / limitations + claims audit</td> <td>Phase 4 Stages 4.3-4.5</td> <td>analysis path implemented; Window-A calibration data exist</td> <td>the floor corpus is strict-valid but claim-evidence-flagged; P2-037 adjudication must preserve the published caveats before any claim promotion</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Complete so far (all verifiable in the repository):</p> <ul> <li>A runnable harness: from a typed config, one command (<code>python3 -m joulewise run ...</code>) produces a complete, schema-valid, auditable run bundle and reduces it to energy/latency summary metrics - proven first on deterministic mock adapters (controller, bundle contract, and reducer math verified without hardware) and now running live on the Mac target. Bundle writer, controller lifecycle, reducer, static-HTML report generator, and CLI verbs <code>run</code> / <code>validate-bundle</code> / <code>reduce</code> (post-hoc re-derivation of summary metrics from the recorded power trace and events) / <code>report</code>. Strict validation now also re-derives powermetrics traces from raw plist evidence, checks legacy additive-summary compatibility, and requires shape-valid provenance on new-era bundles. All bundle consumers read through one shared, tested read layer, which sharply reduces the risk of displayed numbers diverging from reported ones.</li> <li>Typed config and output schemas with validation, JSON-Schema export, and a CLI, plus the canonical suite run in CI on every push, including a mock end-to-end run and bundle validation. The command and CI output own the current result; reader docs do not copy its volatile count. Emitted configs round-trip their own published schema, and config hashes (run identity) are pinned by test.</li> <li>Adapter interface contracts (runtime / telemetry / transport), the run bundle artifact contract, and the measurement methodology (idle subtraction, measurement boundaries, clock synchronization, statistical protocol - highlights below).</li> <li>Evidence-shaped plans for every phase, a design-decision log whose index is mechanically checked against its decision bodies (with D-060 ratified by Ed); the log itself is the structural authority, and most entries record the alternatives considered), a risk register with an explicit descope ladder, and example configs for the Mac and mock targets.</li> <li>The complete Mac vertical slice: the MLX runtime adapter (2G), the <code>powermetrics</code> telemetry adapter (2H, parser pinned to a captured privileged sample, raw plists preserved verbatim in every bundle), and the flagship integration (2I) — three strict-valid repetition bundles of real energy measurements on the M3 Max. <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per 512-token request. <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~44.4 J per request and ~79-90 mJ per generated output token. TTFT was ~94 ms at 257 tokens/s; these are legacy L1 preliminary observations for provisional model Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit, mirrored locally. The separately recorded <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~304.0 J per 512-token request; <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~298.7 J per request and ~583 mJ per generated output token. These historical values are basis labels on the recorded results, not a new reduction.</li> <li>The P2-042 frozen analysis manifest, P2-041 campaign verdict split, P2-037 contrast/claim engine, P2-040 reducer/gate remainder, P2-038 production-uncertainty software path, and NV-GATE-2 code-now hardening. Reducer dispatch is frozen across the legacy and 0.3.x arms and current through 0.4.2. None of this promotes fixture-first NVIDIA evidence to live validation.</li> <li>The report&#39;s related-work survey draft (11 sources with verified citations and an honest positioning audit) and an off-machine iCloud Drive backup whose fresh restored bundles passed strict validation and were byte-identical to their sources.</li> </ul> <p>Live remote-hardware validation has not started: NVIDIA/vLLM and Jetson Orin promotion (2K/2L) remain gated on device access. The fixture-first implementation and NV-GATE-2 software hardening are landed, but all remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL until live hardware contact; a P1-006 evidence checklist exists there. Code-level specs are in <code>docs/phase_2/hardware_slice_implementation_guide.md</code>. The mock-first core landed first by design, so measurement code is never debugging the measurement harness and a live hardware integration at the same time.</p> <p>Waiting on external input (most of it does not block current software work; P0-003&#39;s backup gate is satisfied, and the grading rubric/calendar (P1-008) carries the provisional-contract fallback under ratified D-060):</p> <ol> <li>NVIDIA / Jetson Orin device access evidence — the one hard gate left, for the remote-target slices 2K/2L. (The <code>nvidia_3050</code> in the architecture table is the owned always-available NVIDIA target; the 3080 Ti is a separate, borrowed card used only for Phase 3&#39;s interconnect sweep.)</li> <li>Calendar anchors: colloquium date, report deadline, and the 3080 Ti borrow window, to derive phase target dates.</li> <li>Advisor scope confirmation (see the sanity-check note above) — finalizes model selection; deliberately deprioritized while all work remains harness-shaped and valuable under any scope.</li> </ol> <p>Closed since the last revision: the comprehensive audit; AXI-SA&#39;s burst-decode contract; SITE-02 D1/D2; the SPLIT-AP Part I pre-registration freeze; AXI-SB&#39;s <code>supported</code> static-batch verdict with its Mac C5-2.2 leg; P2-038&#39;s production-shaped live gate; and AXI-SC&#39;s <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> pinned- runtime verdict. Reviewed readout: suite gross <strong>147.96 ± 0.39 J</strong> clean (contaminated cells were ~+30%); frozen-estimator provisional comparative floor <strong>≈ 1.13 J (~0.77%)</strong> from 5 of 10 planned ABBA blocks (~22× tighter, same estimator, than the caveated figure); long-decode <strong>83.9 mJ/output-token</strong>, matching the 07-17 decode cell to ~0.1%. That corpus was claim-ineligible on source provenance (dirty collection tree); details: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-19-recalibration-update.html</code>.</p> <p>UPDATE (2026-07-19 night): the clean re-run is done — 288 strict-valid bundles with clean source provenance (<code>runs_recal3/4/5/6_20260719/</code>) cover every planned Window-A cell except DF-TELEM at planned n, including the complete n=10 suite-ABBA comparative cell; the source provenance gate is closed. <strong>SUPERSEDING UPDATE (2026-07-19/20): a same-day soundness audit found a timing bug, and no energy number from the existing recordings will be used for claims until re-measurement.</strong> In plain terms: the power meter and the workload log time on two different clocks, and our alignment between them could be off by up to ~1 second. Energy is computed by summing meter samples inside the workload&#39;s start/stop window, so a misaligned window integrates the wrong slice of the recording — dramatic for sub-second test runs (one 0.37 s run read 0.27 J when its true consumption, plainly present in the recording, was <del>8 J), and a meaningful hidden uncertainty (</del>±10 J) even on 60-second runs. Nothing measured negative; the recordings are intact and self-consistent; long-run repeatability (~0.3% across nights) shows the platform is stable. Very short workloads are simply below this instrument&#39;s resolution and will not be claimed — by design, not workaround. The fix (align on the meter&#39;s own timestamps, attach an explicit uncertainty range to every number, calibrate end-to-end with 40 precisely-timed GPU bursts before new data) is implemented and in adversarial review. Plain-language explainer: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-20-timing-defect-explainer.md</code>; technical record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>REPAIR COMPLETE (2026-07-22): the instrument repair is finished and signed off.</strong> Over three days the timing defect was fixed and the whole measurement chain was hardened through nine rounds of independent adversarial review (each round tried to break the instrument; the last round found one remaining gap, recorded below). In plain terms, the instrument now: (a) knows precisely when its power readings happened relative to the model&#39;s work (the clock-alignment fix, with the alignment uncertainty — about 27 milliseconds — carried into every result as an explicit error bar); (b) proves its own calibration is genuine and fresh — a calibration recording that was tampered with, mislabeled, taken under the wrong procedure, or older than 24 hours is automatically rejected; and (c) refuses to report a result rather than report a doubtful one, in every failure case we could construct. One known limitation is recorded honestly: the file that stores the detection-floor statistics is not yet cryptographically tied back to the raw measurements it came from, so we only trust such files when our own pipeline produced them in the same verified session (a fix is queued). Live validation on the real hardware passed: the validation recording (made under the earlier 40-pulse calibration procedure) detected all 40 calibration pulses with no false detections, and a test measurement reproduced the expected physics where the old defective pipeline had been wrong by a factor of ~28. Production measurements will use the newer 59-pulse calibration procedure, which supports the stronger statistical guarantee we quote for the timing error bar. Next: a fresh calibration and re-collection of the measurement campaign under the repaired instrument. Record: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-20-p0-instrument-repair.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>COLLECTION ERA UPDATE (2026-07-24): the repaired instrument has now been proven in production.</strong> Over two nights we collected 229 clean measurements across four properly-bracketed windows. The standout result: two identical reference measurements taken three hours apart agreed to within 0.007 joules on a ~38.5 joule task — about 0.02%, which is excellent repeatability for whole-system power measurement. The windows are not yet &quot;claim-grade&quot; for one honest reason: our own stability check (comparing a reference task at each window&#39;s start and end) was found to be asking a mathematically unanswerable question, so it failed every window on a technicality while the underlying data was good. After a formal debate between the two AI models working on the project — which the reviewing model won on one substantive point — the check was redesigned and ratified: windows are now screened for anomalous drift against a limit derived from measured repeatability (instead of an arbitrary constant), and any drift observed is carried into the results&#39; error bars rather than being ignored once a window &quot;passes&quot;. Reference measurements are also being tripled at each window edge. One collection session under the new rules produces the project&#39;s first claim-grade detection-floor table, which then sizes the Splitwise replication experiments. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-23-window-a-collection-arc.md</code>, decision log D-078 clauses 8-10.</p> <p><strong>SCREENING RULES BUILT, AUDITED, AND MERGED (2026-07-25; council C-033).</strong> The redesigned stability screen described above is now implemented and on main: both energy families are screened separately, every passing window carries an explicit drift allowance into its error bars, drift limits expire after 24 hours so stale calibrations cannot be reused, and a measurement whose internal clock had to be guessed can never anchor a result (that one rule alone corrected a floor that was overstated by roughly a factor of three). The code went through an unusually deep adversarial review — four independent audit rounds and three rounds of cross-examination between two different AI models — which caught and fixed several ways the new rules could have been silently bypassed. The step-by-step measurement procedure for the next collection session is written up in <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-24-screen-budget-gauntlet.md</code>, council log C-033.</p> <h3>Exploratory follow-on — not a promoted claim</h3> <p>Nine additional strict-valid, collection-usable bundles cover three repetitions each of unmatched OLMoE-1B-7B BF16, Qwen3-4B INT4, and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4 configurations on the fixed five-item <code>jw_mixed_v1_sentinel</code> shape. Every bundle is claim-evidence-flagged, the model/config points differ in architecture, scale, tokenizer, and quantization, and the repetition count is below the headline protocol. Every aggregate and raw repetition is bundle-cited in <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-exploratory-block/results.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-09-c-027-whole-project-council-review-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-09, C-027 whole-project council review) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The project put itself in front of a hostile examiner and corrected its own front page.</strong> A seven-lens cross-model review (new Codex model, extra-high reasoning) plus an independent final examiner audited the docs, the scientific claims, the statistics implementation, the architecture, and the operating loop itself. The P2-013 evidence-integrity and P2-014 provenance fixes are now complete; next Mac corpus step is the baseline matrix on a quiet machine.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-2026-07-07-fourth-update-30-second-read">Previous Update (2026-07-07, fourth update) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>A flagship-class model is now benchmarked.</strong> Qwen3.5-122B (Feb 2026 generation, 122B-parameter mixture-of-experts with 10B active, a reasoning model) ran through the identical harness and workload on the M3 Max. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~304.0 J per 512-token request. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~298.7 J per request and ~583 mJ per generated output token. class="source-file">PROJECT_STATUS.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise: Project Status — Full Reference</h1> <p><strong><a href="project_status.html">← Back to project status summary</a></strong></p> <p>This page continues the project-status document with its architecture, planning, and historical reference material.</p> <h2 id="summary">Summary</h2> <p>JouleWise combines a reusable, typed measurement harness with a benchmark defined by its frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator. It measures the energy of LLM inference across heterogeneous local hardware. The name nods to JouleSort and Splitwise: energy measurement is the spine of the system; disaggregated (&quot;split&quot;) inference - running prefill and decode on different machines with the KV cache transferred between them - is the validating research study, not the whole architecture.</p> <p>The capstone now has two explicit claim tracks. The guaranteed capstone is auditable local LLM energy measurement: the harness plus the Apple-Silicon characterization it can already execute on the M3 Max. Split (disaggregated) inference remains the differentiating validating study; when Phase 3 hardware and feasibility gates land, it upgrades the capstone from local characterization to a split-energy crossover study.</p> <p>The frozen capstone headline, fallback claims, contribution ladder, and minimum-viable stop-lines are now recorded in <code>docs/contracts/capstone_scope.md</code>; that contract is the scope pointer for reader-facing wording under the claims ladder.</p> <p>The first working slice runs on a MacBook (Apple Silicon) with MLX as the runtime and <code>powermetrics</code> as the power source, producing complete, auditable run bundles. Further backends (NVIDIA + vLLM/llama.cpp, Jetson Orin, Raspberry Pi + Hailo as a feasibility finding) plug into the same adapter interfaces.</p> <p>Research questions:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Q1</strong>: Under what conditions (model size, prompt length, link speed, device pair) does splitting inference reduce total energy versus running monolithically on either device?</li> <li><strong>Q2</strong>: How sensitive is the split&#39;s energy cost to interconnect bandwidth (1GbE vs 2.5GbE vs optional 10GbE) - where is the crossover?</li> <li><strong>Q3</strong>: When splitting saves energy, what latency does it cost, and vice versa (energy-latency Pareto frontier)?</li> <li><strong>Q4</strong> (added 2026-07-07, council C-003): What fixed-vs-marginal energy model <code>E = fixed + prefill(prompt_tokens) + decode(output_tokens)</code> does each target/model/quantization follow — and can split-run energy be predicted compositionally from monolithic coefficients plus transfer measurements?</li> <li><strong>Q5</strong> (C-003/C-007): On one machine, do workload/model/quantization efficiency rankings stay stable as workload shape, model, and quantization change, or where do they flip? A cross-device ranking extension is hardware-gated.</li> <li><strong>Q6</strong> (C-003; gated on the wall meter): Does the measurement boundary (platform rails vs AC wall power) change the conclusions?</li> </ul> <p>Current question status, aliases, gates, and claim ceilings live in the canonical live index, <code>docs/research_question_registry.md</code>. The curated bank of further candidate questions and deliberately killed ones remains the historical/deliberative record in <code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>; the measurement noise floor / detection limit is treated as the methodology centerpiece rather than a numbered question.</p> <p>The capability map by claim ceiling is reflected in <code>docs/research_question_registry.md</code> (C-015), alongside the suite architecture v2 and benchmark interop direction; the guaranteed-capstone stop-line is recorded in the Phase 2 plan.</p> <p><strong>Q4 architectural stress-test agenda (D-070).</strong> Static batching, speculative decoding / native MTP, MoE versus dense execution, quantization, and reasoning-length variance are five stress tests of Q4&#39;s single fixed-plus-marginal energy thesis, not five additional theses. The harness must instrument every axis well enough to produce strict-valid L0 smoke bundles; the benchmark supplies the frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator for claim-bearing runs. Per Ed&#39;s ruling, all five axes have characterized-study commitments. Every study remains floor-gated and capped at L2; L3 is available only through Q4/AP-1&#39;s existing holdout machinery. Window A remains first, and no AXI quiet-Mac characterization starts before Window A completes. Static batching is the capstone scope; continuous batching remains a post-capstone extension.</p> <p><strong>Ranked extension-axis intake (D-075).</strong> The later six-axis evaluation did not create six more theses. It attached DSpark/DFlash break-even, proposal-work, and contamination-control riders to the speculative-decoding home; admitted an on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and one named hybrid pair; and attached cache/context, module-nonattribution, kernel, and backend provenance riders to their existing questions. All admitted units remain candidate work with earliest-phase tags, named forbidden upgrades, floor gates, and an intake ceiling at or below L2. Unverified runtime, pair, adapter, and device-fit questions remain explicitly NEEDS-WEB, and Ed retains commitment and ordering authority under D-070.</p> <h2 id="status-at-a-glance">Status At A Glance</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Phase</th> <th>Scope</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>1. Approval, feasibility, measurement design</td> <td>contracts, methodology, hardware feasibility evidence</td> <td><strong>in progress</strong> — the Phase 1 exit checklist owns exact completion and external gates</td> </tr> <tr> <td>2. Harness, Mac vertical slice, homogeneous baselines</td> <td>runnable harness, first real measurements, per-target baselines</td> <td><strong>in progress</strong> — Mac vertical slice and analysis software are implemented; remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL; the state kernel and quiet-machine rules own execution eligibility</td> </tr> <tr> <td>3. Disaggregation, KV replay, interconnect sweep</td> <td>split-energy decomposition, crossover dataset</td> <td>planned (feasibility-first)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>4. Characterization and analysis</td> <td>statistics, figures, claims audit</td> <td>planned</td> </tr> <tr> <td>5. Presentation and submission</td> <td>report, colloquium, reproducible release</td> <td>planned</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="capstone-artifact-map">Capstone Artifact Map</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>chapter/report-component</th> <th>owning doc or deliverable</th> <th>status</th> <th>missing evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>Background / related work</td> <td>Phase 4 Stage 4.6, <code>docs/phase_4/related_work_draft.md</code></td> <td>drafted (11 verified sources)</td> <td>background-chapter assembly and the Phase 4 exit pass</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Measurement methodology</td> <td><code>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md</code></td> <td>complete</td> <td>Phase 4 ratification may amend statistical details against observed variance</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Harness / instrument</td> <td><code>joulewise/</code></td> <td>complete; pre-campaign software review cleared; C-028 closed</td> <td>live execution eligibility comes from the state kernel; quiet-machine work also requires Ed and the clean hardware lane</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Apple-Silicon characterization / homogeneous baselines</td> <td>Phase 2 Slice 2M, <code>docs/phase_2/baseline_results.md</code></td> <td>Window A open; production shakedown closed and first floors published; quiet-Mac execution remains</td> <td>P2-037 claim adjudication and the live state kernel govern the next baseline step; needs Ed + quiet Mac</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Split-inference study</td> <td>Phase 3</td> <td>planned</td> <td>needs KV-feasibility spikes plus a real pairing, or the synthetic-transfer + analytical-composition floor</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Results / limitations + claims audit</td> <td>Phase 4 Stages 4.3-4.5</td> <td>analysis path implemented; Window-A calibration data exist</td> <td>the floor corpus is strict-valid but claim-evidence-flagged; P2-037 adjudication must preserve the published caveats before any claim promotion</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Complete so far (all verifiable in the repository):</p> <ul> <li>A runnable harness: from a typed config, one command (<code>python3 -m joulewise run ...</code>) produces a complete, schema-valid, auditable run bundle and reduces it to energy/latency summary metrics - proven first on deterministic mock adapters (controller, bundle contract, and reducer math verified without hardware) and now running live on the Mac target. Bundle writer, controller lifecycle, reducer, static-HTML report generator, and CLI verbs <code>run</code> / <code>validate-bundle</code> / <code>reduce</code> (post-hoc re-derivation of summary metrics from the recorded power trace and events) / <code>report</code>. Strict validation now also re-derives powermetrics traces from raw plist evidence, checks legacy additive-summary compatibility, and requires shape-valid provenance on new-era bundles. All bundle consumers read through one shared, tested read layer, which sharply reduces the risk of displayed numbers diverging from reported ones.</li> <li>Typed config and output schemas with validation, JSON-Schema export, and a CLI, plus the canonical suite run in CI on every push, including a mock end-to-end run and bundle validation. The command and CI output own the current result; reader docs do not copy its volatile count. Emitted configs round-trip their own published schema, and config hashes (run identity) are pinned by test.</li> <li>Adapter interface contracts (runtime / telemetry / transport), the run bundle artifact contract, and the measurement methodology (idle subtraction, measurement boundaries, clock synchronization, statistical protocol - highlights below).</li> <li>Evidence-shaped plans for every phase, a design-decision log whose index is mechanically checked against its decision bodies (with D-060 ratified by Ed); the log itself is the structural authority, and most entries record the alternatives considered), a risk register with an explicit descope ladder, and example configs for the Mac and mock targets.</li> <li>The complete Mac vertical slice: the MLX runtime adapter (2G), the <code>powermetrics</code> telemetry adapter (2H, parser pinned to a captured privileged sample, raw plists preserved verbatim in every bundle), and the flagship integration (2I) — three strict-valid repetition bundles of real energy measurements on the M3 Max. <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per 512-token request. <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~44.4 J per request and ~79-90 mJ per generated output token. TTFT was ~94 ms at 257 tokens/s; these are legacy L1 preliminary observations for provisional model Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit, mirrored locally. The separately recorded <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~304.0 J per 512-token request; <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~298.7 J per request and ~583 mJ per generated output token. These historical values are basis labels on the recorded results, not a new reduction.</li> <li>The P2-042 frozen analysis manifest, P2-041 campaign verdict split, P2-037 contrast/claim engine, P2-040 reducer/gate remainder, P2-038 production-uncertainty software path, and NV-GATE-2 code-now hardening. Reducer dispatch is frozen across the legacy and 0.3.x arms and current through 0.4.2. None of this promotes fixture-first NVIDIA evidence to live validation.</li> <li>The report&#39;s related-work survey draft (11 sources with verified citations and an honest positioning audit) and an off-machine iCloud Drive backup whose fresh restored bundles passed strict validation and were byte-identical to their sources.</li> </ul> <p>Live remote-hardware validation has not started: NVIDIA/vLLM and Jetson Orin promotion (2K/2L) remain gated on device access. The fixture-first implementation and NV-GATE-2 software hardening are landed, but all remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL until live hardware contact; a P1-006 evidence checklist exists there. Code-level specs are in <code>docs/phase_2/hardware_slice_implementation_guide.md</code>. The mock-first core landed first by design, so measurement code is never debugging the measurement harness and a live hardware integration at the same time.</p> <p>Waiting on external input (most of it does not block current software work; P0-003&#39;s backup gate is satisfied, and the grading rubric/calendar (P1-008) carries the provisional-contract fallback under ratified D-060):</p> <ol> <li>NVIDIA / Jetson Orin device access evidence — the one hard gate left, for the remote-target slices 2K/2L. (The <code>nvidia_3050</code> in the architecture table is the owned always-available NVIDIA target; the 3080 Ti is a separate, borrowed card used only for Phase 3&#39;s interconnect sweep.)</li> <li>Calendar anchors: colloquium date, report deadline, and the 3080 Ti borrow window, to derive phase target dates.</li> <li>Advisor scope confirmation (see the sanity-check note above) — finalizes model selection; deliberately deprioritized while all work remains harness-shaped and valuable under any scope.</li> </ol> <p>Closed since the last revision: the comprehensive audit; AXI-SA&#39;s burst-decode contract; SITE-02 D1/D2; the SPLIT-AP Part I pre-registration freeze; AXI-SB&#39;s <code>supported</code> static-batch verdict with its Mac C5-2.2 leg; P2-038&#39;s production-shaped live gate; and AXI-SC&#39;s <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> pinned- runtime verdict. The later DSpark/DFlash MLX feasibility smokes and D-075 extension-axis intake are recorded without promoting an energy claim, and the nine-bundle OLMoE/Qwen follow-on remains explicitly exploratory. Window A&#39;s software gates are satisfied, its first floor corpus is published, and the window remains open. The floors are calibration thresholds rather than claim promotion: P2-037 adjudication remains pending because strict-valid collection and claim readiness are separate gates; execution timing is governed by the live work-selection state in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>&#39;s generated state-kernel region and still requires Ed plus a quiet Mac.</p> <h2 id="architecture">Architecture</h2> <pre><code class="language-text">typed config

class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent.
