1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise: Project Status — Full Reference</h1> <p><strong><a href="project_status.html">← Back to project status summary</a></strong></p> <p>This page continues the project-status document with its architecture, planning, and historical reference material.</p> <h2 id="summary">Summary</h2> <p>JouleWise combines a reusable, typed measurement harness with a benchmark defined by its frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator. It measures the energy of LLM inference across heterogeneous local hardware. The name nods to JouleSort and Splitwise: energy measurement is the spine of the system; disaggregated (&quot;split&quot;) inference - running prefill and decode on different machines with the KV cache transferred between them - is the validating research study, not the whole architecture.</p> <p>The capstone now has two explicit claim tracks. The guaranteed capstone is auditable local LLM energy measurement: the harness plus the Apple-Silicon characterization it can already execute on the M3 Max. Split (disaggregated) inference remains the differentiating validating study; when Phase 3 hardware and feasibility gates land, it upgrades the capstone from local characterization to a split-energy crossover study.</p> <p>The frozen capstone headline, fallback claims, contribution ladder, and minimum-viable stop-lines are now recorded in <code>docs/contracts/capstone_scope.md</code>; that contract is the scope pointer for reader-facing wording under the claims ladder.</p> <p>The first working slice runs on a MacBook (Apple Silicon) with MLX as the runtime and <code>powermetrics</code> as the power source, producing complete, auditable run bundles. Further backends (NVIDIA + vLLM/llama.cpp, Jetson Orin, Raspberry Pi + Hailo as a feasibility finding) plug into the same adapter interfaces.</p> <p>Research questions:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Q1</strong>: Under what conditions (model size, prompt length, link speed, device pair) does splitting inference reduce total energy versus running monolithically on either device?</li> <li><strong>Q2</strong>: How sensitive is the split&#39;s energy cost to interconnect bandwidth (1GbE vs 2.5GbE vs optional 10GbE) - where is the crossover?</li> <li><strong>Q3</strong>: When splitting saves energy, what latency does it cost, and vice versa (energy-latency Pareto frontier)?</li> <li><strong>Q4</strong> (added 2026-07-07, council C-003): What fixed-vs-marginal energy model <code>E = fixed + prefill(prompt_tokens) + decode(output_tokens)</code> does each target/model/quantization follow — and can split-run energy be predicted compositionally from monolithic coefficients plus transfer measurements?</li> <li><strong>Q5</strong> (C-003/C-007): On one machine, do workload/model/quantization efficiency rankings stay stable as workload shape, model, and quantization change, or where do they flip? A cross-device ranking extension is hardware-gated.</li> <li><strong>Q6</strong> (C-003; gated on the wall meter): Does the measurement boundary (platform rails vs AC wall power) change the conclusions?</li> </ul> <p>Current question status, aliases, gates, and claim ceilings live in the canonical live index, <code>docs/research_question_registry.md</code>. The curated bank of further candidate questions and deliberately killed ones remains the historical/deliberative record in <code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>; the measurement noise floor / detection limit is treated as the methodology centerpiece rather than a numbered question.</p> <p>The capability map by claim ceiling is reflected in <code>docs/research_question_registry.md</code> (C-015), alongside the suite architecture v2 and benchmark interop direction; the guaranteed-capstone stop-line is recorded in the Phase 2 plan.</p> <p><strong>Q4 architectural stress-test agenda (D-070).</strong> Static batching, speculative decoding / native MTP, MoE versus dense execution, quantization, and reasoning-length variance are five stress tests of Q4&#39;s single fixed-plus-marginal energy thesis, not five additional theses. The harness must instrument every axis well enough to produce strict-valid L0 smoke bundles; the benchmark supplies the frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator for claim-bearing runs. Per Ed&#39;s ruling, all five axes have characterized-study commitments. Every study remains floor-gated and capped at L2; L3 is available only through Q4/AP-1&#39;s existing holdout machinery. Window A remains first, and no AXI quiet-Mac characterization starts before Window A completes. Static batching is the capstone scope; continuous batching remains a post-capstone extension.</p> <p><strong>Ranked extension-axis intake (D-075).</strong> The later six-axis evaluation did not create six more theses. It attached DSpark/DFlash break-even, proposal-work, and contamination-control riders to the speculative-decoding home; admitted an on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and one named hybrid pair; and attached cache/context, module-nonattribution, kernel, and backend provenance riders to their existing questions. All admitted units remain candidate work with earliest-phase tags, named forbidden upgrades, floor gates, and an intake ceiling at or below L2. Unverified runtime, pair, adapter, and device-fit questions remain explicitly NEEDS-WEB, and Ed retains commitment and ordering authority under D-070.</p> <h2 id="status-at-a-glance">Status At A Glance</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Phase</th> <th>Scope</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>1. Approval, feasibility, measurement design</td> <td>contracts, methodology, hardware feasibility evidence</td> <td><strong>in progress</strong> — the Phase 1 exit checklist owns exact completion and external gates</td> </tr> <tr> <td>2. Harness, Mac vertical slice, homogeneous baselines</td> <td>runnable harness, first real measurements, per-target baselines</td> <td><strong>in progress</strong> — Mac vertical slice and analysis software are implemented; remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL; the state kernel and quiet-machine rules own execution eligibility</td> </tr> <tr> <td>3. Disaggregation, KV replay, interconnect sweep</td> <td>split-energy decomposition, crossover dataset</td> <td>planned (feasibility-first)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>4. Characterization and analysis</td> <td>statistics, figures, claims audit</td> <td>planned</td> </tr> <tr> <td>5. Presentation and submission</td> <td>report, colloquium, reproducible release</td> <td>planned</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="capstone-artifact-map">Capstone Artifact Map</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>chapter/report-component</th> <th>owning doc or deliverable</th> <th>status</th> <th>missing evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>Background / related work</td> <td>Phase 4 Stage 4.6, <code>docs/phase_4/related_work_draft.md</code></td> <td>drafted (11 verified sources)</td> <td>background-chapter assembly and the Phase 4 exit pass</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Measurement methodology</td> <td><code>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md</code></td> <td>complete</td> <td>Phase 4 ratification may amend statistical details against observed variance</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Harness / instrument</td> <td><code>joulewise/</code></td> <td>complete; pre-campaign software review cleared; C-028 closed</td> <td>live execution eligibility comes from the state kernel; quiet-machine work also requires Ed and the clean hardware lane</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Apple-Silicon characterization / homogeneous baselines</td> <td>Phase 2 Slice 2M, <code>docs/phase_2/baseline_results.md</code></td> <td>Window A open; production shakedown closed and first floors published; quiet-Mac execution remains</td> <td>P2-037 claim adjudication and the live state kernel govern the next baseline step; needs Ed + quiet Mac</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Split-inference study</td> <td>Phase 3</td> <td>planned</td> <td>needs KV-feasibility spikes plus a real pairing, or the synthetic-transfer + analytical-composition floor</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Results / limitations + claims audit</td> <td>Phase 4 Stages 4.3-4.5</td> <td>analysis path implemented; Window-A calibration data exist</td> <td>the floor corpus is strict-valid but claim-evidence-flagged; P2-037 adjudication must preserve the published caveats before any claim promotion</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Complete so far (all verifiable in the repository):</p> <ul> <li>A runnable harness: from a typed config, one command (<code>python3 -m joulewise run ...</code>) produces a complete, schema-valid, auditable run bundle and reduces it to energy/latency summary metrics - proven first on deterministic mock adapters (controller, bundle contract, and reducer math verified without hardware) and now running live on the Mac target. Bundle writer, controller lifecycle, reducer, static-HTML report generator, and CLI verbs <code>run</code> / <code>validate-bundle</code> / <code>reduce</code> (post-hoc re-derivation of summary metrics from the recorded power trace and events) / <code>report</code>. Strict validation now also re-derives powermetrics traces from raw plist evidence, checks legacy additive-summary compatibility, and requires shape-valid provenance on new-era bundles. All bundle consumers read through one shared, tested read layer, which sharply reduces the risk of displayed numbers diverging from reported ones.</li> <li>Typed config and output schemas with validation, JSON-Schema export, and a CLI, plus the canonical suite run in CI on every push, including a mock end-to-end run and bundle validation. The command and CI output own the current result; reader docs do not copy its volatile count. Emitted configs round-trip their own published schema, and config hashes (run identity) are pinned by test.</li> <li>Adapter interface contracts (runtime / telemetry / transport), the run bundle artifact contract, and the measurement methodology (idle subtraction, measurement boundaries, clock synchronization, statistical protocol - highlights below).</li> <li>Evidence-shaped plans for every phase, a design-decision log whose index is mechanically checked against its decision bodies (with D-060 ratified by Ed); the log itself is the structural authority, and most entries record the alternatives considered), a risk register with an explicit descope ladder, and example configs for the Mac and mock targets.</li> <li>The complete Mac vertical slice: the MLX runtime adapter (2G), the <code>powermetrics</code> telemetry adapter (2H, parser pinned to a captured privileged sample, raw plists preserved verbatim in every bundle), and the flagship integration (2I) — three strict-valid repetition bundles of real energy measurements on the M3 Max. <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per 512-token request. <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~44.4 J per request and ~79-90 mJ per generated output token. TTFT was ~94 ms at 257 tokens/s; these are legacy L1 preliminary observations for provisional model Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit, mirrored locally. The separately recorded <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~304.0 J per 512-token request; <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~298.7 J per request and ~583 mJ per generated output token. These historical values are basis labels on the recorded results, not a new reduction.</li> <li>The P2-042 frozen analysis manifest, P2-041 campaign verdict split, P2-037 contrast/claim engine, P2-040 reducer/gate remainder, P2-038 production-uncertainty software path, and NV-GATE-2 code-now hardening. Reducer dispatch is frozen across the legacy and 0.3.x arms and current through 0.4.2. None of this promotes fixture-first NVIDIA evidence to live validation.</li> <li>The report&#39;s related-work survey draft (11 sources with verified citations and an honest positioning audit) and an off-machine iCloud Drive backup whose fresh restored bundles passed strict validation and were byte-identical to their sources.</li> </ul> <p>Live remote-hardware validation has not started: NVIDIA/vLLM and Jetson Orin promotion (2K/2L) remain gated on device access. The fixture-first implementation and NV-GATE-2 software hardening are landed, but all remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL until live hardware contact; a P1-006 evidence checklist exists there. Code-level specs are in <code>docs/phase_2/hardware_slice_implementation_guide.md</code>. The mock-first core landed first by design, so measurement code is never debugging the measurement harness and a live hardware integration at the same time.</p> <p>Waiting on external input (most of it does not block current software work; P0-003&#39;s backup gate is satisfied, and the grading rubric/calendar (P1-008) carries the provisional-contract fallback under ratified D-060):</p> <ol> <li>NVIDIA / Jetson Orin device access evidence — the one hard gate left, for the remote-target slices 2K/2L. (The <code>nvidia_3050</code> in the architecture table is the owned always-available NVIDIA target; the 3080 Ti is a separate, borrowed card used only for Phase 3&#39;s interconnect sweep.)</li> <li>Calendar anchors: colloquium date, report deadline, and the 3080 Ti borrow window, to derive phase target dates.</li> <li>Advisor scope confirmation (see the sanity-check note above) — finalizes model selection; deliberately deprioritized while all work remains harness-shaped and valuable under any scope.</li> </ol> <p>Closed since the last revision: the comprehensive audit; AXI-SA&#39;s burst-decode contract; SITE-02 D1/D2; the SPLIT-AP Part I pre-registration freeze; AXI-SB&#39;s <code>supported</code> static-batch verdict with its Mac C5-2.2 leg; P2-038&#39;s production-shaped live gate; and AXI-SC&#39;s <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> pinned- runtime verdict. The later DSpark/DFlash MLX feasibility smokes and D-075 extension-axis intake are recorded without promoting an energy claim, and the nine-bundle OLMoE/Qwen follow-on remains explicitly exploratory. Window A&#39;s software gates are satisfied, its first floor corpus is published, and the window remains open. The floors are calibration thresholds rather than claim promotion: P2-037 adjudication remains pending because strict-valid collection and claim readiness are separate gates; execution timing is governed by the live work-selection state in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>&#39;s generated state-kernel region and still requires Ed plus a quiet Mac.</p> <h2 id="architecture">Architecture</h2> <pre><code class="language-text">typed config

review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-u-units/U1-AUDIT-CONTRACT.md:517:1. ACCOUNTING SOURCE. Sol spend: `codex-usage` local accounting (the standing snapshot convention), corroborated by codex-run-v3 manifest `token_usage` rows where populated. The extraction window must cover the full arc — sum incremental snapshots for multi-day arcs; a single trailing-24h view is insufficient. Fable spend: estimated from local usage accounting; each snapshot names its method and price-table version. Price table v2026-07 (pinned until amended): GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30 per M in/out, cached input $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1. All figures are estimates, not billing truth, and are recorded as such. Missing data is recorded as `accounting_unknown`, never as zero.

All figures are estimates, not billing truth, and are recorded as such. Missing data is recorded as `accounting_unknown`, never as zero.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-night-hardening/AUDIT-MINT.md:4127:./docs/site/orchestration.html:1:<!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="utf-8"> <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> <title>The Orchestration Process - JouleWise</title> <script>document.documentElement.classList.add("js-enabled");</script> <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 100 100'><text y='.9em' font-size='90'>⚡</text></svg>"> </head> <body> <header class="site"> <nav class="nav"> <a class="brand" href="index.html"><span class="dot"></span>JOULEWISE</a> <div class="links"> <a href="index.html">Project</a> <a href="research.html">Learn</a> <a href="advisor_brief.html">Advisor Brief</a> <a href="project_status.html">Status</a> <a href="status.html">Live Status</a> <a href="roadmap.html">Roadmap</a> <a href="process.html">Process</a> <a href="record.html">Record</a> <a href="library.html" class="active">Sources</a> <a href="results.html">Measurements</a> </div> </nav> </header> <main> <div class="doc-layout"> <aside class="toc-sidebar"><div class="card-label">Table of contents</div><a href="#roles-a-lead-independent-implementers-reviewers-and-a-human-at-the-top">Roles: a lead, independent implementers/reviewers, and a human at the top</a> <a href="#the-loop-end-to-end">The loop, end to end</a> <a href="#the-artifact-system-where-rigor-becomes-auditable">The artifact system (where rigor becomes auditable)</a> <a href="#council-discipline">Council discipline</a> <a href="#spend-guardrails-wo-022-r2-ruled-ed-ratified-2026-07-13">Spend guardrails (WO-022; R2 ruled, Ed-ratified 2026-07-13)</a> <a href="#topology-how-it-evolved-an-example-of-the-loop-improving-itself">Topology: how it evolved (an example of the loop improving itself)</a> <a href="#what-one-session-looks-like-2026-07-07-08-the-merge-session">What one session looks like (2026-07-07/08, the merge session)</a> <a href="#reconstructing-the-loop-on-a-clean-machine">Reconstructing the loop on a clean machine</a> <a href="#where-to-read-the-evidence">Where to read the evidence</a></aside> <div class="doc-wrap doc-source-docs-orchestration-md"> <p class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>docs/orchestration.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/orchestration.md · commit 0de4cea"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>orchestration.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 0de4cea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>The Orchestration Process</h1> <p>How this project is actually built: a human researcher directing a multi-model AI system whose workflow is itself a deliberate, versioned, self-instrumenting piece of engineering. This document is the single in-repo description of that process. (The executable playbooks live outside the repository as reusable &quot;skills&quot; so they transfer to future projects; this page describes what they do and where their evidence lands in this repo.) Binding role and process changes live in <code>docs/decision_log.md</code>; this page avoids copying volatile model versions.</p> <h2 id="roles-a-lead-independent-implementers-reviewers-and-a-human-at-the-top">Roles: a lead, independent implementers/reviewers, and a human at the top</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Ed (researcher)</strong> sets research direction, methodology non-negotiables (raw-evidence bundles, dual-basis capture with gross-energy headlines, named measurement boundaries, no unauditable claims), hardware/access decisions, and — critically — <em>process policy</em>: every rule below traces to a standing instruction issued after an observed failure or opportunity. External-facing claims and merge authority derive from him (he granted the lead conditional self-merge authority on 2026-07-08 once the review gate had proven itself).</li> <li><strong>The designated lead</strong> owns decomposition, triage, design adjudication, every final diff gate, all live/hardware verification, merge decisions, bookkeeping, and process evolution. Other agents save lead capacity without inheriting final authority; all escalation paths terminate at the lead.</li> <li><strong>Independent implementation and review agents</strong> do the heavy reading and writing: implementation against pinned specs, adversarial review lenses, test writing, test <em>auditing</em> (never of its own tests — a fresh instance audits), docs drafting, and review of the lead&#39;s own consequential decisions. Cross-model review is load-bearing by design: the attributed per-layer catch record (below) shows the two roles consistently catching different classes of defect.</li> <li><strong>Specialist agents</strong> handle bounded sweeps (for example, docs consistency) and, when a stream genuinely needs mid-stream judgment, as a stream director — a role that is now the exception rather than the default (see Topology).</li> <li><strong>Image-heavy analysis uses the designated image-capable review route</strong> per C-012, after the site-observatory stream&#39;s image-critique rounds.</li> <li><strong>Invited-peer validation is allowed to overturn lead designs</strong>; C-014 recorded two lead designs overturned by an invited peer before implementation.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-loop-end-to-end">The loop, end to end</h2> <p>Every substantial session runs one conductor procedure:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Intake</strong> — read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> (the intake pointer), the task queue, the latest run report; never re-decide anything the decision log settled.</li> <li><strong>Decompose</strong> — split work into genuinely independent streams (disjoint expected diff footprints), one git worktree + branch each; assign each stream a review tier by <em>cost of being wrong</em> (measurement-semantics and contract-bearing work gets the full pipeline; docs get a light tier). Preflight gates: hardware-shaped streams require a confirmed device inventory; anything pinned without live validation carries a PROVISIONAL label; measurement sessions require a no-agent &quot;quiet machine&quot; lock.</li> <li><strong>Per-stream pipeline</strong> — for each reviewable unit: an invited design-argument round (the implementer must argue trade-offs before coding), implementation, then a layered review stack: 2–3 fresh-instance counterreview lenses over the diff → lead triage with recorded dispositions → fixes → a dedicated test-amplification round (an independent writer adds edge-case tests) → a writer≠reviewer test audit (a fresh instance hunts tautological, vacuous, or wrong-expectation tests) → the lead&#39;s diff gate.</li> <li><strong>Lead live gates</strong> — never delegated: the lead runs the real flow (real corpus, real CLI, real hardware where present). This layer has repeatedly caught blockers no other layer saw, including defects whose own tests were green because the tests encoded the same wrong assumption as the code.</li> <li><strong>Merge gate</strong> — multi-commit series land as branch + PR. Before any merge: a pre-merge oversight pass by 2–3 fresh reviewers with distinct angles (deep regression hunt; claim-to-evidence trace; merge-order simulation across sibling PRs), lead triage, fixes, CI green. <strong>Final-head rule:</strong> any commit that lands after the last review round gets one more fresh review before merge — no commit merges unreviewed, however small (its first application caught a crash path in a &quot;trivial&quot; post-review fix).</li> <li><strong>Integration review</strong> — after parallel streams merge, one dedicated review hunts <em>interaction</em> defects no single-stream review can see. Its catches are definitionally unique (first outing: two).</li> <li><strong>Bookkeeping</strong> — a single session record (run report) with a verbatim process-trace appendix; the intake pointer and queue refreshed; a delegated docs-consistency sweep before the final commit (its latest pass found 15 real drift items; earlier passes found 5–6). Large documentation batches add the pre-commit docs-verify mode; the <code>consistency-sweep</code> skill owns that shape, including the D-043 supersession check.</li> <li><strong>Same-session distillation</strong> — lessons fold into the process playbooks the same session they are learned. Measured effect: one failure mode recurred five times before its fix was distilled, zero times after. The current operation-loop also runs its §0 primary-deliverable check and §8 shipped-check before the session is considered done.</li> <li><strong>Post-landing verification and close-out</strong> — landed work gets the matching verification workflow with severity-tiered refuters. Sessions that change front-facing state refresh <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code>; no agent regenerates or deploys the site. Automation informs and Ed deploys manually, per D-068 and <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> end-of-work step 8.</li> <li><strong>Meta-review (the final step)</strong> — event-driven, not calendar-driven: when a review layer stops earning its keep, when an intervention repeats despite a folded fix, or when the user asks, the loop is reviewed with its own evidence discipline (see Topology for the consensus one such review produced). After large workloads the post-large-workload meta-reassessment (owned by operation-loop §10) always fires, and it runs LAST.</li> </ol> <h3>Stop cards and paused work</h3> <p>When a session stops with live work in progress, the lead creates or updates an <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code> at the top of <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>. While active, that card is the single restart authority and overrides every lower &quot;what next&quot; list, queue rank, mission guide, and run-report default.</p> <p>A stop card must name:</p> <ul> <li>the resume authority and exact artifact pointer,</li> <li>the reason for stopping,</li> <li>worktrees, branches, PRs, and off-repo artifacts that must not be cleaned accidentally,</li> <li>status terms for each paused item,</li> <li>the first resume action, and</li> <li>the clearance criteria.</li> </ul> <p>Use these status terms for paused work:</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Term</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td><code>APPLIED_UNVERIFIED</code></td> <td>A worker reports code or docs are applied, but the lead has not gated the diff. Not merge-safe.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>LEAD_GATED</code></td> <td>The lead has reviewed and run the required local/live checks for the item.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>PR_OPEN_CI_GREEN</code></td> <td>A PR exists and CI is green, but merge authority has not yet fired.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>MERGED</code></td> <td>The accepted work has landed on main.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>UNREAD_UNADJUDICATED</code></td> <td>A report/synthesis exists but has not been consumed into decisions, queue rows, or rejected findings.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>ADJUDICATED</code></td> <td>Findings have explicit accept/reject/defer disposition and downstream artifacts are updated.</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Before an intentional pause, do the minimal stop sync even if full bookkeeping cannot fit: update only <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>&#39;s stop card and the rank-0 queue row. That is enough to prevent accidental bypass.</p> <h2 id="the-artifact-system-where-rigor-becomes-auditable">The artifact system (where rigor becomes auditable)</h2> <p>Each fact has exactly one home; everything else points at it:</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Artifact</th> <th>Role</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></td> <td>Binding design decisions, each with alternatives considered, consequences, and revisit conditions. The log is the count authority; nothing re-decides these silently.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/council_log.md</code></td> <td>The deliberation record: review-council positions, reasoning exchanged, who prevailed, overridden dissents — so a future reader can reconstruct <em>why</em>, not just <em>what</em>. The log is the range/count authority.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/contracts/</code></td> <td>Claim/evidence contracts: <code>claims_ladder.md</code> (D-037) plus <code>analysis_plans.md</code> (D-038) form the claim gate; strict validation is the evidence ticket.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/stream_logs/</code></td> <td>Per-stream decision ledgers, committed WITH the code they justify: every non-trivial in-stream decision (<code>A-1..A-30</code>, <code>B-1..B-46</code>, …) with mandatory evidence pointers; wrong pins are SUPERSEDED in place, never erased.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/run_reports/</code></td> <td>One record per working session: outcomes, verification evidence, a per-layer catch/yield table, the delegation-calibration ledger, restart instructions.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/process/state_kernel.json</code></td> <td>Source of truth for work selection: active gates, dependencies, and machine-state lanes ([QUIET-MAC] / [AGENT] / [ED-EXTERNAL]).</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code></td> <td>Generated detailed queue projection plus dated history; do not hand-copy its live rows into reader docs.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>RUN_STATE.md</code></td> <td>Intake pointer with the generated restart projection. History lives in run reports.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/risk_register.md</code></td> <td>Live risks with triggers and mitigation states.</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Instrumentation ledgers close the loop on the process itself:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Per-layer yield:</strong> every review layer&#39;s unique catches are attributed and tallied per session under D-061 (C-027; replaces the earlier two-zero-sessions auto-drop, which the integration-review zero/zero/five sequence falsified): applicability is decided by PRE-DECLARED mechanical predicates; outcomes are classified accepted-unique-defect / duplicate / clean-verification / false-positive-suppression (suppression is not a catch); severity weights are fixed before the session; three applicable exposures TRIGGER an expected-loss review decision, never automatic deletion; safety/final-head/integration layers are never auto-dropped on zero-defect streaks. (One layer, the default specialist review lens, was dropped under the old rule before D-061.)</li> <li><strong>Delegation calibration:</strong> every delegated unit gets a row — task altitude (pinned-spec / design-freedom / judgment-call), outcome (assigned by the lead after the gate, never self-labeled), catches, and lead rework minutes, with prompt-defects separated from model-defects. Delegation boundaries move on this evidence, not vibes. Current signal: pinned-spec delegation runs essentially defect-free; the serious defects cluster in volunteered additions and design-freedom wire contracts — which is exactly where the full lens</li> <li><strong>Invocation manifest:</strong> substantial delegated/tool/skill runs get a lightweight manifest row per invocation. Minimum fields: <code>run_id</code>, <code>parent_report</code>, <code>role_or_lens</code>, <code>model</code>, <code>wrapper</code>, <code>session_id</code>, <code>prompt_sha256</code>, <code>prompt_path</code>, <code>output_path</code>, <code>status</code>, <code>consumed_by</code>, <code>disposition</code>, and <code>commit_or_pr</code>. Raw logs can stay out of git; every ephemeral artifact still needs a committed pointer row with <code>path</code>, <code>sha256</code> or stable id, <code>promoted_to</code>, and <code>not_promoted_reason</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="council-discipline">Council discipline</h2> <p>Councils are expensive instruments. Use a full council for methodology, measurement validity, schema/contract changes, claim boundaries, hardware protocols, or explicit user requests. For ordinary implementation, use a small number of targeted lenses plus lead adjudication.</p> <p>Every high-impact council must leave a durable scorecard:</p> <ul> <li>unique catches by severity,</li> <li>accepted/rejected/deferred/false-positive counts,</li> <li>lead triage and rework time when practical,</li> <li>shipped artifacts,</li> <li>queue rows created or re-ranked,</li> <li>decision-log IDs promoted, and</li> <li>a disposition table: finding → ruling → owner → artifact/queue/decision target → closure check.</li> </ul> <p>Deferred decision-log promotion is itself a tracked obligation, not ambient prose in a report.</p> <h2 id="spend-guardrails-wo-022-r2-ruled-ed-ratified-2026-07-13">Spend guardrails (WO-022; R2 ruled, Ed-ratified 2026-07-13)</h2> <p>The following policy text is the R2-ratified section, landed verbatim per audit work order WO-022 (<code>docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/</code>).</p> <p>SPEND GUARDRAILS (capstone benchmark bands) — provisional calibration constants; review after two completed arcs; sunset at capstone submission.</p> <ol> <li><p>ACCOUNTING SOURCE. Sol spend: <code>codex-usage</code> local accounting (the standing snapshot convention), corroborated by codex-run-v3 manifest <code>token_usage</code> rows where populated. The extraction window must cover the full arc — sum incremental snapshots for multi-day arcs; a single trailing-24h view is insufficient. Fable spend: estimated from local usage accounting; each snapshot names its method and price-table version. Price table v2026-07 (pinned until amended): GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30 per M in/out, cached input $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1. All figures are estimates, not billing truth, and are recorded as such. Missing data is recorded as <code>accounting_unknown</code>, never as zero.</p> </li> <li><p>DENOMINATOR AND CACHED-TOKEN TREATMENT. Token bands count total tokens (cached + uncached, all directions) exactly as codex-usage reports them — cached tokens are never excluded (exclusion invites cache-heavy gaming). Dollar figures apply cached pricing honestly. Cross-family aggregate ceilings bind in combined estimated dollars, because raw cross-family token sums are not commensurable (C-028: Sol ~180x the token volume, Fable ~3.4x the cost).</p> </li> <li><p>BOUNDARIES AND ATTRIBUTION. An arc = one council-log C-row, opened at its first delegated session, closed at its closeout snapshot. A work order = one WO/task id. Failed calls, retries, resumes, refuters, fix rounds, delta re-audits, lead usage, and subagents all count against the initiating WO and arc. Arcs and WOs may not be split, renamed, or reopened to reset counters.</p> </li> <li><p>BANDS. Each dimension is independent. SOFT crossing = record-and-continue: flag in the spend snapshot plus a one-line justification in the council row. HARD crossing = pause-and-ask Ed before any NEW delegated work in that category; in-flight sessions finish; quiet-machine measurement is never interrupted.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Scope</th> <th>Soft</th> <th>Hard</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>Sol high session</td> <td>6M tokens</td> <td>12M</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Sol xhigh session</td> <td>8M</td> <td>16M</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Sol ultra session</td> <td>40M</td> <td>60M</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Bench-effort WO</td> <td>10M / 3 Sol sessions / ~$40 combined</td> <td>20M / 6 / ~$80</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Session-effort WO</td> <td>30M / 8 Sol sessions / ~$100 combined</td> <td>60M / 12 / ~$200</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Arc</td> <td>100M / 25 Sol sessions / ~$400 combined / 6 Sol active-hours / 2 elapsed days</td> <td>200M / 40 / ~$800 / 12 h / 4 days</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>WO dollar figures are best-effort: when per-WO Fable attribution is accounting_unknown, the token/session pair binds. Ultra: at most 2 INTENDED ultra sessions per arc, each with a pre-run recorded statement of why xhigh is insufficient and what bounded subagent work it will perform; an unintended ultra is recorded as an anomaly and still counts.</p> <p>Calibration anchors (recorded so recalibration stays honest): healthy xhigh ≈ 2.3–3.5M tokens/session (C-030 post effort-fix; C-028 average); the recorded broken state averaged ~9M. C-028 (330.6M / 59 sessions / ~$1,050 / ~17.5h) crosses every substantive arc HARD dimension — it is the anti-example. The 2026-07-13 comprehensive audit (~30 Sol sessions + ~70 Fable agents, Ed-authorized) crosses arc SOFT on session count only — the intended &quot;exceptional: justify and continue&quot; outcome.</p> </li> <li><p>CHECKPOINTS (procedural; owner = the Fable lead). (a) At arc open: predeclare one accepted deliverable increment for the arc — a corpus/measurement result, analysis/figure/report increment, evaluator requirement, or cited advancement of a D-060 gate — and classify planned delegated work as deliverable-facing or process-facing (mixed sessions count as process-facing unless separately attributable). (b) Before each next delegated call: check the completed session against its tier band (a lightweight glance, not a full snapshot); no runtime killing is promised — evaluation happens on completed sessions before any resume, replacement, or new call. (c) At WO close and arc close: take the spend snapshot and evaluate all bands. One missed checkpoint blocks new process-facing delegation until reconciled.</p> </li> <li><p>DELIVERABLE-PROGRESS TRIPWIRE (binds while ANY D-060 gate is unmet). If process-facing combined estimated cost exceeds 33% of arc cost OR $250 — whichever occurs first — HARD pause-and-ask Ed before further process-facing delegation. Independently, an arc that closes with process-facing spend but NO accepted deliverable increment pauses further non-exempt process work even if the 33% threshold was not crossed.</p> </li> <li><p>EXCEPTIONS AND OVERRIDES. Gate-closing work is deliverable-facing by definition. Correctness-defect and data-preservation work may override the allocation tripwire but is always fully counted. Ed direction is NOT a blanket exemption (the finding&#39;s own exemplar — bridge v1/v1.1 — was Ed-directed): it is a recorded override carrying an incremental budget and an expiry, and its spend counts.</p> </li> <li><p>NAMED-FAILURE BAR FOR PROCESS INNOVATION. Any NEW process layer, tool, skill, wrapper version, or contract version requires a decision-log entry citing: (a) a named recorded failure it addresses, (b) why existing controls did not cover it, (c) the smallest new layer that does, (d) its applicability predicate, (e) its marginal budget, (f) a sunset/retirement condition. Absent that entry, it is D-060 breadth and waits for the gates.</p> </li> <li><p>KEEP-DEFENDER GUARANTEE. No cap consequence auto-deletes a review layer. Layers with recorded unique catches survive any cap; a cap response batches, rescopes, or seeks Ed approval — never silently drops catch-bearing gates (final-head, integration, lead-live, claim/evidence safeguards).</p> </li> <li><p>MECHANISM. This policy is PROCEDURAL, not mechanical: no checker script is built now (adding process code during an overengineering correction is self-defeating; the arithmetic is a handful of numbers already recorded at existing snapshot points). Two recorded accounting discrepancies or skipped checkpoints across two arcs constitute the named failure that authorizes an executable checker with tests — via the §8 bar.</p> </li> <li><p>RECALIBRATION AND OWNERSHIP. Band values are calibration constants: the lead may amend SOFT values at arc close with evidence via a one-line decision-log amendment; HARD values and this section&#39;s structure are Ed-owned. Scheduled review after two completed arcs. The whole policy sunsets at capstone submission.</p> </li> </ol> <p>Court amendments (T09, folded at the register): canonical session inclusion uses manifest-corroborated sessions with known token records; resume rows are deduplicated; non-manifest sessions are reported only as a labeled upper bound. The 2026-07-13 audit anchor in section 4 is estimated/accounting_unknown until an audit-close spend snapshot receipts it (docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/receipts/ WO-022-audit-close-spend.json); only a receipted anchor may be used for recalibration.</p> <h2 id="topology-how-it-evolved-an-example-of-the-loop-improving-itself">Topology: how it evolved (an example of the loop improving itself)</h2> <ul> <li><strong>v1 (2026-07-07 AM):</strong> per-stream Fable orchestrator subagents, each driving its own Codex thread. Worked, but expensive at the apex tier.</li> <li><strong>v2 (2026-07-07 PM):</strong> Opus orchestrators directing Codex, Fable apex-only. Ran four streams — and surfaced a structural flaw: subagent orchestrators are not woken by their childrens&#39; completion (the &quot;wake gap&quot;), forcing the lead to babysit with heartbeats. The session&#39;s own trace captured two fleet-wide stalls.</li> <li><strong>Meta-review (C-009):</strong> a signed cross-model consensus — two blind Codex analyses vs. the lead&#39;s blind position, one conferral round — produced a hybrid: the lead drives pipeline-shaped streams directly (inheriting the harness&#39;s only reliable wake guarantee); subagent directors are reserved for judgment-heavy streams.</li> <li><strong>Validation (C-010, 2026-07-08):</strong> the first full session under the new topology ran ~26 Codex sessions across four streams — resume through merge — with zero coordination stalls, zero manual wake interventions, and no subagent stream directors at all. The consensus is now the stamped default.</li> </ul> <p>The same mechanism has overturned the lead&#39;s own designs: a Codex review of the lead&#39;s process schemas rejected two of them and supplied better ones (now the v2 ledger and calibration formats), and review lenses have refuted two of the lead&#39;s sanctioned wire-protocol pins before they could reach hardware. Seniority is not infallibility; the adjudication of every such challenge remains the lead&#39;s.</p> <h2 id="what-one-session-looks-like-2026-07-07-08-the-merge-session">What one session looks like (2026-07-07/08, the merge session)</h2> <p>Four checkpointed streams resumed, completed, and landed as four PRs: the integrity/provenance overhaul (all 31 audit-pinned defects fixed; strict validation now re-derives the power trace from raw evidence), the docs package, the KV-cache replay feasibility verdict, and the complete fixture-first NVIDIA stack. The layered review recorded, among ~30 attributed catches: two blockers found only by fresh-instance lenses (a provenance hash that did not prove the actual generation input; a strict-gate bypass via mutable metadata), two pinned wire contracts overturned before hardware contact, one fabricated-evidence defect caught only at the lead&#39;s diff gate, two integration defects caught only by the post-merge integration review, and a crash path caught only by the final-head rule on the last commit of the night. Suite: 415 → 546 tests, zero expected failures. Roughly two dozen delegated Codex sessions; the lead never wrote implementation code and never skipped a gate.</p> <h2 id="reconstructing-the-loop-on-a-clean-machine">Reconstructing the loop on a clean machine</h2> <p>Pointer map only; mechanics stay in their owning files.</p> <ul> <li>Committed invocation wrapper: <code>scripts/codex-run</code>. Usage: <code>codex-run &lt;out.md&gt; [--timeout SEC] [-C DIR] [-s SANDBOX] [--resume] &#39;&lt;prompt&gt;&#39;</code>. It writes <code>&lt;out&gt;.status</code>.</li> <li>Project bridge: <code>scripts/codex-bridge</code>; writes prompt snapshots, response snapshots, logs, status files, and <code>.codex-bridge/invocation_manifest.jsonl</code> rows with prompt/output/log hashes.</li> <li>Workspace-write bridge ceremony: <code>scripts/bridge session-open</code> and <code>session-close</code>; the reduced discussion header, tolerant return envelope, receipt anchoring, and recovery primitives are defined only in <code>docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md</code> (<code>bridge-protocol/v1.1</code>).</li> <li>Skill-only mechanics on the operator&#39;s machine live under <code>~/.claude/skills</code>: <code>operation-loop</code> is the conductor, <code>codex-delegation</code> is the invocation/consumption contract, <code>adversarial-review</code> defines refutation tiers, <code>multi-stream-worktrees</code> defines parallel stream mechanics, <code>consistency-sweep</code> owns drift control, and <code>council</code> owns triggers/roles.</li> <li>Repo-derivable on a clean clone: this file gives the loop shape; review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. This entry records only the genuine deliberation.</p> <p>Participants: Fable 5 lead; Codex gpt-5.6-sol xhigh (FIRST production session of the new model; CLI upgraded 0.143.0→0.144.0 mid-session after the old CLI rejected the model) — 7 read-only lenses + 1 counterreview; 1 fresh-context Fable-tier final examiner. Scope declaration: all peer passes were STATIC-ONLY and single-model-family — execution behavior, SSH-path security, and licensing were reviewed by nobody and are recorded as open debts, not clean.</p> <p>Positions → resolutions (design-bearing only):</p> <ul> <li>Legacy-gates framing: lead draft said the six real bundles &quot;failed the advertised gates&quot;; counterreview showed D-037 binds from 2M onward, so the correct frame is legacy L1 + manual waivers — counterreview PREVAILED (the lead&#39;s framing would have manufactured an ex-post-protocol defense problem).</li> <li>Process-restructure staging: lead deferred the machine-readable state kernel; counterreview argued deferral leaves the demonstrated drift mode active and that policy generation is the harder half — counterreview PREVAILED; kernel is Stage 1 (D-063 records the reversal).</li> <li>Layer-drop rule: lead&#39;s &quot;3 applicable sessions, severity-weighted&quot; was attacked as reintroducing post-hoc discretion; adopted WITH the peer&#39;s mechanical-predicate construction (D-061).</li> <li>ARCH severity: undifferentiated blocker trio split into immediate (zero-window, P2-040) vs NVIDIA-gated (NV-GATE-2) per counterreview.</li> <li>Sequential sampling: fixed-n + explicit demotion adopted over both status quo and default alpha-spending (D-062); peer confirmed the demotion rule is coherent only with its four explicit clauses.</li> </ul> <p>Layer yields (C-027): lenses 8 confirmed blocker clusters + ~60 accepted findings, 0 verified false positives (blocker tier; lower tiers unaudited); counterreview 3 synthesis blockers (2 were LEAD errors — the only confirmed review errors this session were the lead&#39;s); final examiner 8 dropped/under-tiered findings + the validity-threats section, all adopted. G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. was self-invalid synthetic-only; B2&#39;s stale-vs-invalid relabel would have broken a ratified distinction); narrowed C1 to a registered nit; split on A1 (contract-confirmed, reachability-refuted) — lead synthesis: pre-existing defense-in-depth hardening, not a round-8 regression.</li> <li>Round-9 confirmation: CR9-1 (floor artifacts self-attesting) — the only finding of the round, repro-backed, lead-reproduced at the bench.</li> <li>Lead unique: false-attribution triage of the 8b audit&#39;s two &quot;blockers&quot; (both were the lead&#39;s own authorized bench edits); the L1 adjudication.</li> </ul> <p>Failure modes recorded: (1) upstream cyber-content filter killed 3/8 refuters mid-run on adversarial phrasing (&quot;malformed/tamper/escape&quot;) — rephrasing as data-quality QA of our own instrument recovered all three (route: keep refuter briefs mechanism-neutral); (2) lead bench-edited the worktree while an enforced-scope Sol session ran in it → false SCOPE_VIOLATION attribution + resume-registry loss (rule: no lead edits in a tree with a live enforced-scope session); (3) the known xhigh review-genre null-final-message mode recurred on round 9; the documented bridge-resume recovery worked first try.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: the 8b delta auditor&#39;s should-fix (OverflowError normalization also reaching v1 replay error behavior) was overridden by lead ruling — frozen-replay doctrine protects computed semantics of parsable artifacts, not crash reproduction on impossible inputs; the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Yield: the peer&#39;s structural correction (anomaly screen must not erase drift from the claim budget) was adopted — the second recorded case of invited peer design judgment beating the lead&#39;s ruling. The debate also surfaced one gap neither model had specced (drift-bound freshness horizon — prompted by Ed&#39;s own risk question) and one open science question (a7-vs-a5 prefill floor scatter, 3x). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-night-hardening/AUDIT-LEDGER.md:11044:docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/register.jsonl:83:{"acceptance_evidence": "The exact R2 spend-guardrail policy text is landed; R-018 cites D-060 as ratified; an audit-close spend-snapshot receipt is attached at docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/receipts/WO-022-audit-close-spend.json with accounting recorded or explicitly accounting_unknown/estimated; canonical session inclusion is checked as manifest-corroborated known-token sessions with resume rows deduplicated and non-manifest sessions only a labeled upper bound.", "action": "[R2 RULED] Implement the ratified spend-guardrail section verbatim: SPEND GUARDRAILS (capstone benchmark bands) \u2014 provisional calibration constants; review after two completed arcs; sunset at capstone submission.\n\n1. ACCOUNTING SOURCE. Sol spend: `codex-usage` local accounting (the standing snapshot convention), corroborated by codex-run-v3 manifest `token_usage` rows where populated. The extraction window must cover the full arc \u2014 sum incremental snapshots for multi-day arcs; a single trailing-24h view is insufficient. Fable spend: estimated from local usage accounting; each snapshot names its method and price-table version. Price table v2026-07 (pinned until amended): GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30 per M in/out, cached input $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1. All figures are estimates, not billing truth, and are recorded as such. Missing data is recorded as `accounting_unknown`, never as zero.\n\n2. DENOMINATOR AND CACHED-TOKEN TREATMENT. Token bands count total tokens (cached + uncached, all directions) exactly as codex-usage reports them \u2014 cached tokens are never excluded (exclusion invites cache-heavy gaming). Dollar figures apply cached pricing honestly. Cross-family aggregate ceilings bind in combined estimated dollars, because raw cross-family token sums are not commensurable (C-028: Sol ~180x the token volume, Fable ~3.4x the cost).\n\n3. BOUNDARIES AND ATTRIBUTION. An arc = one council-log C-row, opened at its first delegated session, closed at its closeout snapshot. A work order = one WO/task id. Failed calls, retries, resumes, refuters, fix rounds, delta re-audits, lead usage, and subagents all count against the initiating WO and arc. Arcs and WOs may not be split, renamed, or reopened to reset counters.\n\n4. BANDS. Each dimension is independent. SOFT crossing = record-and-continue: flag in the spend snapshot plus a one-line justification in the council row. HARD crossing = pause-and-ask Ed before any NEW delegated work in that category; in-flight sessions finish; quiet-machine measurement is never interrupted.\n\n   | Scope | Soft | Hard |\n   |---|---|---|\n   | Sol high session | 6M tokens | 12M |\n   | Sol xhigh session | 8M | 16M |\n   | Sol ultra session | 40M | 60M |\n   | Bench-effort WO | 10M / 3 Sol sessions / ~$40 combined | 20M / 6 / ~$80 |\n   | Session-effort WO | 30M / 8 Sol sessions / ~$100 combined | 60M / 12 / ~$200 |\n   | Arc | 100M / 25 Sol sessions / ~$400 combined / 6 Sol active-hours / 2 elapsed days | 200M / 40 / ~$800 / 12 h / 4 days |\n\n   WO dollar figures are best-effort: when per-WO Fable attribution is accounting_unknown, the token/session pair binds. Ultra: at most 2 INTENDED ultra sessions per arc, each with a pre-run recorded statement of why xhigh is insufficient and what bounded subagent work it will perform; an unintended ultra is recorded as an anomaly and still counts.\n\n   Calibration anchors (recorded so recalibration stays honest): healthy xhigh \u2248 2.3\u20133.5M tokens/session (C-030 post effort-fix; C-028 average); the recorded broken state averaged ~9M. C-028 (330.6M / 59 sessions / ~$1,050 / ~17.5h) crosses every substantive arc HARD dimension \u2014 it is the anti-example. The 2026-07-13 comprehensive audit (~30 Sol sessions + ~70 Fable agents, Ed-authorized) crosses arc SOFT on session count only \u2014 the intended \"exceptional: justify and continue\" outcome.\n\n5. CHECKPOINTS (procedural; owner = the Fable lead). (a) At arc open: predeclare one accepted deliverable increment for the arc \u2014 a corpus/measurement result, analysis/figure/report increment, evaluator requirement, or cited advancement of a D-060 gate \u2014 and classify planned delegated work as deliverable-facing or process-facing (mixed sessions count as process-facing unless separately attributable). (b) Before each next delegated call: check the completed session against its tier band (a lightweight glance, not a full snapshot); no runtime killing is promised \u2014 evaluation happens on completed sessions before any resume, replacement, or new call. (c) At WO close and arc close: take the spend snapshot and evaluate all bands. One missed checkpoint blocks new process-facing delegation until reconciled.\n\n6. DELIVERABLE-PROGRESS TRIPWIRE (binds while ANY D-060 gate is unmet). If process-facing combined estimated cost exceeds 33% of arc cost OR $250 \u2014 whichever occurs first \u2014 HARD pause-and-ask Ed before further process-facing delegation. Independently, an arc that closes with process-facing spend but NO accepted deliverable increment pauses further non-exempt process work even if the 33% threshold was not crossed.\n\n7. EXCEPTIONS AND OVERRIDES. Gate-closing work is deliverable-facing by definition. Correctness-defect and data-preservation work may override the allocation tripwire but is always fully counted. Ed direction is NOT a blanket exemption (the finding's own exemplar \u2014 bridge v1/v1.1 \u2014 was Ed-directed): it is a recorded override carrying an incremental budget and an expiry, and its spend counts.\n\n8. NAMED-FAILURE BAR FOR PROCESS INNOVATION. Any NEW process layer, tool, skill, wrapper version, or contract version requires a decision-log entry citing: (a) a named recorded failure it addresses, (b) why existing controls did not cover it, (c) the smallest new layer that does, (d) its applicability predicate, (e) its marginal budget, (f) a sunset/retirement condition. Absent that entry, it is D-060 breadth and waits for the gates.\n\n9. KEEP-DEFENDER GUARANTEE. No cap consequence auto-deletes a review layer. Layers with recorded unique catches survive any cap; a cap response batches, rescopes, or seeks Ed approval \u2014 never silently drops catch-bearing gates (final-head, integration, lead-live, claim/evidence safeguards).\n\n10. MECHANISM. This policy is PROCEDURAL, not mechanical: no checker script is built now (adding process code during an overengineering correction is self-defeating; the arithmetic is a handful of numbers already recorded at existing snapshot points). Two recorded accounting discrepancies or skipped checkpoints across two arcs constitute the named failure that authorizes an executable checker with tests \u2014 via the \u00a78 bar.\n\n11. RECALIBRATION AND OWNERSHIP. Band values are calibration constants: the lead may amend SOFT values at arc close with evidence via a one-line decision-log amendment; HARD values and this section's structure are Ed-owned.
