docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-night-hardening/AUDIT-LEDGER.md:11064:docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/packets/ed-rulings.json:16:    "concrete_spec": "SPEND GUARDRAILS (capstone benchmark bands) \u2014 provisional calibration constants; review after two completed arcs; sunset at capstone submission.\n\n1. ACCOUNTING SOURCE. Sol spend: `codex-usage` local accounting (the standing snapshot convention), corroborated by codex-run-v3 manifest `token_usage` rows where populated. The extraction window must cover the full arc \u2014 sum incremental snapshots for multi-day arcs; a single trailing-24h view is insufficient. Fable spend: estimated from local usage accounting; each snapshot names its method and price-table version. Price table v2026-07 (pinned until amended): GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30 per M in/out, cached input $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1. All figures are estimates, not billing truth, and are recorded as such. Missing data is recorded as `accounting_unknown`, never as zero.\n\n2. DENOMINATOR AND CACHED-TOKEN TREATMENT. Token bands count total tokens (cached + uncached, all directions) exactly as codex-usage reports them \u2014 cached tokens are never excluded (exclusion invites cache-heavy gaming). Dollar figures apply cached pricing honestly. Cross-family aggregate ceilings bind in combined estimated dollars, because raw cross-family token sums are not commensurable (C-028: Sol ~180x the token volume, Fable ~3.4x the cost).\n\n3. BOUNDARIES AND ATTRIBUTION. An arc = one council-log C-row, opened at its first delegated session, closed at its closeout snapshot. A work order = one WO/task id. Failed calls, retries, resumes, refuters, fix rounds, delta re-audits, lead usage, and subagents all count against the initiating WO and arc. Arcs and WOs may not be split, renamed, or reopened to reset counters.\n\n4. BANDS. Each dimension is independent. SOFT crossing = record-and-continue: flag in the spend snapshot plus a one-line justification in the council row. HARD crossing = pause-and-ask Ed before any NEW delegated work in that category; in-flight sessions finish; quiet-machine measurement is never interrupted.\n\n   | Scope | Soft | Hard |\n   |---|---|---|\n   | Sol high session | 6M tokens | 12M |\n   | Sol xhigh session | 8M | 16M |\n   | Sol ultra session | 40M | 60M |\n   | Bench-effort WO | 10M / 3 Sol sessions / ~$40 combined | 20M / 6 / ~$80 |\n   | Session-effort WO | 30M / 8 Sol sessions / ~$100 combined | 60M / 12 / ~$200 |\n   | Arc | 100M / 25 Sol sessions / ~$400 combined / 6 Sol active-hours / 2 elapsed days | 200M / 40 / ~$800 / 12 h / 4 days |\n\n   WO dollar figures are best-effort: when per-WO Fable attribution is accounting_unknown, the token/session pair binds. Ultra: at most 2 INTENDED ultra sessions per arc, each with a pre-run recorded statement of why xhigh is insufficient and what bounded subagent work it will perform; an unintended ultra is recorded as an anomaly and still counts.\n\n   Calibration anchors (recorded so recalibration stays honest): healthy xhigh \u2248 2.3\u20133.5M tokens/session (C-030 post effort-fix; C-028 average); the recorded broken state averaged ~9M. C-028 (330.6M / 59 sessions / ~$1,050 / ~17.5h) crosses every substantive arc HARD dimension \u2014 it is the anti-example. The 2026-07-13 comprehensive audit (~30 Sol sessions + ~70 Fable agents, Ed-authorized) crosses arc SOFT on session count only \u2014 the intended \"exceptional: justify and continue\" outcome.\n\n5. CHECKPOINTS (procedural; owner = the Fable lead). (a) At arc open: predeclare one accepted deliverable increment for the arc \u2014 a corpus/measurement result, analysis/figure/report increment, evaluator requirement, or cited advancement of a D-060 gate \u2014 and classify planned delegated work as deliverable-facing or process-facing (mixed sessions count as process-facing unless separately attributable). (b) Before each next delegated call: check the completed session against its tier band (a lightweight glance, not a full snapshot); no runtime killing is promised \u2014 evaluation happens on completed sessions before any resume, replacement, or new call. (c) At WO close and arc close: take the spend snapshot and evaluate all bands. One missed checkpoint blocks new process-facing delegation until reconciled.\n\n6. DELIVERABLE-PROGRESS TRIPWIRE (binds while ANY D-060 gate is unmet). If process-facing combined estimated cost exceeds 33% of arc cost OR $250 \u2014 whichever occurs first \u2014 HARD pause-and-ask Ed before further process-facing delegation. Independently, an arc that closes with process-facing spend but NO accepted deliverable increment pauses further non-exempt process work even if the 33% threshold was not crossed.\n\n7. EXCEPTIONS AND OVERRIDES. Gate-closing work is deliverable-facing by definition. Correctness-defect and data-preservation work may override the allocation tripwire but is always fully counted. Ed direction is NOT a blanket exemption (the finding's own exemplar \u2014 bridge v1/v1.1 \u2014 was Ed-directed): it is a recorded override carrying an incremental budget and an expiry, and its spend counts.\n\n8. NAMED-FAILURE BAR FOR PROCESS INNOVATION. Any NEW process layer, tool, skill, wrapper version, or contract version requires a decision-log entry citing: (a) a named recorded failure it addresses, (b) why existing controls did not cover it, (c) the smallest new layer that does, (d) its applicability predicate, (e) its marginal budget, (f) a sunset/retirement condition. Absent that entry, it is D-060 breadth and waits for the gates.\n\n9. KEEP-DEFENDER GUARANTEE. No cap consequence auto-deletes a review layer. Layers with recorded unique catches survive any cap; a cap response batches, rescopes, or seeks Ed approval \u2014 never silently drops catch-bearing gates (final-head, integration, lead-live, claim/evidence safeguards).\n\n10. MECHANISM. This policy is PROCEDURAL, not mechanical: no checker script is built now (adding process code during an overengineering correction is self-defeating; the arithmetic is a handful of numbers already recorded at existing snapshot points). Two recorded accounting discrepancies or skipped checkpoints across two arcs constitute the named failure that authorizes an executable checker with tests \u2014 via the \u00a78 bar.\n\n11. RECALIBRATION AND OWNERSHIP. Band values are calibration constants: the lead may amend SOFT values at arc close with evidence via a one-line decision-log amendment; HARD values and this section's structure are Ed-owned. Scheduled review after two completed arcs. The whole policy sunsets at capstone submission.",

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-night-hardening/AUDIT-LEDGER.md:11087:docs/site/orchestration.html:1:<!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="utf-8"> <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> <title>The Orchestration Process - JouleWise</title> <script>document.documentElement.classList.add("js-enabled");</script> <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 100 100'><text y='.9em' font-size='90'>⚡</text></svg>"> </head> <body> <header class="site"> <nav class="nav"> <a class="brand" href="index.html"><span class="dot"></span>JOULEWISE</a> <div class="links"> <a href="index.html">Project</a> <a href="research.html">Learn</a> <a href="advisor_brief.html">Advisor Brief</a> <a href="project_status.html">Status</a> <a href="status.html">Live Status</a> <a href="roadmap.html">Roadmap</a> <a href="process.html">Process</a> <a href="record.html">Record</a> <a href="library.html" class="active">Sources</a> <a href="results.html">Measurements</a> </div> </nav> </header> <main> <div class="doc-layout"> <aside class="toc-sidebar"><div class="card-label">Table of contents</div><a href="#roles-a-lead-independent-implementers-reviewers-and-a-human-at-the-top">Roles: a lead, independent implementers/reviewers, and a human at the top</a> <a href="#the-loop-end-to-end">The loop, end to end</a> <a href="#the-artifact-system-where-rigor-becomes-auditable">The artifact system (where rigor becomes auditable)</a> <a href="#council-discipline">Council discipline</a> <a href="#spend-guardrails-wo-022-r2-ruled-ed-ratified-2026-07-13">Spend guardrails (WO-022; R2 ruled, Ed-ratified 2026-07-13)</a> <a href="#topology-how-it-evolved-an-example-of-the-loop-improving-itself">Topology: how it evolved (an example of the loop improving itself)</a> <a href="#what-one-session-looks-like-2026-07-07-08-the-merge-session">What one session looks like (2026-07-07/08, the merge session)</a> <a href="#reconstructing-the-loop-on-a-clean-machine">Reconstructing the loop on a clean machine</a> <a href="#where-to-read-the-evidence">Where to read the evidence</a></aside> <div class="doc-wrap doc-source-docs-orchestration-md"> <p class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>docs/orchestration.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/orchestration.md · commit 0de4cea"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>orchestration.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 0de4cea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>The Orchestration Process</h1> <p>How this project is actually built: a human researcher directing a multi-model AI system whose workflow is itself a deliberate, versioned, self-instrumenting piece of engineering. This document is the single in-repo description of that process. (The executable playbooks live outside the repository as reusable &quot;skills&quot; so they transfer to future projects; this page describes what they do and where their evidence lands in this repo.) Binding role and process changes live in <code>docs/decision_log.md</code>; this page avoids copying volatile model versions.</p> <h2 id="roles-a-lead-independent-implementers-reviewers-and-a-human-at-the-top">Roles: a lead, independent implementers/reviewers, and a human at the top</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Ed (researcher)</strong> sets research direction, methodology non-negotiables (raw-evidence bundles, dual-basis capture with gross-energy headlines, named measurement boundaries, no unauditable claims), hardware/access decisions, and — critically — <em>process policy</em>: every rule below traces to a standing instruction issued after an observed failure or opportunity. External-facing claims and merge authority derive from him (he granted the lead conditional self-merge authority on 2026-07-08 once the review gate had proven itself).</li> <li><strong>The designated lead</strong> owns decomposition, triage, design adjudication, every final diff gate, all live/hardware verification, merge decisions, bookkeeping, and process evolution. Other agents save lead capacity without inheriting final authority; all escalation paths terminate at the lead.</li> <li><strong>Independent implementation and review agents</strong> do the heavy reading and writing: implementation against pinned specs, adversarial review lenses, test writing, test <em>auditing</em> (never of its own tests — a fresh instance audits), docs drafting, and review of the lead&#39;s own consequential decisions. Cross-model review is load-bearing by design: the attributed per-layer catch record (below) shows the two roles consistently catching different classes of defect.</li> <li><strong>Specialist agents</strong> handle bounded sweeps (for example, docs consistency) and, when a stream genuinely needs mid-stream judgment, as a stream director — a role that is now the exception rather than the default (see Topology).</li> <li><strong>Image-heavy analysis uses the designated image-capable review route</strong> per C-012, after the site-observatory stream&#39;s image-critique rounds.</li> <li><strong>Invited-peer validation is allowed to overturn lead designs</strong>; C-014 recorded two lead designs overturned by an invited peer before implementation.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-loop-end-to-end">The loop, end to end</h2> <p>Every substantial session runs one conductor procedure:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Intake</strong> — read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> (the intake pointer), the task queue, the latest run report; never re-decide anything the decision log settled.</li> <li><strong>Decompose</strong> — split work into genuinely independent streams (disjoint expected diff footprints), one git worktree + branch each; assign each stream a review tier by <em>cost of being wrong</em> (measurement-semantics and contract-bearing work gets the full pipeline; docs get a light tier). Preflight gates: hardware-shaped streams require a confirmed device inventory; anything pinned without live validation carries a PROVISIONAL label; measurement sessions require a no-agent &quot;quiet machine&quot; lock.</li> <li><strong>Per-stream pipeline</strong> — for each reviewable unit: an invited design-argument round (the implementer must argue trade-offs before coding), implementation, then a layered review stack: 2–3 fresh-instance counterreview lenses over the diff → lead triage with recorded dispositions → fixes → a dedicated test-amplification round (an independent writer adds edge-case tests) → a writer≠reviewer test audit (a fresh instance hunts tautological, vacuous, or wrong-expectation tests) → the lead&#39;s diff gate.</li> <li><strong>Lead live gates</strong> — never delegated: the lead runs the real flow (real corpus, real CLI, real hardware where present). This layer has repeatedly caught blockers no other layer saw, including defects whose own tests were green because the tests encoded the same wrong assumption as the code.</li> <li><strong>Merge gate</strong> — multi-commit series land as branch + PR. Before any merge: a pre-merge oversight pass by 2–3 fresh reviewers with distinct angles (deep regression hunt; claim-to-evidence trace; merge-order simulation across sibling PRs), lead triage, fixes, CI green. <strong>Final-head rule:</strong> any commit that lands after the last review round gets one more fresh review before merge — no commit merges unreviewed, however small (its first application caught a crash path in a &quot;trivial&quot; post-review fix).</li> <li><strong>Integration review</strong> — after parallel streams merge, one dedicated review hunts <em>interaction</em> defects no single-stream review can see. Its catches are definitionally unique (first outing: two).</li> <li><strong>Bookkeeping</strong> — a single session record (run report) with a verbatim process-trace appendix; the intake pointer and queue refreshed; a delegated docs-consistency sweep before the final commit (its latest pass found 15 real drift items; earlier passes found 5–6). Large documentation batches add the pre-commit docs-verify mode; the <code>consistency-sweep</code> skill owns that shape, including the D-043 supersession check.</li> <li><strong>Same-session distillation</strong> — lessons fold into the process playbooks the same session they are learned. Measured effect: one failure mode recurred five times before its fix was distilled, zero times after. The current operation-loop also runs its §0 primary-deliverable check and §8 shipped-check before the session is considered done.</li> <li><strong>Post-landing verification and close-out</strong> — landed work gets the matching verification workflow with severity-tiered refuters. Sessions that change front-facing state refresh <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code>; no agent regenerates or deploys the site. Automation informs and Ed deploys manually, per D-068 and <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> end-of-work step 8.</li> <li><strong>Meta-review (the final step)</strong> — event-driven, not calendar-driven: when a review layer stops earning its keep, when an intervention repeats despite a folded fix, or when the user asks, the loop is reviewed with its own evidence discipline (see Topology for the consensus one such review produced). After large workloads the post-large-workload meta-reassessment (owned by operation-loop §10) always fires, and it runs LAST.</li> </ol> <h3>Stop cards and paused work</h3> <p>When a session stops with live work in progress, the lead creates or updates an <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code> at the top of <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>. While active, that card is the single restart authority and overrides every lower &quot;what next&quot; list, queue rank, mission guide, and run-report default.</p> <p>A stop card must name:</p> <ul> <li>the resume authority and exact artifact pointer,</li> <li>the reason for stopping,</li> <li>worktrees, branches, PRs, and off-repo artifacts that must not be cleaned accidentally,</li> <li>status terms for each paused item,</li> <li>the first resume action, and</li> <li>the clearance criteria.</li> </ul> <p>Use these status terms for paused work:</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Term</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td><code>APPLIED_UNVERIFIED</code></td> <td>A worker reports code or docs are applied, but the lead has not gated the diff. Not merge-safe.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>LEAD_GATED</code></td> <td>The lead has reviewed and run the required local/live checks for the item.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>PR_OPEN_CI_GREEN</code></td> <td>A PR exists and CI is green, but merge authority has not yet fired.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>MERGED</code></td> <td>The accepted work has landed on main.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>UNREAD_UNADJUDICATED</code></td> <td>A report/synthesis exists but has not been consumed into decisions, queue rows, or rejected findings.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>ADJUDICATED</code></td> <td>Findings have explicit accept/reject/defer disposition and downstream artifacts are updated.</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Before an intentional pause, do the minimal stop sync even if full bookkeeping cannot fit: update only <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>&#39;s stop card and the rank-0 queue row. That is enough to prevent accidental bypass.</p> <h2 id="the-artifact-system-where-rigor-becomes-auditable">The artifact system (where rigor becomes auditable)</h2> <p>Each fact has exactly one home; everything else points at it:</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Artifact</th> <th>Role</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></td> <td>Binding design decisions, each with alternatives considered, consequences, and revisit conditions. The log is the count authority; nothing re-decides these silently.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/council_log.md</code></td> <td>The deliberation record: review-council positions, reasoning exchanged, who prevailed, overridden dissents — so a future reader can reconstruct <em>why</em>, not just <em>what</em>. The log is the range/count authority.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/contracts/</code></td> <td>Claim/evidence contracts: <code>claims_ladder.md</code> (D-037) plus <code>analysis_plans.md</code> (D-038) form the claim gate; strict validation is the evidence ticket.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/stream_logs/</code></td> <td>Per-stream decision ledgers, committed WITH the code they justify: every non-trivial in-stream decision (<code>A-1..A-30</code>, <code>B-1..B-46</code>, …) with mandatory evidence pointers; wrong pins are SUPERSEDED in place, never erased.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/run_reports/</code></td> <td>One record per working session: outcomes, verification evidence, a per-layer catch/yield table, the delegation-calibration ledger, restart instructions.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/process/state_kernel.json</code></td> <td>Source of truth for work selection: active gates, dependencies, and machine-state lanes ([QUIET-MAC] / [AGENT] / [ED-EXTERNAL]).</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code></td> <td>Generated detailed queue projection plus dated history; do not hand-copy its live rows into reader docs.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>RUN_STATE.md</code></td> <td>Intake pointer with the generated restart projection. History lives in run reports.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/risk_register.md</code></td> <td>Live risks with triggers and mitigation states.</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Instrumentation ledgers close the loop on the process itself:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Per-layer yield:</strong> every review layer&#39;s unique catches are attributed and tallied per session under D-061 (C-027; replaces the earlier two-zero-sessions auto-drop, which the integration-review zero/zero/five sequence falsified): applicability is decided by PRE-DECLARED mechanical predicates; outcomes are classified accepted-unique-defect / duplicate / clean-verification / false-positive-suppression (suppression is not a catch); severity weights are fixed before the session; three applicable exposures TRIGGER an expected-loss review decision, never automatic deletion; safety/final-head/integration layers are never auto-dropped on zero-defect streaks. (One layer, the default specialist review lens, was dropped under the old rule before D-061.)</li> <li><strong>Delegation calibration:</strong> every delegated unit gets a row — task altitude (pinned-spec / design-freedom / judgment-call), outcome (assigned by the lead after the gate, never self-labeled), catches, and lead rework minutes, with prompt-defects separated from model-defects. Delegation boundaries move on this evidence, not vibes. Current signal: pinned-spec delegation runs essentially defect-free; the serious defects cluster in volunteered additions and design-freedom wire contracts — which is exactly where the full lens</li> <li><strong>Invocation manifest:</strong> substantial delegated/tool/skill runs get a lightweight manifest row per invocation. Minimum fields: <code>run_id</code>, <code>parent_report</code>, <code>role_or_lens</code>, <code>model</code>, <code>wrapper</code>, <code>session_id</code>, <code>prompt_sha256</code>, <code>prompt_path</code>, <code>output_path</code>, <code>status</code>, <code>consumed_by</code>, <code>disposition</code>, and <code>commit_or_pr</code>. Raw logs can stay out of git; every ephemeral artifact still needs a committed pointer row with <code>path</code>, <code>sha256</code> or stable id, <code>promoted_to</code>, and <code>not_promoted_reason</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="council-discipline">Council discipline</h2> <p>Councils are expensive instruments. Use a full council for methodology, measurement validity, schema/contract changes, claim boundaries, hardware protocols, or explicit user requests. For ordinary implementation, use a small number of targeted lenses plus lead adjudication.</p> <p>Every high-impact council must leave a durable scorecard:</p> <ul> <li>unique catches by severity,</li> <li>accepted/rejected/deferred/false-positive counts,</li> <li>lead triage and rework time when practical,</li> <li>shipped artifacts,</li> <li>queue rows created or re-ranked,</li> <li>decision-log IDs promoted, and</li> <li>a disposition table: finding → ruling → owner → artifact/queue/decision target → closure check.</li> </ul> <p>Deferred decision-log promotion is itself a tracked obligation, not ambient prose in a report.</p> <h2 id="spend-guardrails-wo-022-r2-ruled-ed-ratified-2026-07-13">Spend guardrails (WO-022; R2 ruled, Ed-ratified 2026-07-13)</h2> <p>The following policy text is the R2-ratified section, landed verbatim per audit work order WO-022 (<code>docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/</code>).</p> <p>SPEND GUARDRAILS (capstone benchmark bands) — provisional calibration constants; review after two completed arcs; sunset at capstone submission.</p> <ol> <li><p>ACCOUNTING SOURCE. Sol spend: <code>codex-usage</code> local accounting (the standing snapshot convention), corroborated by codex-run-v3 manifest <code>token_usage</code> rows where populated. The extraction window must cover the full arc — sum incremental snapshots for multi-day arcs; a single trailing-24h view is insufficient. Fable spend: estimated from local usage accounting; each snapshot names its method and price-table version. Price table v2026-07 (pinned until amended): GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30 per M in/out, cached input $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1. All figures are estimates, not billing truth, and are recorded as such. Missing data is recorded as <code>accounting_unknown</code>, never as zero.</p> </li> <li><p>DENOMINATOR AND CACHED-TOKEN TREATMENT. Token bands count total tokens (cached + uncached, all directions) exactly as codex-usage reports them — cached tokens are never excluded (exclusion invites cache-heavy gaming). Dollar figures apply cached pricing honestly. Cross-family aggregate ceilings bind in combined estimated dollars, because raw cross-family token sums are not commensurable (C-028: Sol ~180x the token volume, Fable ~3.4x the cost).</p> </li> <li><p>BOUNDARIES AND ATTRIBUTION. An arc = one council-log C-row, opened at its first delegated session, closed at its closeout snapshot. A work order = one WO/task id. Failed calls, retries, resumes, refuters, fix rounds, delta re-audits, lead usage, and subagents all count against the initiating WO and arc. Arcs and WOs may not be split, renamed, or reopened to reset counters.</p> </li> <li><p>BANDS. Each dimension is independent. SOFT crossing = record-and-continue: flag in the spend snapshot plus a one-line justification in the council row. HARD crossing = pause-and-ask Ed before any NEW delegated work in that category; in-flight sessions finish; quiet-machine measurement is never interrupted.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Scope</th> <th>Soft</th> <th>Hard</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>Sol high session</td> <td>6M tokens</td> <td>12M</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Sol xhigh session</td> <td>8M</td> <td>16M</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Sol ultra session</td> <td>40M</td> <td>60M</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Bench-effort WO</td> <td>10M / 3 Sol sessions / ~$40 combined</td> <td>20M / 6 / ~$80</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Session-effort WO</td> <td>30M / 8 Sol sessions / ~$100 combined</td> <td>60M / 12 / ~$200</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Arc</td> <td>100M / 25 Sol sessions / ~$400 combined / 6 Sol active-hours / 2 elapsed days</td> <td>200M / 40 / ~$800 / 12 h / 4 days</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>WO dollar figures are best-effort: when per-WO Fable attribution is accounting_unknown, the token/session pair binds. Ultra: at most 2 INTENDED ultra sessions per arc, each with a pre-run recorded statement of why xhigh is insufficient and what bounded subagent work it will perform; an unintended ultra is recorded as an anomaly and still counts.</p> <p>Calibration anchors (recorded so recalibration stays honest): healthy xhigh ≈ 2.3–3.5M tokens/session (C-030 post effort-fix; C-028 average); the recorded broken state averaged ~9M. C-028 (330.6M / 59 sessions / ~$1,050 / ~17.5h) crosses every substantive arc HARD dimension — it is the anti-example. The 2026-07-13 comprehensive audit (~30 Sol sessions + ~70 Fable agents, Ed-authorized) crosses arc SOFT on session count only — the intended &quot;exceptional: justify and continue&quot; outcome.</p> </li> <li><p>CHECKPOINTS (procedural; owner = the Fable lead). (a) At arc open: predeclare one accepted deliverable increment for the arc — a corpus/measurement result, analysis/figure/report increment, evaluator requirement, or cited advancement of a D-060 gate — and classify planned delegated work as deliverable-facing or process-facing (mixed sessions count as process-facing unless separately attributable). (b) Before each next delegated call: check the completed session against its tier band (a lightweight glance, not a full snapshot); no runtime killing is promised — evaluation happens on completed sessions before any resume, replacement, or new call. (c) At WO close and arc close: take the spend snapshot and evaluate all bands. One missed checkpoint blocks new process-facing delegation until reconciled.</p> </li> <li><p>DELIVERABLE-PROGRESS TRIPWIRE (binds while ANY D-060 gate is unmet). If process-facing combined estimated cost exceeds 33% of arc cost OR $250 — whichever occurs first — HARD pause-and-ask Ed before further process-facing delegation. Independently, an arc that closes with process-facing spend but NO accepted deliverable increment pauses further non-exempt process work even if the 33% threshold was not crossed.</p> </li> <li><p>EXCEPTIONS AND OVERRIDES. Gate-closing work is deliverable-facing by definition. Correctness-defect and data-preservation work may override the allocation tripwire but is always fully counted. Ed direction is NOT a blanket exemption (the finding&#39;s own exemplar — bridge v1/v1.1 — was Ed-directed): it is a recorded override carrying an incremental budget and an expiry, and its spend counts.</p> </li> <li><p>NAMED-FAILURE BAR FOR PROCESS INNOVATION. Any NEW process layer, tool, skill, wrapper version, or contract version requires a decision-log entry citing: (a) a named recorded failure it addresses, (b) why existing controls did not cover it, (c) the smallest new layer that does, (d) its applicability predicate, (e) its marginal budget, (f) a sunset/retirement condition. Absent that entry, it is D-060 breadth and waits for the gates.</p> </li> <li><p>KEEP-DEFENDER GUARANTEE. No cap consequence auto-deletes a review layer. Layers with recorded unique catches survive any cap; a cap response batches, rescopes, or seeks Ed approval — never silently drops catch-bearing gates (final-head, integration, lead-live, claim/evidence safeguards).</p> </li> <li><p>MECHANISM. This policy is PROCEDURAL, not mechanical: no checker script is built now (adding process code during an overengineering correction is self-defeating; the arithmetic is a handful of numbers already recorded at existing snapshot points). Two recorded accounting discrepancies or skipped checkpoints across two arcs constitute the named failure that authorizes an executable checker with tests — via the §8 bar.</p> </li> <li><p>RECALIBRATION AND OWNERSHIP. Band values are calibration constants: the lead may amend SOFT values at arc close with evidence via a one-line decision-log amendment; HARD values and this section&#39;s structure are Ed-owned. Scheduled review after two completed arcs. The whole policy sunsets at capstone submission.</p> </li> </ol> <p>Court amendments (T09, folded at the register): canonical session inclusion uses manifest-corroborated sessions with known token records; resume rows are deduplicated; non-manifest sessions are reported only as a labeled upper bound. The 2026-07-13 audit anchor in section 4 is estimated/accounting_unknown until an audit-close spend snapshot receipts it (docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/receipts/ WO-022-audit-close-spend.json); only a receipted anchor may be used for recalibration.</p> <h2 id="topology-how-it-evolved-an-example-of-the-loop-improving-itself">Topology: how it evolved (an example of the loop improving itself)</h2> <ul> <li><strong>v1 (2026-07-07 AM):</strong> per-stream Fable orchestrator subagents, each driving its own Codex thread. Worked, but expensive at the apex tier.</li> <li><strong>v2 (2026-07-07 PM):</strong> Opus orchestrators directing Codex, Fable apex-only. Ran four streams — and surfaced a structural flaw: subagent orchestrators are not woken by their childrens&#39; completion (the &quot;wake gap&quot;), forcing the lead to babysit with heartbeats. The session&#39;s own trace captured two fleet-wide stalls.</li> <li><strong>Meta-review (C-009):</strong> a signed cross-model consensus — two blind Codex analyses vs. the lead&#39;s blind position, one conferral round — produced a hybrid: the lead drives pipeline-shaped streams directly (inheriting the harness&#39;s only reliable wake guarantee); subagent directors are reserved for judgment-heavy streams.</li> <li><strong>Validation (C-010, 2026-07-08):</strong> the first full session under the new topology ran ~26 Codex sessions across four streams — resume through merge — with zero coordination stalls, zero manual wake interventions, and no subagent stream directors at all. The consensus is now the stamped default.</li> </ul> <p>The same mechanism has overturned the lead&#39;s own designs: a Codex review of the lead&#39;s process schemas rejected two of them and supplied better ones (now the v2 ledger and calibration formats), and review lenses have refuted two of the lead&#39;s sanctioned wire-protocol pins before they could reach hardware. Seniority is not infallibility; the adjudication of every such challenge remains the lead&#39;s.</p> <h2 id="what-one-session-looks-like-2026-07-07-08-the-merge-session">What one session looks like (2026-07-07/08, the merge session)</h2> <p>Four checkpointed streams resumed, completed, and landed as four PRs: the integrity/provenance overhaul (all 31 audit-pinned defects fixed; strict validation now re-derives the power trace from raw evidence), the docs package, the KV-cache replay feasibility verdict, and the complete fixture-first NVIDIA stack. The layered review recorded, among ~30 attributed catches: two blockers found only by fresh-instance lenses (a provenance hash that did not prove the actual generation input; a strict-gate bypass via mutable metadata), two pinned wire contracts overturned before hardware contact, one fabricated-evidence defect caught only at the lead&#39;s diff gate, two integration defects caught only by the post-merge integration review, and a crash path caught only by the final-head rule on the last commit of the night. Suite: 415 → 546 tests, zero expected failures. Roughly two dozen delegated Codex sessions; the lead never wrote implementation code and never skipped a gate.</p> <h2 id="reconstructing-the-loop-on-a-clean-machine">Reconstructing the loop on a clean machine</h2> <p>Pointer map only; mechanics stay in their owning files.</p> <ul> <li>Committed invocation wrapper: <code>scripts/codex-run</code>. Usage: <code>codex-run &lt;out.md&gt; [--timeout SEC] [-C DIR] [-s SANDBOX] [--resume] &#39;&lt;prompt&gt;&#39;</code>. It writes <code>&lt;out&gt;.status</code>.</li> <li>Project bridge: <code>scripts/codex-bridge</code>; writes prompt snapshots, response snapshots, logs, status files, and <code>.codex-bridge/invocation_manifest.jsonl</code> rows with prompt/output/log hashes.</li> <li>Workspace-write bridge ceremony: <code>scripts/bridge session-open</code> and <code>session-close</code>; the reduced discussion header, tolerant return envelope, receipt anchoring, and recovery primitives are defined only in <code>docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md</code> (<code>bridge-protocol/v1.1</code>).</li> <li>Skill-only mechanics on the operator&#39;s machine live under <code>~/.claude/skills</code>: <code>operation-loop</code> is the conductor, <code>codex-delegation</code> is the invocation/consumption contract, <code>adversarial-review</code> defines refutation tiers, <code>multi-stream-worktrees</code> defines parallel stream mechanics, <code>consistency-sweep</code> owns drift control, and <code>council</code> owns triggers/roles.</li> <li>Repo-derivable on a clean clone: this file gives the loop shape; council log C-009/C-010 give topology and gates; the claims and analysis-plans contracts give claim gating; <code>docs/stream_logs/</code> and <code>docs/run_reports/</code> provide live templates for ledgers and trace appendices; <code>scripts/codex-run</code> and <code>scripts/codex-bridge</code> provide execution entry points.</li> <li>Skill-only: exact conductor sequencing, delegated-agent prompt/consumption contract, severity-tiered refuter recipes, multi-worktree stream operations, and consistency-sweep checklists.</li> </ul> <h2 id="where-to-read-the-evidence">Where to read the evidence</h2> <ul> <li>Yield tables and calibration aggregates: the latest run reports (<code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-07-resume-merge-session.md</code> and <code>...checkpoint-multistream-session.md</code>).</li> <li>Deliberations and consensus texts: <code>docs/council_log.md</code> (C-007 design council; C-009 topology consensus; C-010 validation).</li> <li>The binding rules themselves: <code>docs/decision_log.md</code>.</li> <li>Per-decision, in-stream reasoning: <code>docs/stream_logs/</code>.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/orchestration.md · commit 0de4cea · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

class="source-file">docs/<wbr>council_log.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. Two v3 sessions (doc008-r3, pr59-review) still RUNNING at the manifest snapshot.</p> <p>Spend snapshot addendum (2026-07-11 ~20:00Z, <code>codex-usage</code> 24h window, arc-close truth for the table above; estimates, not billing): 59 Sol sessions / 330.6M tokens / ~17.5h session time — xhigh 55 ≈ 190.4M, ultra 2 ≈ 100.3M, high 2 ≈ 40.0M (both FAILED). Composition (measured from raw session records): ~97.4% of Sol input is cached, output ≈ 0.37% of volume. API-list-price equivalent (GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30, cached $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1): Sol ≈ $240, Fable ≈ $810 — combined ≈ $1,050 for the recorded arc; upper bound ≈ $2,300 counting all local Codex sessions (includes non-manifest sessions; resume rows may double-count). Note the inversion: Sol is ~180x the token volume but Fable is ~3.4x the cost — cache reads dominate the lead&#39;s footprint. Snapshot convention now standing in the council skill §Recording + instrumentation.</p> <p>Process artifacts adopted this arc (ratified as/alongside D-064):</p> <ul> <li><strong>claude-codex-report/v1</strong> — canonical machine-parsed session report envelope; run_finished rows record parse validity, finding counts, verification counts, scope flags.</li> <li><strong>codex-run-v3</strong> — append-only event-stream manifest (run_started/run_finished/run_consumed), retry-with-resume, lead-authored recovery rows on wrapper failure.</li> <li><strong>WRITE_SCOPE backstop</strong> — post-run diff vs declared scope; exit 77 + evidence bundle on violation; NEEDS_SCOPE prospective-only expansion (AGENTS.md precedence section, <code>9ca89cc</code>).</li> <li><strong>NEEDS_RULING</strong> — any blocking non-delegable decision early-returns a structured question instead of a guess (<code>31b3f5e</code>); usage guard + usage-pressure mode active.</li> <li><strong>Design-consult-by-default</strong> — Ed-prompted global-rule amendment; exercised for P2-044 (HAC/ESS design consult, <code>827df12</code>) before implementation.</li> </ul> <p>Dissents overridden: none unresolved. The P2-041 RED tranche (ultra round deleting P2-038/P2-040 wholesale) was not landed or argued — it was triaged per-file and rebuilt from main under three Ed-approved C rulings (<code>96e10bd</code>, <code>750f7d0</code>).</p> <p>Calibration note (model-version scoping, per C-027): the refuter contradictory-verdict pattern produced correct narrowings twice; the two scope violations and one thin-output ultra warning are the arc&#39;s recorded 5.6-sol failure modes. Sealed A/B remains the gate before any delegation-boundary change.</p> <h2 id="c-031-d-078-p0-instrument-repair-close-out-session-round-8-landing-round-9-final-confirmation-sign-off-2026-07-22">C-031: D-078 P0 instrument-repair close-out session — round-8 landing, round-9 final confirmation, sign-off (2026-07-22)</h2> <p>Shape: lead resumed the paused arc cold from scratchpad pointers; collected the checkpointed Sol round-8 fix wave; §C-028 delta re-audit (3 fresh read-only Sol lenses over a shared packet → 8 xhigh refuter verdicts, blockers 2 refuters with distinct lenses); Sol xhigh round-8b fix wave under enforced WRITE_SCOPE (one NEEDS_SCOPE early-return, lead-ruled, fixture fix applied at the bench); bounded 8b delta re-audit; lead full-suite gates (2081 → 2088 passed, 0 failures); commit <code>040ca3a</code>; round-9 FINAL confirmation (Sol xhigh review genre); CR9-1 adjudicated as registered limitation L1 per the loop-termination doctrine; close-out <code>debc6d2</code>; PR #79 opened for Ed-named merge.</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li>Sol review lenses: A1 (v3 claim-eligibility contract divergence), B1 (ClockStamp physical-sanity gap → understated B_fiducial ~3 µs), C1/C2 (boundary float, OverflowError escape), C3/C4 (test-wiring gaps).</li> <li>Sol xhigh refuters: killed A2/B2 outright (both plausible, both wrong — A2&#39;s &quot;legacy records break&quot; was self-invalid synthetic-only; B2&#39;s stale-vs-invalid relabel would have broken a ratified distinction); narrowed C1 to a registered nit; split on A1 (contract-confirmed, reachability-refuted) — lead synthesis: pre-existing defense-in-depth hardening, not a round-8 regression.</li> <li>Round-9 confirmation: CR9-1 (floor artifacts self-attesting) — the only finding of the round, repro-backed, lead-reproduced at the bench.</li> <li>Lead unique: false-attribution triage of the 8b audit&#39;s two &quot;blockers&quot; (both were the lead&#39;s own authorized bench edits); the L1 adjudication.</li> </ul> <p>Failure modes recorded: (1) upstream cyber-content filter killed 3/8 refuters mid-run on adversarial phrasing (&quot;malformed/tamper/escape&quot;) — rephrasing as data-quality QA of our own instrument recovered all three (route: keep refuter briefs mechanism-neutral); (2) lead bench-edited the worktree while an enforced-scope Sol session ran in it → false SCOPE_VIOLATION attribution + resume-registry loss (rule: no lead edits in a tree with a live enforced-scope session); (3) the known xhigh review-genre null-final-message mode recurred on round 9; the documented bridge-resume recovery worked first try.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: the 8b delta auditor&#39;s should-fix (OverflowError normalization also reaching v1 replay error behavior) was overridden by lead ruling — frozen-replay doctrine protects computed semantics of parsable artifacts, not crash reproduction on impossible inputs; the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Yield: the peer&#39;s structural correction (anomaly screen must not erase drift from the claim budget) was adopted — the second recorded case of invited peer design judgment beating the lead&#39;s ruling. The debate also surfaced one gap neither model had specced (drift-bound freshness horizon — prompted by Ed&#39;s own risk question) and one open science question (a7-vs-a5 prefill floor scatter, 3x). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. ## Verdict

The fast-mode fan-out was a protocol violation, not an allowed “non-governed mode.”

The bridge contract covers Claude–Codex collaboration generally and says every delegated prompt must begin with `BRIDGE_TASK_V1` ([§1, lines 28–53](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:28)); autonomous calls require the full header even when read-only ([§1, lines 99–100](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:99)). The routing table sends autonomous work to audited CLI; it does not define an ungoverned or fast-tier exception ([§4, lines 225–238](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:225)).

The only audited-CLI exception is from the two-line trailer when a valid `claude-codex-report/v1` body exists; it does not waive the prompt header ([§2, lines 138–145](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:138)). Section 9’s statement that enforcement exists only where adapters validate it is a limitation, not an opt-out ([§9, lines 781–785](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:781)).

### Confirmed bypasses

1. **Bare fast-mode prompts and noncompliant returns.**  
   The representative proposal transcript starts directly with “PAPER-PROPOSAL DEVELOPMENT SESSION,” not a bridge header ([proposal lines 1–17](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-attention-variant-energy.md:1)), and ends in ordinary prose rather than either accepted return form ([lines 5206–5212](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-attention-variant-energy.md:5206)). The same is true of the two xhigh syntheses ([example lines 12–24](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:12)). Contract §2 explicitly says missing or malformed required envelopes cannot be interpreted as success ([lines 174–183](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:174)).

2. **Implementation/audit prompts used an older ad hoc contract.**  
   U1 begins with only `WRITE_SCOPE: [...]`, omitting `TASK_SHAPE`, `GENRE`, `BASE_HEAD`, baseline manifest/digest, acceptance, verification, and output protocol ([U1 lines 1–12](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-u-units/U1-CONTRACT.md:1)). The audit likewise begins bare ([U1 audit lines 14–21](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-u-units/U1-AUDIT-CONTRACT.md:14)). This fails §1 and the mandatory pre-write baseline rule in §7 ([lines 543–573](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:543)), even if `codex-run-v3` separately performed its older post-hoc scope check.

3. **“Fast mode” was treated as governance selection.**  
   The ratification says standard-tier `codex-run-v3` is used when scope enforcement matters and fast mode for all read-only/ideation work ([lines 31–39](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-plan-freeze/RATIFICATION.md:31)). That is the conceptual error: service tier affects latency/credits, not whether headers, output validation, provenance, or status semantics apply. The per-call directive itself is recorded only in live state ([RUN_STATE lines 427–436](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/RUN_STATE.md:427)).

4. **The completed C-049 working session still lacks its required run report.**  
   Orchestration requires one run report per working session and describes it as the session record ([lines 84–90](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:84), [artifact table lines 146–155](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:146)); M0 repeats that requirement ([lines 74–78](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/agent_playbook.md:74)). C-049 instead identifies scattered traces and `RUN_STATE` blocks as its full record ([C-049 lines 2798–2808](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:2798)); no August 5/6 run report exists.

5. **Portfolio consumption is not auditable at the prescribed invocation level.**  
   Orchestration requires model, wrapper, session ID, prompt hash/path, output path, status, consumer, disposition, and commit/PR for each substantial invocation ([lines 180–187](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:180)). The adjudication records “24 Sol + 24 Opus + two syntheses” ([lines 3–8](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/ADJUDICATION.md:3)), but the tracked corpus has no invocation-to-artifact/consumer/disposition manifest, especially for the Opus reviews. It also lacks the complete high-impact-council scorecard required by orchestration ([lines 191–205](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:191)). Because today’s session remains live, this is still remediable, but it is current compliance debt.

I did not classify the unfinished U1/U3 gauntlets or the absent end-of-session sweep as violations: `RUN_STATE` explicitly marks the session and those units in flight.

## Routine practice missing from prescriptive docs

- **Opus counter-reviewer/lieutenant layer.** The council’s standing-role text still says the Opus tier was dropped ([lines 23–33](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:23)), while later practice made Opus the primary lieutenant ([C-038 lines 1891–1904](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:1891)) and today used 24 Opus referees. No named process doc defines its applicability, independence, authority ceiling, or yield/sunset rule.

- **Proposal factory.** The `24 proposal → 24 paired referee → two opposing-prior syntheses → magistrate adjudication` topology is now relied upon for paper strategy, but no process document specifies its packet, provenance, scoring, duplication handling, or stopping rule.

- **Per-call fast-tier opt-in.** Live state records `CODEX_SERVICE_TIER=fast`, never standing-default ([RUN_STATE lines 431–436](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/RUN_STATE.md:431)); neither `CLAUDE.md` nor the bridge contract records that doctrine.

- **Tracked-poll/watcher lifecycle.** Five wake failures established the mandatory status-file/PID/deadline pattern ([run report lines 119–125](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/run_reports/2026-07-28-floor-mint-implementation.md:119)), and stale `RUNNING` has already survived a dead job ([council lines 2197–2203](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:2197)). The contract defines thread states ([§5, lines 332–350](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:332)) but never maps them to wrapper `.status` files, PID liveness, stale-state recovery, or consumption.

## Verdict

The fast-mode fan-out was a protocol violation, not an allowed “non-governed mode.”

The bridge contract covers Claude–Codex collaboration generally and says every delegated prompt must begin with `BRIDGE_TASK_V1` ([§1, lines 28–53](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:28)); autonomous calls require the full header even when read-only ([§1, lines 99–100](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:99)). The routing table sends autonomous work to audited CLI; it does not define an ungoverned or fast-tier exception ([§4, lines 225–238](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:225)).

The only audited-CLI exception is from the two-line trailer when a valid `claude-codex-report/v1` body exists; it does not waive the prompt header ([§2, lines 138–145](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:138)). Section 9’s statement that enforcement exists only where adapters validate it is a limitation, not an opt-out ([§9, lines 781–785](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:781)).

### Confirmed bypasses

1. **Bare fast-mode prompts and noncompliant returns.**  
   The representative proposal transcript starts directly with “PAPER-PROPOSAL DEVELOPMENT SESSION,” not a bridge header ([proposal lines 1–17](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-attention-variant-energy.md:1)), and ends in ordinary prose rather than either accepted return form ([lines 5206–5212](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-attention-variant-energy.md:5206)). The same is true of the two xhigh syntheses ([example lines 12–24](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:12)). Contract §2 explicitly says missing or malformed required envelopes cannot be interpreted as success ([lines 174–183](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:174)).

2. **Implementation/audit prompts used an older ad hoc contract.**  
   U1 begins with only `WRITE_SCOPE: [...]`, omitting `TASK_SHAPE`, `GENRE`, `BASE_HEAD`, baseline manifest/digest, acceptance, verification, and output protocol ([U1 lines 1–12](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-u-units/U1-CONTRACT.md:1)). The audit likewise begins bare ([U1 audit lines 14–21](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-u-units/U1-AUDIT-CONTRACT.md:14)). This fails §1 and the mandatory pre-write baseline rule in §7 ([lines 543–573](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:543)), even if `codex-run-v3` separately performed its older post-hoc scope check.

3. **“Fast mode” was treated as governance selection.**  
   The ratification says standard-tier `codex-run-v3` is used when scope enforcement matters and fast mode for all read-only/ideation work ([lines 31–39](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-plan-freeze/RATIFICATION.md:31)). That is the conceptual error: service tier affects latency/credits, not whether headers, output validation, provenance, or status semantics apply. The per-call directive itself is recorded only in live state ([RUN_STATE lines 427–436](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/RUN_STATE.md:427)).

4. **The completed C-049 working session still lacks its required run report.**  
   Orchestration requires one run report per working session and describes it as the session record ([lines 84–90](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:84), [artifact table lines 146–155](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:146)); M0 repeats that requirement ([lines 74–78](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/agent_playbook.md:74)). C-049 instead identifies scattered traces and `RUN_STATE` blocks as its full record ([C-049 lines 2798–2808](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:2798)); no August 5/6 run report exists.

5. **Portfolio consumption is not auditable at the prescribed invocation level.**  
   Orchestration requires model, wrapper, session ID, prompt hash/path, output path, status, consumer, disposition, and commit/PR for each substantial invocation ([lines 180–187](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:180)). The adjudication records “24 Sol + 24 Opus + two syntheses” ([lines 3–8](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/ADJUDICATION.md:3)), but the tracked corpus has no invocation-to-artifact/consumer/disposition manifest, especially for the Opus reviews. It also lacks the complete high-impact-council scorecard required by orchestration ([lines 191–205](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:191)). Because today’s session remains live, this is still remediable, but it is current compliance debt.

I did not classify the unfinished U1/U3 gauntlets or the absent end-of-session sweep as violations: `RUN_STATE` explicitly marks the session and those units in flight.
